informal.NFChoice.Foundation.NFStandard.NF_proves: Standard New Foundations formally derives the negation of WPP. WPP says that, for all sets x and y, if a function maps y onto x and an injective function maps y into x, then an injective function maps x into y.
informal.NFChoice.Foundation.NFStandard.nf_hailpe: Extensionality together with every integer-stratified comprehension instance and Metamath's Hailperin-derived finite first-order presentation, including its added singleton axiom, derive exactly the same sentences.

records.title: The sharp finite-field Nikodym exponent
records.abstract: Proves a lower bound for Nikodym sets over arbitrary finite fields and a matching exponent upper construction over sufficiently large prime fields, using interpolation, algebraic degree bounds, and multiquadratic constructions.

informal.Nikodym.card_ge_pow_sub: Every Nikodym set in dimension d ≥ 2 over a finite field of size q has size at least q^d − (8d²+1)q^(d−2^(1−d)).
informal.Nikodym.exists_isNikodym_card_le: For every positive ε and dimension d ≥ 2, sufficiently large prime fields admit a Nikodym set of size at most q^d − q^(d−2^(1−d)−ε).

records.title: Nivat's conjecture
records.abstract: Formalizes the proof of Nivat's conjecture found by GPT-6 Pro. A configuration on the integer lattice over a finite alphabet whose number of distinct patterns on some m-by-n rectangle is at most m times n has a nonzero period. Develops rational alphabet labelings, the Laurent-polynomial shift action and its annihilator ideals, the exact line ideal of a half-plane-supported difference of orbit-closure points, complexity descent to a smaller rectangle, and Szabados's two-factor theorem for finite-range configurations.

informal.Nivat.nivat: For every finite alphabet A and configuration c from the integer lattice to A, if for some positive m and n the number of distinct patterns of c on the m-by-n rectangle, counted over all integer translations, is at most m times n, then there is a nonzero lattice vector h with c(z + h) = c(z) for every z.
informal.NivatSubmission.nivat: The same statement written with Mathlib vocabulary only, as registered with Palomar. The pattern set is the range of the restriction of translates of c to the product of the integer intervals [0, m) and [0, n), its natural cardinality is at most m times n, and the conclusion is a lattice vector h different from (0, 0) with c(z + h) = c(z) for all z.
informal.Nivat.nivat_rational: A finite-range rational-valued configuration whose pattern count on some m-by-n rectangle with m, n positive is at most m times n is periodic. This is proved by strong induction on the area of the rectangle.
informal.Nivat.two_factors: If a finite-range rational configuration has pattern count at most m times n on an m-by-n rectangle with m, n positive and is annihilated by the product of two difference operators in nonzero directions h and t, then it is periodic.
informal.Nivat.Descent.exists_smaller_low_complex: If two pointwise limits x and y of translates of a finite-range rational configuration c have nonzero difference whose Laurent annihilator ideal is generated by a nonzero polynomial, and c has pattern count at most m times n on an m-by-n rectangle, then applying that polynomial to c yields a configuration with pattern count at most its area on some rectangle of strictly smaller positive area.
informal.Nivat.Algebra.exact_line_in_basis: A nonzero rational configuration that vanishes on the open lower half-plane of a lattice basis and is periodic with positive period q along the first basis direction has Laurent annihilator ideal generated by a single line-supported polynomial, obtained from a monic divisor of X^q - 1 of positive degree.

records.title: Existence of a finitely presented non-sofic group
records.abstract: Constructs a finitely presented group that is not sofic, resolving the question whether every group admits arbitrarily accurate finite permutation approximations. The development combines an explicit elementary group with property T, a finite-table construction of a finitely presented group, finite-model expansion, and a local obstruction to sofic approximation.

informal.SoficGroups.exists_finitelyPresented_non: There exists a group admitting a finite presentation but no sofic approximation.

records.title: Equal-area and equal-perimeter convex partitions
records.abstract: Formalizes the Akopyan–Avvakumov–Karasev theorem that every planar convex body can be partitioned into any prescribed positive number of convex pieces with equal area and equal perimeter. Area is Lebesgue measure and perimeter is Hausdorff measure of the boundary.

informal.HumanVerification.equalAreaEqualPerimete: Every compact convex planar set with nonempty interior admits a convex partition into any positive number of pieces whose areas and perimeters are all equal.

records.title: Exact odd-prime distributions of central-binomial valuations
records.abstract: Formalizes the exact distribution of the p-adic valuation of the central binomial coefficient binom(2n,n) over every complete block 0 <= n < p^k for every odd prime p. The development proves Kummer correctness for padded digit words, constructs the two-state doubling carry enumerator, identifies it with the arithmetic valuation polynomial, derives its second-order recurrence, proves the rational bivariate generating function, and obtains closed formulas for valuations zero and one.

informal.OddPrimeValuationDistribution.oddPrimeVa: For every odd prime p = 2h+1, proves the denominator-cleared identity for the bivariate series whose coefficient of T^k X^r counts n < p^k with nu_p(binomial(2n,n)) = r; equivalently the series is (1-XT)/(1-(h+1)(1+X)T+pXT^2).
Proves that the exact valuation polynomials satisfy F_{k+2}(X)+pX F_k(X)=(h+1)(1+X)F_{k+1}(X), with F_0=1 and F_1=(h+1)+hX.
informal.OddPrimeValuationDistribution.padicValNa: Proves Kummer correctness for every valid padded base-p word: the p-adic valuation of its central binomial coefficient equals the number of carries produced by doubling the word.
informal.OddPrimeValuationDistribution.card_oddPr: Gives a closed formula for the number of n below p^(k+2) whose central binomial coefficient has p-adic valuation exactly one.

records.title: Poitou's Explicit Odlyzko Bound for Root Discriminants
records.abstract: Formalizes the unconditional explicit-formula argument for a lower bound on root discriminants of totally complex number fields. Develops the completed Dedekind zeta function and its functional equation, Poitou's explicit formula, the Tartar test function, and a certified numerical estimate proving that degree at least 18 forces root discriminant at least 8.25.

informal.NumberField.Odlyzko.odlyzkoBound: Proves that every totally complex number field of degree at least 18 has absolute discriminant at least 8.25 raised to its degree.

records.title: Order closure, order adherence and Fatou norms
records.abstract: Formalizes order and unbounded-order adherence in vector lattices, the Gao-Leung characterization of order-continuous norms on sigma-order-complete Banach lattices, and the Solovay/Stone-space construction of order-complete C(K) spaces with arbitrarily large density and norm-closed separable sublattices whose only order-closed vector-sublattice extension is the whole C(K) space. Constructs solid sets with a prescribed infinite number kappa of solid generators whose adherence towers are strict below any ordinal at most kappa's successor cardinal. Constructs a complete weakly Fatou lattice norm with constant 2 that is not equivalent to any Fatou lattice norm. Includes reusable vector-lattice, net-convergence, sublattice, seminorm, Boolean-algebra and transfinite-iteration infrastructure.

informal.OrderClosures.gaoLeung_orderContinuous_c: For a sigma-order-complete Banach lattice X, the following are equivalent: every vector sublattice has order-closed order adherence; every vector sublattice has equal order and unbounded-order adherence; and the norm of X is order continuous.
informal.OrderClosures.gao_counterexample: For every cardinal kappa there is a compact Hausdorff space K such that C(K, R) is order complete and has density at least kappa, with a norm-closed separable vector sublattice Y whose only order-closed vector-sublattice extension is all of C(K, R).
informal.OrderClosures.solid_sets_require_arbitra: For every infinite cardinal kappa and ordinal xi at most the initial ordinal of kappa's successor cardinal, there is a vector lattice and a solid set with solid generator number kappa whose order-adherence tower has a proper step at every stage below xi. The witness and cardinal/ordinal parameters are lifted one universe in Lean.
informal.OrderClosures.exists_weaklyFatou_not_equ: There is a real vector lattice with a complete lattice norm p satisfying the weak Fatou property with constant 2, such that no lattice norm q with the Fatou property is equivalent to p. Norms, completeness and equivalence are represented explicitly by PaperLatticeNorm, IsCompleteFor and EquivalentNorms.

records.title: Classification of groups of order p * q
records.abstract: Classification of noncyclic finite groups of order p*q, including the prime-square direct-product case and the p<q semidirect-product normal form.

informal.OrderPQ.exists_card_eq_prime_mul_prime_a: There exists a noncyclic group of order p*q exactly when p=q, p divides q-1, or q divides p-1.
informal.OrderPQ.nonempty_mulEquiv_of_card_eq_pri: Any two noncyclic groups of order p*q are isomorphic.
informal.OrderPQ.nonempty_mulEquiv_semidirectProd: If p<q, every group of order p*q is isomorphic to a semidirect product of MulZMod q by MulZMod p.

records.title: Osterwalder-Schrader Axioms for the Gaussian Free Field
records.abstract: Formalizes Osterwalder-Schrader axioms for the massive Gaussian free field using Minlos, covariance, and reflection-positivity infrastructure.

informal.OSforGFF.gaussianFreeField_satisfies_all: Proves that the massive Gaussian free field satisfies the OS0-OS4 Osterwalder-Schrader axioms.

records.title: Clique trees, subtree representations and chordal treewidth
records.abstract: Develops rooted clique forests with the running-intersection property, constructs them from perfect elimination orders of finite chordal graphs, characterizes chordality by their existence, and obtains maximal-clique, separator, and counting results. Also characterizes chordality under retained-clique gluing of induced pieces, with exact vertex and edge inclusion-exclusion identities. The original library was extracted as a reusable byproduct of the published Paper IV formalization of the chordal-graph case of Erdős problem #81; this library is not by itself a proof of that paper's partition bound. Gavril's characterization supplies exact finite-tree subtree representations and the converse to chordality. Finite subtree Helly places every finite clique in a bag of any tree decomposition and gives optimal chordal treewidth. The supplied representation includes an empty connector; no minimal-host or runtime bound is claimed.

informal.SimpleGraph.IsChordal.exists_isPEO: Every finite chordal graph admits a perfect elimination order.
informal.SimpleGraph.isChordal_iff_nonempty_cliqu: A finite graph is chordal if and only if it has a rooted clique tree.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsChordal.exists_maximalCliq: A nonempty finite chordal graph has a clique tree whose distinct bags are precisely its maximal cliques, with no more bags than vertices.
informal.SimpleGraph.CliqueTree.exists_parent_eq_: In a clique tree, each minimal separator of two reachable vertices is the intersection of two adjacent bags.
informal.SimpleGraph.CliqueTree.card_eq_sum_card_: The total bag size minus the total parent-child bag intersection size equals the number of graph vertices.
informal.SimpleGraph.CliqueTree.toSubtreeRepresen: A finite rooted clique forest gives nonempty connected vertex sets of a finite host tree, with adjacency of distinct source vertices exactly equivalent to intersection of their assigned sets. Empty and disconnected source graphs are supported through one empty connector node.
informal.SimpleGraph.isChordal_iff_nonempty_subtr: A finite graph on a vertex type in Type is chordal if and only if it has an exact representation by nonempty connected vertex sets of a finite tree.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsTree.finite_subtree_helly: A finite pairwise-intersecting family of nonempty connected vertex sets of a finite tree has a common vertex; the empty family is also allowed.
informal.Utilities.Treewidth.TreeDecomposition.ex: Every finite clique is contained in one bag of any tree decomposition.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsChordal.treewidth_succ_eq_: For every finite nonempty chordal graph on a vertex type in Type, its natural treewidth plus one equals its clique number.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsChordal.exists_optimal_tre: A finite nonempty chordal graph admits a tree decomposition whose width plus one is its clique number.
informal.SimpleGraph.CliqueGluing.isChordal_iff: If two induced pieces cover a finite graph, their overlap is a clique, and no edge joins their exclusive parts, the graph is chordal exactly when both pieces are chordal. Overlap edges are retained.
informal.SimpleGraph.CliqueGluing.card_vertices_a: The vertex count of the graph plus the overlap size equals the sum of the vertex counts of the two covering pieces.
informal.SimpleGraph.CliqueGluing.card_edges_add_: The graph edge count plus the number of pairs in the retained clique overlap equals the sum of the induced pieces' edge counts.

records.title: Independence of Playfair's axiom via Euclidean and Klein models
records.abstract: Constructs Euclidean and Klein models of a synthetic Hilbert plane, proving that Playfair's axiom is independent of incidence, Pasch order, and congruence axioms, even with Archimedes and Dedekind continuity. Develops reusable coordinate geometry over ordered fields, projective motions, Klein angles and metric, smooth-path length and distance, congruence constructions, and a coordinate curvature calculation. Dedekind continuity replaces Hilbert's maximal completeness axiom; their equivalence is not formalized. Curvature uses Brioschi's formula, and distance uses C1 paths; no identification with Mathlib's Riemannian distance or connection curvature is asserted.

informal.ParallelPostulate.Hilbert.playfair_indep: There exists a Hilbert plane satisfying Archimedes and Dedekind continuity and Playfair's axiom, and there exists another satisfying the same continuity axioms and the negation of Playfair's axiom. The models use real coordinate planes with bounds zero and minus one.
informal.ParallelPostulate.HyperbolicPlane.hyperb: Over any linearly ordered field, for every negative bound and every line in the bounded coordinate plane, infinitely many distinct lines pass through any point of the plane outside that line without meeting it.
informal.ParallelPostulate.HyperbolicPlane.kleinD: For every negative real bound and every pair of points in its plane, the infimum of C1-path lengths in Klein's coordinate metric equals arsinh of the square root of minus the bound times apart, divided by the square root of minus the bound.
informal.ParallelPostulate.HyperbolicPlane.kleinM: For every real bound, Brioschi's coordinate curvature formula applied to the three coefficients of Klein's metric equals that bound at every point of its coordinate plane.

records.title: Parameter-Free Gradient Minimization in l_p Geometry
records.abstract: Exact value-gradient query-complexity results for convex differentiable objectives on finite-dimensional real l_p spaces with attained minima and a positive global primal-to-dual Lipschitz-gradient bound. For finite real p > 1, the development proves strict-local scale-identification impossibility at LR/epsilon = 4 and a deterministic method family with three post-secant-initialization query-rate regimes. For p > 2 it also proves deterministic known-parameter upper and lower query exponents p/(p+2), with explicit horizon and dimension restrictions on the lower bound.

informal.V7.scaleIdentificationImpossibility: For finite real p > 1 and positive epsilon, measurable strict-local exact value-gradient methods satisfy scale-identification lower bounds on convex smooth one-dimensional objectives with unique minimizers, even at LR/epsilon = 4. The result includes deterministic and randomized finite-horizon statements and infinite worst-case expected queried-or-returned hitting time.
informal.V7.knownParameterAboveTwoOptimality: For finite real p > 2 and convex differentiable objectives with attained minima and a positive global primal-to-dual Lipschitz-gradient bound, deterministic known-parameter exact value-gradient methods have upper query exponent p/(p+2). The matching lower exponent concerns the first T queries, requires d >= 2 and 1 <= T <= d, and retains the explicit min(p, log d) dependence.
informal.V7.main: For convex differentiable objectives with attained minima and positive global L-Lipschitz gradients from l_p to its dual, one deterministic family works for every finite real p > 1 and positive epsilon after supplied nondegenerate secant initialization with 0 < M0 <= L. It returns a queried point with dual gradient norm at most epsilon. Writing R for distance to the minimizer set, the post-initialization oracle-call bound has polynomial dependence on max(1, LR/epsilon) with exponent 1/2 for 1 < p < 2 and p = 2, and p/(p+2) for p > 2, plus additive log(e + L/M0) calibration cost. Constants depend only on p, with a universal constant at p = 2; discovering the secant pair is outside the count.

records.title: Partial Combinatory Algebras
records.abstract: Formalises partial combinatory algebras with the K/S combinators, programming combinators, the free combinatory algebra, and the graph model.

informal.LeanPool.PartialCombinatoryAlgebras.PCA: Defines the class of partial combinatory algebras (PCAs) with K and S combinators.
informal.LeanPool.PartialCombinatoryAlgebras.CA: Defines total combinatory algebras and exhibits every total combinatory algebra as a PCA.
informal.LeanPool.PartialCombinatoryAlgebras.Free: Constructs the free total combinatory algebra as a quotient of formal expressions.
informal.LeanPool.PartialCombinatoryAlgebras.Grap: Constructs the graph-model combinatory algebra on the powerset of any Listing-typed carrier.

records.title: Almost all primes are partially regular
records.abstract: Formalizes an asymptotic theorem about partial regularity of primes via Bernoulli-number irregularity.

informal.LeanPool.PartialRegularity.Extension.irr: Proves the asymptotic big-O bound behind the partial-regularity theorem.

records.title: PCF Theory
records.abstract: Formalizes foundational results from Shelah's Possible Cofinality theory, including the existence of club-guessing sequences.

informal.Ordinal.exists_isClubGuessing_of_cof_unc: Proves the existence of a club-guessing sequence on a stationary set whose elements share a common uncountable cofinality bounded by the cofinality of the ambient ordinal.

records.title: Craig interpolation and Beth definability for propositional dynamic logic
records.abstract: Proves Craig interpolation for full propositional dynamic logic, including tests and Kleene star, by constructing interpolants from uniform cyclic tableaux. Interpolants use only atomic propositions and atomic programs common to the two formulas. The development also proves the local Beth definability property for a propositional letter, and supplies reusable syntax, Kripke semantics, Fischer-Ladner closure, tableau soundness and completeness, finite reachability and game-theoretic infrastructure. The results assert existence; no executable extraction algorithm or complexity bound is claimed. Human contributors and Aristotle jointly developed the formalization. The completeness modules reuse the finite game determinacy theorem already pooled in `LeanPool.Lean4GlCoalgebras` instead of duplicating it.

informal.PDL.interpolation: If the implication from PDL formula phi to psi is valid in every Kripke model, there exists a PDL formula theta whose atomic proposition and program vocabulary is contained in the intersection of theirs, such that phi implies theta and theta implies psi in every model.
informal.PDL.beth: If a PDL formula phi implicitly determines a propositional letter p (all two-letter substitutions agree wherever both substituted formulas hold), there is a formula psi using only phi's vocabulary other than p such that phi entails that p is equivalent to psi.
informal.PDL.consIffSat: A free sequent is tableau-consistent if and only if it is satisfiable in a Kripke model.

records.title: Optimal Pebbling Number of the Hypercube
records.abstract: Formalizes that the optimal pebbling number of the n-dimensional hypercube Q_n is Theta((4/3)^n).  Builds a weight-function lower bound of (4/3)^n and a probabilistic recursive upper bound C * (4/3)^n with an explicit constant, combining them into a two-sided big-Theta witness.

informal.PebblingLean.Hypercube.Paper.optimalPebb: The optimal pebbling number of Q_n has order (4/3)^n: there is a positive constant C with (4/3)^n <= o(Q_n) <= C * (4/3)^n for all n.
informal.PebblingLean.Hypercube.Paper.lower_bound: The optimal pebbling number of Q_n is at least (4/3)^n, proved by a weight-function argument summing one-pebble weights over the cube.
informal.PebblingLean.Hypercube.Paper.upper_bound: The optimal pebbling number of Q_n is at most C * (4/3)^n for an explicit constant C, via a probabilistic recursive splitting construction.

records.title: Euler's pentagonal number theorem, two independent proofs, and the Jacobi triple product
records.abstract: Two independent proofs of Euler's pentagonal number theorem that share no lemmas, so each confirms the result on its own. The primary development is combinatorial: Franklin's sign-reversing involution on partitions into distinct parts, giving p_e(n) - p_o(n) = (-1)^|k| when n is the generalized pentagonal number k(3k-1)/2 and 0 otherwise, stated under a single integer index, together with the identification of that signed count with the coefficient of X^n in the truncated product over ℤ⟦X⟧. It builds on Mathlib's Nat.Partition.genFun. The second route develops q-Pochhammer symbols, the Gaussian binomial coefficient, Euler's two identities and the Cauchy identity, proves the Jacobi triple product both as a formal power series identity in (LaurentPolynomial ℂ)⟦X⟧ and analytically over ℂ for ‖q‖ < 1, and reaches the same theorem for the infinite product by specialization. The Lean proofs in both routes were largely generated by Aristotle; the Franklin route additionally has an author-written blueprint that the formalization follows lemma by lemma, and carries substantially more manual intervention and review, whereas the q-series route is machine-generated blueprint and all. The Franklin route and the analytic pentagonal number theorem overlap the pooled `pentagonal-number-theorem` development, which states its analytic form over RCLike fields rather than only over the complex numbers; the q-Pochhammer, Gaussian binomial and Euler identity definitions overlap arXiv:2607.01544. The project's distinct contribution is the complex-analytic layer: an analytic Jacobi triple product over the complex numbers for norm q < 1, its extension to the punctured disc, the analytic Cauchy identity, and the summability and locally-uniform-convergence machinery they require. Neither the pooled entry nor the non-archimedean development of arXiv:2607.01544 covers that setting.

informal.PentagonalNumberTheorem.Franklin.euler_p: The primary result. For every n, either n is a generalized pentagonal number k(3k-1)/2 for some integer k, in which case the number of partitions of n into an even number of distinct parts exceeds the number with an odd number of distinct parts by exactly (-1)^|k|; or n is not of that form, in which case the two counts are equal. Proved by Franklin's sign-reversing involution.
informal.PentagonalNumberTheorem.Franklin.coeff_p: The coefficient of X^n in the truncated product ∏_{k=1}^{n}(1 - X^k) over ℤ⟦X⟧ equals p_e(n) - p_o(n), the signed count of partitions of n into distinct parts. Truncating at n is harmless because the omitted factors are ≡ 1 mod X^{n+1}.
informal.QSeries.jacobiTripleProduct: For ‖q‖ < 1, ‖z‖ < 1 and z ≠ 0, the product (q;q)_∞ (-z;q)_∞ (-q/z;q)_∞ equals the bilateral theta series ∑_{k ∈ ℤ} z^k q^{k(k-1)/2}.
informal.QSeries.euler_pentagonal_number: For ‖q‖ < 1, the infinite product (q;q)_∞ equals ∑_{k ∈ ℤ} (-1)^k q^{ω(k)} over the generalized pentagonal numbers ω(k) = k(3k-1)/2, written as two one-sided sums. Obtained from the Jacobi triple product by specialization.
informal.QSeries.FormalPowerSeries.jacobiTriplePr: The Jacobi triple product as an identity of formal power series in (LaurentPolynomial ℂ)-coefficient power series, with no convergence hypothesis: the product of q-Pochhammer symbols equals the bilateral theta series coefficientwise.

records.title: Euler's pentagonal number theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes Euler's pentagonal number theorem as a generating-function identity for power series and for real/complex numbers, with a partition-recurrence corollary and a self-contained Franklin-style combinatorial proof.

informal.pentagonalNumberTheorem_powerSeries: Proves Euler's pentagonal number theorem as a formal power series identity ∏(1-xⁿ) = Σ(-1)ᵏ x^(k(3k-1)/2).
informal.pentagonalNumberTheorem_complex: Proves the analytic version of the pentagonal number theorem for real or complex numbers of norm less than one.
informal.Nat.Partition.sum_partition: Derives Euler's pentagonal recurrence for the partition function from the pentagonal number theorem.

records.title: Quartic-over-logarithmic lower bound for rational permanent formulas
records.abstract: Proves that every valid rational arithmetic formula over the complex numbers computing the n-by-n permanent, for n at least 32, has at least n^4 / (192 log_2 n) variable leaves. The development derives the bound through coefficient-field transcendence degree, Jacobian minors, matching-polynomial identities, and a cyclic block decomposition.

informal.PermanentFormulaLowerBound.permanent_rat: For n at least 32, every valid rational formula over the complex numbers that computes the n-by-n permanent has at least n^4 / (192 log_2 n) variable leaves.
The same quartic-over-logarithmic lower bound controls variable leaves, total leaves, and vertices, and half that bound controls internal gates.

records.title: Stable phase retrieval for Hermite-Fock expansions
records.abstract: Formalizes stable phase retrieval for finite Hermite-Fock polynomials and their Gaussian L2 closure in d complex dimensions, together with the quantitative one-dimensional Fock-space local stability estimate that underlies it.

informal.DimdPolyShowcaseChallenge.stable_phase_r: Proves stable phase retrieval for the Gaussian L2 closure of finite d-dimensional Hermite-Fock polynomials at a fixed level, giving a uniform stability constant bounding the phase-aligned L2 distance by the L2 distance of magnitudes.
informal.FockSPR.orthogonalReduction_exists_phase: Proves the phase-aligned one-dimensional Fock-space local stability estimate, producing a unit phase for which the L2 distance to one is controlled by the magnitude defect.
informal.FockSPR.orthogonalReduction_core: Proves the quantitative centered core estimate bounding the Gaussian Fock norm of a polynomial with small norm by the magnitude defect against one.
informal.FockSPR.LocalFockSPR: Proves the local Fock-space stable phase retrieval coercivity estimate for centered polynomials.
informal.DimdPolyShowcaseChallenge.HermitePoly: Defines the normalized one-variable complex Hermite-Fock basis polynomial.
informal.DimdPolyShowcaseChallenge.TrueHermiteFun: Defines the Gaussian L2 closure of finite Hermite-Fock polynomials at a fixed level.

records.title: Accelerated Nesterov convergence under local Polyak-Lojasiewicz conditions
records.abstract: Formalizes accelerated Nesterov convergence near a smooth minimizer manifold under a local Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition, including embedded-manifold and C3 public theorem statements with explicit exponential rate and prefactor.

informal.PLAcceleratedNesterovLean.nesterov_pl_ac: Proves an accelerated Nesterov convergence rate for state positions near a C2 embedded minimizer manifold, with an existential momentum parameter, explicit exponential decay, and prefactor 2.
Proves the corresponding C3 public theorem, deriving the minimizer geometry internally from smoothness and the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition.
informal.PLAcceleratedNesterovLean.nesterov_conve: Provides the reusable local theta-retuned convergence theorem used by the public accelerated-rate statements.

records.title: Poincaré's Nonintegrability Theorem for the Restricted Three-Body Problem
records.abstract: Formalizes Poincaré's classical parameter-analytic nonintegrability theorem for the planar circular restricted three-body problem. The development defines the rotating-frame Hamiltonian on its collision-free domain, proves logarithmic blow-up of the resonant disturbing average at an apoapsis collision boundary, and analytically propagates the resulting dense resonant obstruction to exclude an additional analytic first integral. The final statement is the fixed-coordinate, global uniform-domain special case of the planar part of Yagasaki's Theorem 1.1; his local meromorphic resonant-orbit obstruction is Theorem 3.1.

informal.LeanPool.PoincareThreeBody.nonintegrabil: No jointly real-analytic family near zero mass can be an additional first integral of the planar circular restricted three-body Hamiltonian with phase differential independent from the Hamiltonian differential anywhere on the uniform collision-free domain.
informal.LeanPool.PoincareThreeBody.delaunayHomol: If the first homological equation holds and its perturbing Fourier coefficient is nonzero at every positive rational Kepler resonance, then the leading differential of a putative analytic first integral is nowhere independent of the unperturbed Hamiltonian frequency.
informal.LeanPool.PoincareThreeBody.delaunayDense: For the rotating Kepler frequency in Delaunay actions, orthogonality of a continuous candidate differential to every positive rational resonance vector forces dependence with the Hamiltonian frequency at every positive action.
informal.LeanPool.PoincareThreeBody.homologicalEq: At a resonant action in two degrees of freedom, a nonzero perturbing Fourier mode and the first homological equation force the unperturbed frequency and the differential of a putative leading first-integral coefficient to be linearly dependent.
informal.LeanPool.PoincareThreeBody.denseResonanc: If the resonant obstruction holds on a dense set of actions and the frequency and differential vary continuously, then they are linearly dependent at every action.

records.title: Pointwise Birkhoff Ergodic Theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the pointwise Birkhoff ergodic theorem for integrable real-valued observables.

informal.LeanPool.PointwiseBirkhoff.birkhoffErgod: Proves almost-everywhere convergence of Birkhoff averages to invariant conditional expectation for any integrable real-valued observable.
Proves the measurable-observable version of the pointwise Birkhoff ergodic theorem.

records.title: Pólya's enumeration theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes Pólya's enumeration theorem counting orbits of colorings under a group action.

informal.LeanPool.PolyaEnumerationTheorem.polya_t: Counts distinct colorings of a finite set under a group action by averaging powers of the number of colors over cycle indices.

records.title: Polylean Unit Conjecture Counterexample
records.abstract: Formalizes Gardam's counterexample to Kaplansky's Unit Conjecture, including the Promislow group, group rings, torsion-freeness of the group, and the non-trivial unit in 𝔽₂[P].

informal.LeanPool.Polylean.P.torsionFree: Proves that the Promislow group used in Gardam's construction is torsion-free.
informal.LeanPool.Polylean.Gardam.GardamTheorem: Proves Gardam's counterexample to Kaplansky's Unit Conjecture by constructing a non-trivial unit in the group ring 𝔽₂[P].

records.title: Polylogarithms and sixteen log-trigonometric integral identities
records.abstract: Formalizes the sixteen A-series identities from rainrzk's PolyLog Integrals tutorial, together with reusable real and complex polylogarithm series, absolute convergence on the closed unit disk, differentiation, duplication, Euler reflection and Landen identities, logarithmic moments, Fubini kernels and radial integration machinery. The formulas involve Catalan's constant, zeta(3), Li_4(1/2) and Im Li_3((1+i)/2). These are classical identities, not new informal results. A004 uses the corrected factor pi^2/24; A014 uses a proved expression entirely inside the unit disk, replacing the tutorial's invalid series expansion. A015 uses radial differentiation instead of a half-disc contour integral. The formalization was materially completed on 2026-10-01 at 00:01:57 UTC. The 2022 informal tutorial is older; the eligibility date is that of the completed Lean proofs.

informal.LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A001: Li_2(i) equals -pi^2/48 plus i times Catalan's constant.
informal.LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A002: Li_2(1/(1+i)) equals 5 pi^2/96 - log^2(2)/8 plus i times (pi log(2)/8 - G).
informal.LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A004: The integral from 0 to 1 of log(1+x^2)/x equals pi^2/24, correcting the tutorial's factor of two.
informal.LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A005: The integral from 0 to 1 of log^2(1+x^2)/x^3 equals pi^2/12 - log^2(2).
informal.LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A006_cos: The integral from 0 to pi/4 of log(cos x) equals G/2 - (pi/4) log(2).
informal.LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A006_sin: The integral from 0 to pi/4 of log(sin x) equals -G/2 - (pi/4) log(2).
informal.LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A007: The integral from 0 to pi/4 of x log(cos x) equals pi G/8 - pi^2 log(2)/32 - 21 zeta(3)/128.
informal.LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A008: The integral from 0 to pi/4 of x log(1+tan x) equals pi^2 log(2)/64 - pi G/8 + 21 zeta(3)/64.
informal.LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A009: The integral from 0 to pi/2 of x^2 cot x equals pi^2 log(2)/4 - 7 zeta(3)/8.
informal.LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A010: The integral from 0 to pi/4 of x^2 tan^2 x equals -G + pi^2/16 - pi^3/192 + pi log(2)/4.
informal.LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A011: The integral from 0 to 1 of Li_2(x)/(x sqrt(1-x^2)) equals 3 pi^2 log(2)/8 - 7 zeta(3)/16.
informal.LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A012: The integral from 0 to 1 of arctan(x) log(x)/(1+x) equals -pi^3/64 + G log(2)/2.
informal.LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A013: The integral from 0 to 1 of arctan(x) log^2(x)/(1+x) equals -pi^2 G/24 - pi^3 log(2)/32 + 21 pi zeta(3)/64.
informal.LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A014: The integral from 0 to 1 of log(x) log(1+x)/(1+x^2) equals 11 pi^3/128 + 3 pi log^2(2)/32 - 2 G log(2) - 3 Im Li_3((1+i)/2).
informal.LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A015: The integral from 0 to pi/2 of x log^2(sin x) equals Li_4(1/2) - 19 pi^4/2880 + log^4(2)/24 + pi^2 log^2(2)/12.
informal.LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A016: The integral from 0 to 1 of Li_3(x)/(x sqrt(1-x^2)) equals Li_4(1/2)/2 + 41 pi^4/5760 + log^4(2)/48 + pi^2 log^2(2)/6.
informal.LeanPolyLog.Dilog.hasDerivAt_Li_succ: For every natural s and nonzero complex z in the open unit disk, Li_(s+1) has derivative Li_s(z)/z at z.
informal.LeanPolyLog.Dilog.Li_two_add_Li_two_div_: For complex z of norm at most 1 and real part at most 1/2, Li_2(z) + Li_2(z/(z-1)) = -log^2(1-z)/2, with the principal logarithm.
informal.LeanPolyLog.Arcsin.integral_Lir_div_mul_: For s at least 2 and a measurable nonnegative weight w on (0,1] with integrable moments equal to 1/(n+1)^s, the integral from 0 to 1 of Li_s(x)/(x sqrt(1-x^2)) equals the integral from 0 to pi/2 of w(sin t) times (pi/2+t).
informal.LeanPolyLog.Radial.integral_im_logCube: If (log^3((1+r)/2)-log^3((1-r)/2))/r is interval integrable from 0 to 1, its integral equals the integral from 0 to pi of the imaginary part of the cube of the principal complex logarithm of (1+exp(i t))/2.

records.title: The polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture
records.abstract: Formalizes Marton's polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture by the entropy method, including the characteristic-two bounds with exponents twelve and nine, the bounded-torsion theorem with an explicit exponent, and quantitative consequences for affine dimension and approximate homomorphisms. The supporting development builds entropic Ruzsa distance, multidistance, conditional entropy, and additive-energy machinery. This optimized import reuses the pooled Zhang–Yeung entropy and kernel library in place of duplicate upstream modules while preserving all six closed headline statements.

informal.Marton.pfr_conjecture: A nonempty finite set A of doubling at most K in an abelian group of exponent two is covered by fewer than 2 K^12 cosets of a finite subgroup no larger than A.
informal.Marton.pfr_conjecture_nine: Strengthens the characteristic-two covering theorem to fewer than 2 K^9 cosets of a finite subgroup no larger than A.
informal.Marton.torsion_pfr_conjecture: In an abelian group of exponent m at least two, a nonempty finite set of doubling at most K is covered by fewer than m K^(256 m^3 + 1) cosets of a subgroup no larger than A.
informal.Marton.weak_pfr_int: A nonempty finite set of doubling at most K in a finite-rank free abelian group has a subset of relative size at least K^(-34) and affine dimension at most (80 / log 2) log K.
informal.Marton.homomorphism_pfr: A map between finite abelian groups of exponent two whose additive defects lie in S differs from a homomorphism by a map taking at most |S|^10 values.
informal.Marton.approx_hom_pfr: A map between finite abelian groups of exponent two that is additive on at least a 1/K fraction of pairs agrees with a homomorphism on at least (|G| / (2^144 K^122) - 1) / 2 points.

records.title: The polynomial method and restricted sums of congruence classes
records.abstract: Formalizes the polynomial method (Alon–Tarsi-style combinatorial Nullstellensatz arguments) and applies it to restricted sums of congruence classes, including Cauchy–Davenport, Dias da Silva–Hamidoune, and a Vandermonde coefficient formula.

informal.ANR_polynomial_method: The Alon–Nathanson–Rusza polynomial method theorem, giving a non-vanishing-coefficient criterion for restricted sums.
informal.cauchy_davenport: The Cauchy–Davenport theorem on sums of subsets of the cyclic group of prime order.
informal.dias_da_silva_hamidoune: The Dias da Silva–Hamidoune lower bound for restricted sums of distinct elements in a prime cyclic group.
informal.restricted_sum_distinct_sizes: A lower bound for restricted sums when the summand sets have distinct sizes.
informal.Vandermonde_coefficient_formula: A closed-form expression for a specific Vandermonde-style coefficient used by the polynomial method.

records.title: Puiseux's theorem
records.abstract: Constructs Puiseux series as the bounded-denominator subfield of rational-exponent Hahn series. Proves that this field is algebraic over Laurent series over any coefficient field, and is an algebraic closure when the coefficient field is algebraically closed of characteristic zero. The Newton-Puiseux proof includes reusable Hensel splitting and polynomial translation lemmas. Dean Cureton directed the AI formalization and subsequently simplified its proofs.

informal.PuiseuxSeries.isAlgClosure: For an algebraically closed field K of characteristic zero, the field of Puiseux series over K is an algebraic closure of the Laurent series field K((t)).
informal.PuiseuxSeries.isAlgebraic: Over any field K, the Puiseux series field is algebraic over the Laurent series field.
informal.PuiseuxSeries.mem_subfield_iff_support: A rational-exponent Hahn series belongs to the Puiseux subfield if and only if its support lies in (1/n) times the integers for some positive integer n.
informal.Polynomial.Monic.exists_factorization_ro: A monic degree-m polynomial over K[[t]] whose reduction has a root of multiplicity k, with 0 < k < m, factors into monic polynomials of degrees k and m-k.

records.title: Pumping Lemma for Context-Free Grammars
records.abstract: Formalizes the pumping lemma for context-free languages via parse trees of Chomsky-normal-form grammars and a pigeonhole argument.

informal.Language.IsContextFree.pumping: Every context-free language admits a pumping length p such that any word of length at least p decomposes as u v x y z with vy nonempty, vxy of length at most p, and u vⁱ x yⁱ z in the language for every i.
informal.ChomskyNormalFormGrammar.pumping: The pumping lemma at the level of a Chomsky-normal-form grammar, obtained from a sufficiently tall parse tree with a repeated nonterminal.

records.title: Polynomial parametrizations of Pythagorean triples
records.abstract: Formalizes Frisch and Vaserstein's result that Pythagorean triples are not parametrizable by one triple of integer-coefficient polynomials in any number of variables, but are parametrizable by a single triple of integer-valued rational polynomials, including the positive and sixteen-parameter variants.

informal.LeanPool.PythagoreanPolynomialParametriz: Proves that no single triple of integer-coefficient polynomials in any number of variables parametrizes all Pythagorean triples.
Gives the explicit four-variable integer-valued polynomial parametrization of all Pythagorean triples.
Formalizes the positive Pythagorean-triple parametrization with positive parameters and a nonnegative auxiliary parameter.
Converts the positive parametrization to an unrestricted sixteen-integer-parameter parametrization using the four-square theorem.
Proves the cited reduction from one integer-valued polynomial tuple to finitely many integer-coefficient polynomial tuples.
Records the integer-valued polynomial ring non-UFD phenomenon behind the paper's motivating discussion.

records.title: Quantum code certificates and hypergraph-product theory
records.abstract: Formalizes general binary row reduction, kernel bases and rank certificates; quantum-code distance bounds from witnesses and exhaustive low-weight enumeration; arbitrary-matrix hypergraph-product dimension and X/Z cleaning bounds; and CSS orthogonality of lifted products over finite groups. Includes a Pauli expression translation modulo global phase, a Boolean encoding with proved soundness and model extension, and sound checking of RUP additions in LRAT certificates, bridged to matrix-level distance bounds. Concrete code-family datasets, large certificate replays and measurement protocols are outside this import.

informal.QECCertificates.hgp_kunneth: For arbitrary finite binary matrices A and B, the number of columns of their hypergraph product minus its X and Z ranks equals nullity(A) times nullity(B) plus nullity(transpose A) times nullity(transpose B), expressed with natural-number rank differences.
informal.QECCertificates.hgp_X_distance_ge: If a binary vector is killed by the hypergraph-product X check and is outside the Z row space, its Hamming weight is at least the minimum of supplied lower bounds for nonzero vectors in the kernels of the first input and the transpose of the second input.
informal.QECCertificates.hgp_Z_distance_ge: Dually, a vector killed by the Z check and outside the X row space has weight at least the minimum of supplied lower bounds for the kernels of the transpose of the first input and the second input.
informal.QECCertificates.lp_orthogonal: For arbitrary matrices of binary-valued functions on a finite group, the left/right regular expansion gives lifted-product X and Z checks whose every pair of rows has zero binary dot product.
informal.QECCertificates.Matrix.rank_eq_length_ro: The rank of a finite binary matrix equals the length of the verified row-reduction output for its list of rows.
informal.QECCertificates.eq_minWeight_of_decide: For two binary matrices, if d is at most the number of columns, exhaustive enumeration finds no vector of weight below d in the first kernel outside the second row space, and a supplied vector has those membership properties and weight d, then the minimum such weight is d. The empty-set distance convention is the number of columns plus one.
informal.QECCertificates.LRAT.unsat_of_checkSteps: Acceptance by the RUP certificate checker implies unsatisfiability of the original CNF. No correctness assumption on an external SAT solver is needed; the clause-database interface carries proved soundness laws.
informal.QECCertificates.LRAT.buildPair_complete: For a positive number n of input bits and nonempty row supports within that range, a Boolean assignment satisfying the parity constraints, odd bilinear pairing and weight bound extends to a model of buildPair while agreeing on all 2n input variables. The complementary soundness theorem extracts those constraints from every model.
informal.QECCertificates.LRAT.le_minWeight_of_uns: For a positive number n of columns and k + 1 ≤ n, an unsatisfiable Boolean encoding gives a matrix-level distance lower bound of k + 1. Support-row correspondence, nonemptiness, index bounds and duplicate-free hypotheses are explicit. This composes with kernel-checked RUP replay.

records.title: Endpoint estimates for Stein's purely quadratic Carleson operator
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of four principal endpoint assertions from Fragkos, Krause, and Lacey's Endpoint Estimates for Stein's Purely Quadratic Carleson Operator: two failures of modular estimates below t log₂ t, a full-modulation L log L endpoint estimate, and a lacunary L (log₂ L)² log₄ L endpoint estimate.

informal.QuadraticCarleson.StatementSurface.Paper: Lacunary purely quadratic modulation fails modular estimates below the specified iterated-logarithmic threshold.
Full purely quadratic modulation fails modular estimates below the specified iterated-logarithmic threshold.
The full-modulation operator satisfies the L log L endpoint estimate.
The lacunary operator satisfies the L (log₂ L)² log₄ L endpoint estimate.

records.title: Galois groups of quadratic polynomial iterates
records.abstract: Formalizes Stoll's criterion for when the Galois group of the n-th iterate of X² + a over the rationals is the full n-fold iterated wreath product of C₂. It proves the criterion in terms of two-independence of a signed critical-orbit sequence and its pairwise-coprime Möbius factors, and derives the paper's congruence families for which maximality holds at every level. The supporting library develops reusable multiquadratic-extension, iterated wreath-product, Möbius-factor, and valuation results.

informal.QuadraticIterates.section1_equiv: For each n, assuming -a is not a rational square, the Galois group of the n-th iterate of X² + a is the full n-fold iterated wreath product of C₂ exactly when either the first n terms of the signed sequence c₁ = -a, cₖ = fₖ(0) for k ≥ 2, or the first n integer Möbius factors of that sequence are independent modulo rational squares.
informal.QuadraticIterates.section1_squarefree: If -a is not a rational square and none of the absolute Möbius factors from levels 2 through n is a rational square, then the n-th iterate has the full iterated-wreath-product Galois group.
informal.QuadraticIterates.section3_main: The Galois group is the full iterated wreath product at every positive level when a is positive and congruent to 1 or 2 modulo 4, or when a is negative and divisible by 4 with -a nonsquare.

records.title: Quantum parallel repetition
records.abstract: Proves a quantitative parallel-repetition theorem for finite two-player quantum games: whenever the entangled value is below one, the entangled values of parallel repetitions decay exponentially, with an explicit universal exponent in the game gap and answer-alphabet sizes.

informal.QuantumParallelRepetition.distributionUn: There is a universal positive constant giving an explicit exponential upper bound on the repeated entangled value of every finite game with positive gap and nonempty answer alphabets.
informal.QuantumParallelRepetition.standardQuantu: Every finite two-player game whose entangled value is below one has exponentially decaying entangled value under parallel repetition.

records.title: Adversary bounds and the polynomial method for quantum queries
records.abstract: Develops finite quantum query algorithms, real adversary primal and dual programs, strong duality, exact Boolean block composition, explicit constant-factor bounded-error query characterizations, and degree bounds for output-probability polynomials. Query models include idle and blank sectors; bounds count queries, not gate complexity or running time. Uniform algorithm extraction assumes a supplied dual certificate.

informal.QuantumQueryComplexity.advDual_eq_advPM: For every total Boolean function on a finite Boolean input cube, the all-pairs real adversary dual infimum equals the real symmetric primal supremum.
informal.QuantumQueryComplexity.advPM_composeFun_: The negative-weight adversary value of total Boolean functions composed on disjoint blocks equals the product of their adversary values, including constant functions and empty index types.
informal.QuantumQueryComplexity.boundedErrorQQuer: For a total Boolean function at error one third, quantum value-query complexity lies between ADV±/36 and 2^14 ADV±. The value oracle swaps a blank answer with the queried letter and includes an idle query index.
informal.QuantumQueryComplexity.xorQQuery_charact: For the Boolean XOR oracle with idle and blank sectors, query complexity at error one third lies between ADV±/72 and 2^15 ADV±.
informal.QuantumQueryComplexity.qQueryOn_third_le: A supplied all-pairs real dual certificate of nonnegative cost c gives a finite quantum algorithm using at most 8192(1+c) value queries at error one third, for any finite promise domain and nonempty decidable output type.
informal.QuantumQueryComplexity.QAlg.exists_proba: Each output probability of a q-query value-oracle algorithm on Boolean inputs agrees on the Boolean cube with a real polynomial of total degree at most 2q.
informal.QuantumQueryComplexity.exists_xor_probab: Each output probability of a q-query Boolean XOR algorithm agrees on the Boolean cube with a real polynomial of total degree at most 2q.

records.title: Quasi-Borel Spaces
records.abstract: Formalizes quasi-Borel spaces and quasi-Borel pre-domains, a category for higher-order probability theory.

informal.QuasiBorelSpace: Defines a quasi-Borel space as a type with a set of random variables closed under constants, measurable precomposition, and gluing.
informal.QuasiBorelSpace.IsHom: Defines morphisms of quasi-Borel spaces as maps that preserve random variables under precomposition.
informal.OmegaQuasiBorelSpace: Combines the quasi-Borel and ω-complete partial order structures with the compatibility axiom of Vakar-Kammar-Staton.
informal.QuasiBorelSpace.ProbabilityMeasure: Defines the probability-measure monad on quasi-Borel spaces by quotienting pre-probability measures by integral equivalence.

records.title: Radó's theorem for Riemann surfaces
records.abstract: Proves that every connected Hausdorff one-dimensional complex manifold is second countable. The development constructs a nonconstant harmonic function by Perron's method, builds the étale space of its harmonic-conjugate germs, and applies a formalized Poincaré-Volterra lemma to its discrete-fiber evaluation map.

informal.rado_riemannSurface: Every connected Hausdorff topological space carrying the structure of a one-dimensional complex manifold has a second-countable topology.
informal.Rado.poincare_volterra: A connected Hausdorff, locally compact, locally connected and locally second-countable space is second countable whenever it admits a continuous, locally injective map into a second-countable Hausdorff space.
informal.Rado.exists_harmonic_extension: Every continuous real-valued function on a Euclidean circle extends continuously to its closed disk and harmonically to the open disk; unlike the existing LeanComplexAnalysis Poisson theorems, this constructs the harmonic function rather than assuming one.
informal.Rado.IsPerronFamily.surfaceHarmonicOn_pe: The pointwise upper envelope of a Perron family of surface subharmonic functions is harmonic on its open domain.

records.title: The Ramanujan-Nagell theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the Ramanujan-Nagell theorem, proving that the Diophantine equation x^2 + 7 = 2^n has exactly the five positive-integer solutions (|x|, n) = (1, 3), (3, 4), (5, 5), (11, 7), (181, 15).

informal.ramanujanNagellExact: Proves that the integer solutions of x^2 + 7 = 2^n are exactly (x, n) = (+/-1, 3), (+/-3, 4), (+/-5, 5), (+/-11, 7), (+/-181, 15).

records.title: ABC implies that Ramanujan's tau function misses almost all primes
records.abstract: Formalizes the ABC-conditional proof that Ramanujan's tau function takes prime values only rarely.

informal.main_theorem: ABC implies that Ramanujan's tau function misses almost all primes.
informal.reduction_lemma: Reduces the main prime-value statement to the key analytic estimates.
informal.abc_bound_E2: ABC-bound input for the Eisenstein-series term E2.
informal.abc_bound_E4: ABC-bound input for the Eisenstein-series term E4.

records.title: Improved Lower Bounds for Strong n-Conjectures
records.abstract: Formalizes the disproof of Ramaekers's conjecture, constructing tuple families whose abc-style quality stays bounded above 1, and proves Browkin-Brzezinski lower bounds on the quality of the n-conjecture tuples.

informal.RamaekersConjecture: Defines Ramaekers's conjecture for fixed n as the statement that the quality of the relevant tuple set equals 1.
informal.not_ramaekersConjecture_ge_six: Proves Ramaekers's conjecture fails for every n at least 6 (the general case, Theorem 1.14).
informal.not_ramaekersConjecture_odd_ge_five: Proves Ramaekers's conjecture fails for every odd n at least 5 (the odd case via Pell equations, Theorem 1.13).
informal.not_ramaekersConjecture_five: Proves Ramaekers's conjecture fails for n equal to 5 (the Konyagin prelude bound).
informal.le_quality_nConjectureTuples: Proves the Browkin-Brzezinski 1994 lower bound 2n-5 on the quality of the n-conjecture tuples (Theorem 1.3).

records.title: A proof of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture, formalized
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture. A complex-valued graph parameter, normalized at the empty graph and invariant under isomorphism, has exponentially bounded edge-connection rank if and only if it is a mixed partition function. For a natural rank base R, a representing model can be chosen with k even and 2ℓ odd colours satisfying k + 2ℓ ≤ R. The development also proves the even connection-rank growth limit, minimum total colour dimension, minimal parity formulas and prescribed-dimension criterion. Schrijver's factorial argument supplies nilpotent-trace vanishing; semisimplicity and Deligne's fibre-functor theorem give the model; a polynomial commutant estimate gives the sharp colour budget. Deligne's theorem and the required symmetric-group character theory are proved within the development. The appendix's trace-zeta results give rationality and degree bounds, with an independent proof of nilpotent-trace vanishing. The theorems of record use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, checked by pinned audits.

informal.RS.regts_sevenster_characterisation: Normalized isomorphism-invariant complex graph parameters with exponentially bounded edge-connection ranks are precisely mixed partition functions.
informal.RS.regts_sevenster_total: A natural rank bound R admits a representing mixed model with total color dimension at most R.
informal.RS.deligne_theorem: The development proves its stated Deligne fiber-functor theorem for the symmetric tensor categories used in the representation.

records.title: Rellich–Kondrachov compact embedding theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the Rellich–Kondrachov compact embedding theorem: the Sobolev embedding H¹ → L² is a compact operator on compact Riemannian manifolds. The proof builds the Euclidean core (compactness of the H¹ → L² inclusion on a fixed compact support via the Fréchet–Kolmogorov criterion and the H¹ translation estimate ‖τₐu − u‖₂ ≤ ‖a‖ · ‖∇u‖₂), glues chart contributions over a finite atlas, and specializes to the Levi-Civita Riemannian volume measure.

informal.RellichKondrachov.Geometry.Manifold.Sobo: On a compact Riemannian manifold, the Sobolev inclusion H¹ → L² for the Levi-Civita volume measure is a compact operator.
informal.RellichKondrachov.Analysis.FunctionalSpa: Euclidean Rellich–Kondrachov compactness: on a fixed compact support K, the H¹ → L² inclusion restricted to functions supported in K is a compact operator.
informal.RellichKondrachov.Geometry.Manifold.Sobo: On a compact Riemannian manifold there exists finite chart data equipped with explicit Lipschitz neighborhoods and a subordinate partition of unity, the input to the manifold Rellich glue.

records.title: Riemann Mapping Theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes a proof of the Riemann mapping theorem for proper simply connected plane domains with primitives.

informal.RMT: Proves the Riemann mapping theorem for the project's domain hypotheses.
informal.main: Constructs a conformal map from a good domain onto the unit disk.
informal.montel: Proves a Montel compactness theorem for uniformly bounded holomorphic families.
informal.hurwitz: Proves the Hurwitz theorem used to preserve injectivity under limits.

records.title: Riemann–Roch for algebraic function fields
records.abstract: Formalizes the Riemann–Roch theorem for algebraic function fields of one variable through the adelic route. Divisors are indexed by intrinsic places (discrete rank-one valuation subrings containing the constants), with an equivalence to a two-chart coordinate model via Ostrowski's theorem. The development builds Riemann–Roch spaces, the genus, an intrinsic adele space, Weil differentials and the canonical class, and proves Riemann's inequality, the duality theorem, Riemann–Roch, Clifford's inequality, and the standard corollaries. As an application it shows that a Weierstrass elliptic curve has genus one and identifies its degree-one places with the class group of the coordinate ring compatibly with the group law.

informal.FunctionField.riemann_roch: For a function field K over its full constant field k, a canonical divisor W, and any divisor D indexed by intrinsic places, ℓ(D) = deg D + 1 − g + ℓ(W − D).
informal.FunctionField.duality: For a canonical divisor W and any divisor D, ℓ(W − D) equals the index of specialty i(D), the codimension of L(D) plus K inside the adele space.
informal.FunctionField.riemann_ineq: Riemann's inequality ℓ(D) ≥ deg D + 1 − g holds for every divisor D.
informal.FunctionField.clifford: Clifford's inequality 2(ℓ(D) − 1) ≤ deg D holds for every divisor D with 0 ≤ deg D ≤ 2g − 2, ℓ(D) > 0, and ℓ(W − D) > 0 for a canonical divisor W. The degree bounds are not needed for the inequality and are dropped in FunctionField.clifford_of_ell_pos.
informal.FunctionField.exists_isCanonical: Every function field admits a canonical divisor, namely the divisor of a nonzero Weil differential.
informal.WeierstrassCurve.Affine.genus_eq_one: The function field of a Weierstrass elliptic curve over a field k that is its full constant field (for example any algebraically closed k, in any characteristic) has genus one.
informal.WeierstrassCurve.Affine.picTorsor_compat: The bijection between degree-one places of an elliptic function field and the class group of the coordinate ring is compatible with the elliptic group law.

records.title: RL Theory in Lean
records.abstract: Develops probability, Markov-chain, and stochastic-matrix infrastructure for reinforcement-learning theory.

informal.StochasticMatrix.stationary_distribution: Proves existence of a stationary distribution for a stochastic matrix.

records.title: Explicit type Aₙ and BCₙ root pairings
records.abstract: Constructs the type Aₙ and BCₙ root pairings explicitly over ℤ — from signed intervals on Fin n and from the reflective vectors of the standard dot product — proves the pairing and reflection identities exhibiting them as Mathlib `RootPairing`s, and identifies the BCₙ roots with the classical set {±eᵢ, ±2eᵢ, ±eᵢ ± eⱼ}.

informal.An.rootPairing: Constructs the type Aₙ root pairing over the integers from signed intervals on Fin n, with finiteness, reducedness, and crystallographic properties.
informal.BCn.rootPairing: Constructs the type BCₙ root pairing from the reflective vectors of the standard dot product on ℤⁿ via a symmetric nondegenerate form.
informal.BCn.isReflective_iff_isClassicalRoot: Characterizes the reflective vectors of the standard dot product on ℤⁿ as exactly the classical type BCₙ roots ±eᵢ, ±2eᵢ, and ±eᵢ ± eⱼ for i ≠ j.
informal.BCn.range_rootPairing_root: Identifies the root set of the type BCₙ root pairing with the classical type BCₙ root set.

records.title: The nonmeagre lower bound for the rearrangement number
records.abstract: Formalizes the inequality non(M) ≤ rr in ZFC via relational systems, category and slalom bounds, finite-vector constructions, and rearrangements of conditionally convergent real series. The reverse inequality from the accompanying manuscript is outside the upstream Lean formalization.

informal.NonMRR.nonM_le_rr: The uniformity of the meagre ideal is at most the rearrangement number.

records.title: Certified Runge-Kutta Order Conditions
records.abstract: Certifies Runge-Kutta order conditions over planar rooted trees, including RK4 order four, Dormand-Prince order five, and Gauss-Legendre order six.

informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.satisf: Reduces order-p Runge-Kutta conditions to a finite catalogue check over rooted trees.
informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.rk4_or: Certifies that classical RK4 satisfies all planar rooted-tree order conditions through order four.
informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.rk4_no: Shows that RK4 fails a fifth-order condition, pinning its order exactly.
informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.orderC: Proves order conditions are invariant under permutations of a node's children.
informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.dp_ord: Certifies the Dormand-Prince RK45 fifth-order tableau through order five.
informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.gauss_: Certifies the Gauss-Legendre three-stage tableau through order four over Q(sqrt(15)).
Certifies the denominator-cleared (360-scaled) integer Z(sqrt(15)) Gauss-Legendre tableau through order six, the scaled certificate feeding the homogeneity bridge.
Certifies the Gauss-Legendre s=3 tableau through order six over Q(sqrt(15)), via the formalized homogeneity bridge from the 360-scaled integer certificate.

records.title: The Rupert Problem for convex polyhedra
records.abstract: Formalizes the Rupert property for the cube, the regular tetrahedron, and the triakis tetrahedron, exhibiting for each an explicit straight-through hole admitting a congruent copy.

informal.Cube.rupert: Proves that the cube has the Rupert property.
informal.Tetrahedron.rupert: Proves that the regular tetrahedron has the Rupert property.
informal.TriakisTetrahedron.rupert: Proves that the triakis tetrahedron has the Rupert property.

records.title: Sabidussi's compatibility conjecture for Eulerian multigraphs
records.abstract: Formalizes Sabidussi's compatibility conjecture for finite labelled endpoint multigraphs with loops and parallel edges, where a loop contributes two half-edge incidences to the degree of its vertex. Given an Euler tour and minimum degree at least four, the main theorem constructs a partition of all edges into nonempty, edge-connected, 2-regular ordinary circuits such that consecutive edges of the Euler tour never lie in the same circuit. The proof runs a four-colour (F_2^2) algebra over the cyclic transition word, uses an odd balancing parity lemma to choose compatible local frames, and transports the resulting colouring back to a compatible ordinary circuit decomposition.

informal.Sabidussi.LoopMultigraph.loop_sabidussi_: For any finite endpoint multigraph with an Euler tour and minimum degree at least four, the edges partition into ordinary, nonempty, connected, 2-regular circuits that are compatible with the tour: no circuit contains two consecutive tour edges.
The same compatibility statement phrased with the intrinsic even-edge-set circuit decomposition, from which the ordinary-circuit form is derived.

records.title: Every Pisot number is a two-sided limit of Salem numbers
records.abstract: Proves Salem’s two-sided approximation theorem for Pisot numbers, preserving both the polynomial reciprocal-family construction and the exceptional quadratic-unit construction.

informal.SalemTheorem.salem_theorem: Every Pisot number is approached by Salem numbers from both below and above.
informal.SalemTheorem.salem_construction_two_side: For the nondegenerate Pisot polynomial pattern, reciprocal-family polynomials have Salem roots arbitrarily near the Pisot root from either side.
informal.SalemTheorem.salem_quadratic_unit: The quadratic-unit family supplies Salem roots approaching each reciprocal quadratic Pisot unit from either side.

records.title: Moreira's version of Sard's theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes Moreira's strengthening of Sard's theorem, bounding the Hausdorff dimension of critical-value images of C^{k+alpha} maps.

informal.hausdorffMeasure_sardMoreiraBound_image_: Proves Hausdorff-measure nullity for images of points where the derivative rank is bounded by p, at Moreira's Sard bound.
informal.dimH_image_le_sardMoreiraBound_of_finran: Converts the measure-null theorem into the headline Hausdorff-dimension upper bound for critical-value images.

records.title: Jordan–Schönflies theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the Jordan curve theorem and the extension of every homeomorphism between Jordan curves to a plane homeomorphism.

informal.Schoenflies.jordan_schoenflies_of_homeom: Every homeomorphism between two Jordan curves in the plane extends to a self-homeomorphism of the plane.
informal.Schoenflies.jordan_schoenflies: A homeomorphism between Jordan curves extends to a global homeomorphism agreeing with it on the source curve.
informal.Schoenflies.forall_isSeparating_of_isJor: Every Jordan curve separates the plane into an inside and an outside region.

records.title: Selberg Sieve
records.abstract: Formalizes the Selberg sieve with applications to prime-counting bounds and a Brun-Titchmarsh-style estimate.

informal.fundamental_theorem_simple: Proves the simple Selberg sieve upper-bound theorem.
informal.primeCounting_isBigO_atTop: Derives the asymptotic prime-counting upper bound.
informal.primeCounting_le_mul: Gives an eventual explicit constant upper bound for the prime-counting function.
informal.primesBetween_le: Bounds the number of primes in an interval using the sieve estimate.

records.title: Genus-Zero Pairings and Catalan Numbers
records.abstract: Formalizes the finite combinatorics behind the genus-zero term of the Wigner semicircle law: a pairing of Fin (2n), viewed as a fixed-point-free involution, has genus zero (total cycle count of the rotation product maximal) exactly when it is noncrossing, and these genus-zero pairings are counted by the Catalan number Cₙ. The Catalan recurrence is obtained from an explicit equivalence decomposing a noncrossing pairing by the partner of vertex 0 into independent inside and outside pairings.

informal.card_noncrossingPairing_eq_catalan: The number of noncrossing pairings on 2n points equals the Catalan number catalan n.
informal.Pairing.genus_zero_count: The number of genus-zero pairings of Fin (2n) equals the Catalan number catalan n.
informal.Pairing.genus_zero_iff_noncrossing: A pairing has genus zero if and only if it is noncrossing.

records.title: Wigner Semicircle Distribution
records.abstract: Defines the real Wigner semicircle distribution, its normalized density, affine transformations, and finite-moment integrability.

informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.semicirclePDFReal: Defines the real-valued density of the semicircle distribution with mean μ and variance v.
informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.semicirclePDF: Defines the ℝ≥0∞-valued density of the semicircle distribution.
informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.integral_semicirc: Proves that the real-valued semicircle density integrates to one for nonzero variance.
informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.semicircleReal: Defines the semicircle measure on ℝ, equal to a Dirac mass when the variance is zero.
informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.semicircleReal_ma: Shows that translating a semicircle measure translates its mean parameter.
Shows that scaling by a nonzero constant scales the mean and variance parameters.
informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.memLp_id_semicirc: Shows that the identity has all finite Lp moments under a semicircle distribution.

records.title: Sendov's conjecture and the Phelps–Rodriguez conjecture
records.abstract: Proves Sendov's conjecture in full generality: if every zero of a complex polynomial of degree at least two lies in the closed unit disk, then every zero has a critical point within distance one. Also proves the Phelps–Rodriguez strengthening, with strict inequality unless the zero lies on the unit circle and the polynomial is a scalar multiple of z^n - a^n, and recovers Rubinstein's boundary theorem. Formalizes Tao's digestion of Lech Mazur's proof: the problem is reduced to a numerical inequality in the degree and one real parameter, settled by exact rational Bernstein certificates for degrees up to one hundred and by an analytic large-degree reduction beyond. Includes the top case of Maclaurin's inequality and multiset AM–GM, a defect inequality on the closed unit disk, a sharp bound on log(sinh h / h), kernel-checked polynomial certificate infrastructure, and a packed-exponentiation bridge for exact moment integrals.

informal.Sendov.sendov: For every natural number n at least two and every complex polynomial p of degree n all of whose roots have norm at most one, every root a of p admits a root of the derivative of p within distance at most one of a.
informal.Sendov.phelps_rodriguez: Under the same hypotheses, either some root of the derivative lies at distance strictly less than one from a, or a has norm one and p equals a nonzero scalar multiple of X^n - a^n.
informal.SendovConjecture.sendov: The same statement in the Mathlib-only form of the upstream statement of record: for every complex polynomial p of degree at least two such that every complex w with p(w) = 0 has norm at most one, every zero a of p admits a root of the derivative within distance at most one of a.
informal.Sendov.rubinstein_one: If a polynomial of degree n at least two with all roots in the closed unit disk vanishes at one, then either its derivative has a root within distance strictly less than one of the point one, or the polynomial equals its leading coefficient times X^n - 1.
informal.Sendov.stat_lt_one: For every degree n at least five and every real parameter alpha between zero and seventeen satisfying the feasibility constraint c^2 ≤ A, the quantity R n alpha of the blog post's equation stat is strictly less than one.
informal.Multiset.esymm_card_pred_le: For a nonempty multiset of nonnegative reals of cardinality m, the (m-1)-st elementary symmetric function is at most m times the (m-1)-st power of the mean.
informal.Multiset.prod_le_mean_pow: The product of a multiset of nonnegative reals is at most the mean raised to the cardinality.
informal.Sendov.defect: For a multiset of complex numbers in the closed unit disk, the product of the norms times the sum of the norms of 1/z minus the conjugate of z is at most one minus the square of that product.
informal.Sendov.log_sinh_div_le: For every positive real h, the logarithm of sinh h divided by h is at most the square root of h^2 + 9 minus three.
informal.Sendov.pev_pos_of_bern: If the Bernstein expansion of an integer coefficient list on an interval from zero to p/q equals p^d times a polynomial P and every Bernstein coefficient is positive, then P is positive on that interval.

records.title: Sensitivity Conjecture: sqrt(deg) <= sensitivity
records.abstract: Formalizes the quantitative Nisan-Szegedy/Huang sensitivity theorem for Boolean functions.

informal.LeanPoolSensitivity.sensitivity_ge_sqrt_: Proves that the square root of multilinear degree is bounded above by sensitivity.
informal.LeanPoolSensitivity.degree_le_sensitivit: Derives the degree bound by the square of sensitivity.

records.title: Serre's mass formula for totally ramified local-field extensions
records.abstract: Proves both of Serre's mass formulas for totally ramified separable extensions of a nonarchimedean local field of any positive degree, together with the discriminant bound, tame-ramification criterion, finiteness dichotomy, convergence, and automorphism-weighted orbit count. The proof develops Eisenstein monogenicity, quantitative Newton-Hensel lifting, local constancy of root counts, and Haar measures of lattices over discrete valuation rings.

informal.MassFormula.tsum_one_div_q_pow_c: For every nonarchimedean local field K with residue-field cardinality q and every positive integer n, the sum of q^(-c(L)) over the totally ramified degree-n subextensions L of a separable closure of K is n, where c(L) is the discriminant exponent minus n plus one.
informal.MassFormula.tsum_one_div_w_mul_q_pow_c: For every nonarchimedean local field K, positive n, and set of representatives of K-isomorphism classes of totally ramified separable degree-n extensions, the sum of 1/(|Aut_K(L)| q^c(L)) is one.
informal.MassFormula.sigma_infinite_iff: For positive n, the set of totally ramified separable degree-n subextensions is infinite exactly when K and its residue field have the same characteristic p and p divides n.
informal.MassFormula.sub_one_le_d: For positive n, the discriminant exponent of a totally ramified degree-n extension is at least n-1.
informal.MassFormula.c_eq_zero_iff: For positive n and a totally ramified degree-n extension, the wild discriminant exponent vanishes exactly when the residue characteristic does not divide n.
informal.MassFormula.summable_one_div_q_pow_c: For positive n, the real-valued series of the unweighted mass terms is summable.
informal.MassFormula.ncard_isomorphic_mul_w: For a nonarchimedean local field K and a totally ramified separable extension L of positive degree n, the number of K-isomorphic copies of L inside a separable closure, multiplied by |Aut_K(L)|, is n.

records.title: The Kunen inconsistency theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes elementary embeddings of models of ZF set theory and proves the Kunen inconsistency theorem, that there is no nontrivial elementary embedding of the set-theoretic universe into itself.

informal.SetTheory.kunen_inconsistency_V: Proves the Kunen inconsistency theorem, that every elementary embedding of the von Neumann universe V into itself is the identity.
informal.SetTheory.kunen_inconsistency_vonNeumann: Proves the Kunen inconsistency theorem for von Neumann levels V_μ at a successor-limit ordinal, computing the supremum of the critical-point iterates.
informal.SetTheory.crit: Defines the critical point of a nontrivial elementary embedding as the least ordinal it moves.
informal.NontrivialElementaryEmbedding: Defines a nontrivial elementary embedding of a model of ZF into itself.

records.title: Shannon Entropy Characterization
records.abstract: Formalizes Shannon's finite-alphabet characterization theorem for entropy from the 1948 paper.

informal.LeanPool.Shannon1948Formalization.entrop: Proves that any finite-alphabet uncertainty functional satisfying Shannon's conditions equals natural-log entropy up to a positive scale.
Restates the characterization for any logarithm base greater than one.
Proves the converse, showing that Shannon entropy satisfies the formal condition bundle.
informal.LeanPool.Shannon1948Formalization.chain_: Proves the finite joint-entropy chain rule.
informal.LeanPool.Shannon1948Formalization.entrop: Proves subadditivity of finite joint entropy.

records.title: Quadratic-order prime classification
records.abstract: Formalizes foundational algebra for quadratic orders associated to discriminants, including their power basis, norm and discriminant identities, odd-prime splitting/ramification/inertness criteria via Legendre symbols, and root-counting results for quadratic congruences modulo odd prime powers.

informal.QuadraticOrder.prime_inert_iff: Proves that for an odd rational prime p and a valid discriminant d, the ideal (p) is maximal in the quadratic order O_d exactly when the Legendre symbol (d/p) is -1.
informal.QuadraticOrder.prime_ramified_iff: Proves that for an odd rational prime p and a valid discriminant d, the ideal (p) is not radical in O_d exactly when p divides d.
informal.QuadraticOrder.prime_split_iff: Proves that for an odd rational prime p and a valid discriminant d, the ideal (p) is radical but not maximal exactly when the Legendre symbol (d/p) is 1.
informal.QuadraticOrder.cardSqrts_prime_pow_copri: Counts roots of x^2 = c modulo p^n for odd prime p and p not dividing c, giving two roots when the Legendre symbol is 1 and none otherwise.
informal.QuadraticOrder.cardSqrts_prime_pow_even_: Counts roots of x^2 = p^(2r) u modulo p^n for odd prime p, p not dividing u, and 2r < n, reducing to the coprime case and multiplying by p^r.
informal.QuadraticOrder.tau_sub_tauConj_sq_of_val: Proves the discriminant identity (tau - tauConj)^2 = d for valid quadratic-order discriminants d congruent to 0 or 1 modulo 4.

records.title: Spectral positivity
records.abstract: Perron-Frobenius theory, Jentzsch's theorem, and matrix/operator positivity in Lean 4. At the matrix level it proves that nonnegative matrices have nonnegative powers, the Metzler decomposition and positivity of the matrix exponential of a Metzler matrix, M-matrix inverse positivity, and the Perron-Frobenius theorem for irreducible nonnegative matrices (a positive dominant eigenvalue with a strictly positive eigenvector). At the operator level it proves Jentzsch's theorem for compact self-adjoint positivity-improving operators on L2 — a simple, strictly positive ground state with a spectral gap — together with a kernel positivity criterion.

informal.allpos_has_pos_eigenvec: A matrix with all strictly positive entries has a positive eigenvalue with a strictly positive eigenvector (Perron-Frobenius for positive matrices, via the Collatz-Wielandt characterization).
informal.perron_frobenius: An irreducible (primitive) nonnegative matrix has a positive eigenvalue with a strictly positive eigenvector.
informal.ground_state_strictly_positive: The ground eigenfunction of a compact self-adjoint positivity-improving operator on L2 is strictly positive almost everywhere (Jentzsch).
informal.SpectralPositivity.Matrix.MMatrix.invers: The inverse of a nonsingular irreducible M-matrix is entrywise strictly positive.

records.title: Sharp asymptotic upper bounds for sphere packing
records.abstract: Formalizes the sharp high-dimensional asymptotics of the unrestricted Cohn--Elkies linear program and bridges them to sphere-packing density. The development constructs radial test functions through Mellin, saddle-point, and harmonic analysis, proves radialization preserves the unrestricted optimum, and certifies the exact natural- and base-two exponential rates.

informal.PackingBounds.FullMain.exact_limit: The d-th root of the unrestricted Cohn--Elkies linear-program bound converges to the sharp constant sqrt(e / (2 pi)).
