informal.PackingBounds.FullMain.exact_binary_expo: The base-two logarithm of the unrestricted linear-program bound, divided by dimension, converges to -1/2 log_2(2 pi / e).
informal.PackingBounds.PackingBridge.sphere_packi: There is a vanishing error sequence such that, in every positive dimension, sphere-packing density is at most (sqrt(e / (2 pi)) plus that error) to the dimension.
informal.PackingBounds.sharpFullCohnElkiesManuscr: Packages the complete sharp asymptotic conclusions for the unrestricted program, including quotient-root, natural-logarithmic, and base-two limits, vanishing-error formulas, a universal bound for all admissible functions, and a certified decimal exponent interval.

records.title: Stafford 3.8
records.abstract: Lean formalization of Stafford's Conjecture 3.8 for every characteristic-zero field and every Weyl-algebra rank, proving that each nonzero d admits F, R, and S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S. The development also proves an exact Bernstein-degree fixed-source strengthening and derived localization, adjoint, and evolutionary results.

informal.Stafford38.universalStatement: For every characteristic-zero field, every Weyl algebra rank, and every nonzero d, there are F, R, S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S.
informal.Stafford38.universalFixedSourceStatement: The stated fixed-source strengthening holds with its exact Bernstein-degree bound.

records.title: Verified Stallings folding for finitely generated subgroups of F2
records.abstract: Constructs a finite inverse automaton recognizing the subgroup generated by any finite list of signed words in the rank-two free group. Proves exact subgroup preservation and correctness of canonical reduced-word membership testing. Reusable infrastructure includes inverse-automaton walks, reduction-compatible traversal, finite fold congruences, coset potentials, flower graphs, and basis roses. Folding uses exhaustive finite search over Boolean relations; no complexity bound, core pruning, subgroup basis, intersection, or index algorithm is claimed.

informal.Stallings.folded_recognizer_exists: For every finite list S of signed words on two generators, there exist a finite type of states, a base state, and a partial transition table with inverse-labelled reverse edges, such that traversing the canonical reduced word of any g in FreeGroup (Fin 2) returns to the base exactly when g lies in the subgroup generated by the word values in S. The witness is the computed flower-graph fold.
informal.Stallings.foldWords_loopSubgroup_eq_gene: For every finite input list of signed words in the rank-two free group, the based-loop subgroup of the computed folded flower graph equals the subgroup generated by the input words.
informal.Stallings.foldedMembershipTest_eq_true_i: For any finite generating list S and any rank-two free-group element g, the executable folded-automaton test returns true if and only if g belongs to the subgroup generated by S. There is no efficiency guarantee for constructing the automaton.

records.title: Monotonicity Formula for Stationary Harmonic Maps
records.abstract: Formalizes the monotonicity formula for stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` maps with Euclidean target. The proof is target independent: it uses only the displayed weak gradient and a vanishing domain first variation, so no target-manifold structure enters the argument. From a bundled stationary Sobolev witness `StationaryW12LocMap u Omega` it proves, for `0 < s <= r < R0`, that the normalized energy `Theta(Du, a, rho) = rho^(2-n) * integral over B(a, rho) of |Du|^2` is monotone: `weakTheta Du a s <= weakTheta Du a r`, together with the exact increment formula `weakTheta Du a r - weakTheta Du a s = weakMonotonicityRhs Du a s r`. The Sobolev layer is project-defined from Mathlib's `MemLp`, weak-derivative identities, Bochner integration, and Euclidean measure theory, following the De Giorgi-Nash-Moser engineering choice; the internal proof routes through a radial vector-field first variation, a coarea/Radon-Nikodym radius representation, smooth radial cutoffs, and an absolute-continuity boundary step.

informal.LeanStationaryHarmonicMaps.StationaryHar: The public input package: a domain-variation stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` Sobolev map bundling a chosen weak gradient (`W12LocMapWitness`) with the vanishing domain first-variation identity. This is the object users construct to invoke the monotonicity theorem.

Witness-style monotonicity: from a stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` map package, the normalized weak energy `weakTheta` is monotone in the radius, `weakTheta Du a s <= weakTheta Du a r` for `0 < s <= r < R0`.

Witness-style monotonicity formula: the increment of `weakTheta` equals the nonnegative annular radial-energy term, `weakTheta Du a r - weakTheta Du a s = weakMonotonicityRhs Du a s r` for `0 < s < r < R0`.

Componentwise convenience wrapper: the same monotonicity inequality stated directly from the local `L^2`, measurability, weak-gradient, and first-variation hypotheses, without first constructing the witness package.

records.title: Split, cograph and threshold graph structures
records.abstract: Connects split partitions, cotrees and threshold creation sequences on Mathlib SimpleGraph. Proves the finite forbidden-induced-subgraph characterizations, split iff chordal and co-chordal, and completeness of cotrees and creation sequences. Supplies certificate-preserving operations, twins and nonempty union/join decompositions for cographs, maximum-clique split partitions, and induced/isomorphic transport of existing chordal elimination orders and clique trees. Classical graph theory is formalized; no new mathematical theorem, canonical certificate or recognition-time bound is claimed.

informal.SimpleGraph.isSplit_iff_forbidden_induce: A finite graph is split iff it contains no induced 2K2, C4 or C5.
informal.SimpleGraph.isSplit_iff_isChordal_and_co: A finite graph is split iff both it and its complement are chordal.
informal.SimpleGraph.isCograph_iff_nonempty_cotre: A finite graph is P4-free iff it is isomorphic to the graph of a cotree, whose constructors are empty, singleton, disjoint union and join.
informal.SimpleGraph.isThreshold_iff_isSplit_and_: A graph has a split partition with nested independent-side neighbourhoods iff it is both split and P4-free. No finiteness is required.
informal.SimpleGraph.isThreshold_iff_forbidden_in: A finite graph is threshold iff it contains no induced 2K2, C4 or P4.
informal.SimpleGraph.isThreshold_iff_nonempty_cre: A finite graph is threshold iff it is isomorphic to a graph constructed from the empty graph by successively adding an isolated or universal vertex.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsCograph.exists_twins: A finite cograph with at least two vertices has two distinct vertices with identical adjacency outside their pair, whether adjacent or not.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsCograph.exists_union_root: A finite cograph that is not preconnected admits a cotree representation with a union root and two nonempty children. This is an existence claim, not a claim about every unreduced cotree.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsCograph.exists_join_root: A preconnected finite cograph with at least two vertices admits a cotree representation with a join root and two nonempty children.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsSplit.exists_partition_wit: Every finite split graph admits a split partition whose clique part has maximum cardinality. Such a partition need not be unique.

records.title: The optimal exponent relating sumsets and difference sets
records.abstract: For a finite integer set A with at least two elements, proves that C(A) = log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A-A|/|A|) is strictly below 2, while explicit finite sets have exponents tending to 2. Thus 2 is the supremum and is never attained. Also gives an explicit witness within 10^(-999) of 2. This imports the upstream base-39 row-and-column variant, not the paper's base-12 automaton construction or its quantitative cardinality estimates. Supporting infrastructure includes injective digit expansions and the strict Pluennecke-Petridis equality argument for finite integer sets.

informal.SumDifferenceExponent.growthExponent_lt_: For every finite set A of integers with at least two elements, log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A-A|/|A|) is strictly less than 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.tendsto_growthExpo: The growth exponents of the explicit finite integer sets approximatingSet l converge to 2 as l tends to infinity; these sets have at least two elements whenever l is positive.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.isLUB_admissibleEx: The number 2 is the least upper bound of the growth exponents of all finite integer sets with at least two elements.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.sSup_admissibleExp: The supremum of the growth exponents of all finite integer sets with at least two elements equals 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.supremum_not_attai: No finite integer set with at least two elements has growth exponent equal to 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.quantitative_examp: The explicitly defined finite integer set quantitativeSet has growth exponent strictly between 2 - 10^(-999) and 2.

records.title: Sums of Three Squares
records.abstract: Formalizes a blueprint step in the three-squares theorem using quadratic forms and geometry of numbers.

informal.LeanPool.SumsThreeSquares.blueprint_case: Proves the mod-8-equals-3 blueprint case for the three-squares theorem.

records.title: Sundog certificates
records.abstract: A referee-free, axiom-clean Lean development of coding-theory certificates: syndrome decoding soundness and lossiness bounds for GF(2) parity-check schemes (with a Reed–Solomon evaluation-dual variant), and a fully machine-checked correctness proof of the Karp reduction chain 3SAT ≤ 3DM ≤ X3C ≤ bounded-weight syndrome decoding. Only the logical iff of each reduction is formalized; polynomial-time bounds, NP classes, and Cook–Levin are unformalized external inputs, so NP-hardness of decoding is conditional on those standard facts.

informal.Sundog.SATReductionMain.sat_iff_decodes: The end-to-end reduction correctness: a formula is satisfiable iff its image under the composed 3SAT-to-decoding reduction is a yes-instance of bounded-weight syndrome decoding.
informal.Sundog.MatchingNPHard.threeDM_iff_X3C: The 3-dimensional matching instance has a perfect matching iff the reduced exact-cover-by-3-sets instance has an exact cover, both directions machine-checked.
informal.Sundog.Certificate.accept_sound: Soundness of the cheap syndrome-decoding verifier when it accepts: an exhibited light same-syndrome witness certifies the body is safe within the decoding radius.
informal.Sundog.Certificate.reject_sound: Soundness of the verifier when it rejects: a sound column-weight lower bound on the minimum same-syndrome weight rules out every light witness, so the body is genuinely unsafe.

records.title: Synthetic Euclidean geometry: Euclid's Elements Book I
records.abstract: Formalizes Book I of Euclid's Elements via an axiomatic synthetic-geometry system (incidence, betweenness, congruence, and area), culminating in the Pythagorean theorem and its converse.

informal.SyntheticEuclid4.IncidenceGeometry: The axiomatic class of synthetic Euclidean geometry, bundling points, lines, circles, and the incidence, betweenness, congruence, and area primitives with Euclid's axioms.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.square_of_len: Constructs a square on a given segment off a given line.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras_construct: Constructs the three squares and parallelograms on the sides of a triangle used in the proof of the Pythagorean theorem.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras: Euclid I.47, the Pythagorean theorem, that the square on the hypotenuse of a right triangle equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras_converse: Euclid I.48, the converse of the Pythagorean theorem, that a triangle whose square areas satisfy the Pythagorean relation has a right angle.

records.title: The Three-Gap (Steinhaus) Theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the three-gap (Steinhaus, three-distance) theorem: for every real `a` and every `N`, the `N`-point orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` partitions `[0,1)` into gaps taking at most three distinct lengths, and when exactly three occur the largest is the sum of the other two. The proof works in `[0,1)` via `Int.fract` (not `AddCircle`) through the two first-return times `η⁺` and `η⁻`, and is uniform in the rotation number, covering rational and irrational `a` with no case split.

informal.SteinhausThreeGap.three_gap_card_le_thre: For every real `a` and natural `N`, the gaps of the orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` take at most three distinct lengths.
informal.SteinhausThreeGap.three_gap_lengths_eq: When the gaps take exactly three distinct lengths, those lengths are precisely the two first returns `η⁺`, `η⁻`, and their sum `η⁺ + η⁻`; in particular the largest gap is the sum of the other two.

records.title: Turán's theorem (the "Book" weighting proof)
records.abstract: Formalizes the weighting/optimization proof of Turán's theorem from Proofs from THE BOOK, bounding the number of edges of a p-clique-free simple graph by (1/2)(1 - 1/(p-1)) n².

informal.Turan3.turans: Turán's theorem — a p-clique-free simple graph on n vertices has at most (1/2)(1 - 1/(p-1)) n² edges.
informal.Turan3.finale_bound: For any weight distribution on a p-clique-free graph, the total edge weight is at most ((p-1)(p-2)/2)·(1/(p-1))², the bound used to derive the edge count.
informal.Turan3.Better_forms_clique: Starting from any weight function, the minimal-support weight-non-decreasing improvement has support that forms a clique.
informal.Turan3.Enhance_total_weight_stricinc: Equalizing weights between a maximum- and minimum-weight vertex in the clique support strictly increases the total edge weight.

records.title: Tutte’s path theorem for matroids
records.abstract: Proves the modular-cut path theorem for finite matroids, with reusable rank-partition, hyperplane-separation, relative-complement, indecomposable-cover, and diamond constructions.

informal.TutteFormalization.path_theorem: In a finite connected matroid, any two hyperplanes containing a proper indecomposable flat and lying outside a modular cut are joined by a finite Tutte path all of whose vertices contain that flat and avoid the cut. Consecutive vertices are distinct hyperplanes with indecomposable corank-two intersection; repeated nonconsecutive vertices are permitted.
informal.TutteFormalization.path_theorem_of_indec: In any finite matroid, two hyperplanes containing an indecomposable flat F and lying outside a modular cut are joined by a Tutte path whose vertices contain F and avoid the cut. This strengthens the cited path theorem by requiring only connectedness of the contraction by F; properness of F follows from containment in an endpoint hyperplane.
informal.TutteFormalization.exists_indecomposable: If an indecomposable flat S and a flat U span the ground, every indecomposable flat T contained in both extends inside S to an indecomposable flat R spanning the ground with U, with corank R equal to rank U minus rank T.
informal.TutteFormalization.exists_relative_compl: For nested flats T contained in S, there is a flat U containing T whose intersection with S is T, whose join with S is the ground, and whose corank equals rank S minus rank T.

records.title: Ulm's theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups
records.abstract: Formalizes Ulm's classification theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups in arbitrary Lean universes. The development constructs the transfinite Ulm filtration and invariants, proves their invariance under additive equivalence, establishes Kaplansky's one-generator extension lemma, and completes the countable back-and-forth classification. A finite-group regression distinguishes Z/4 x Z/4 from Z/2 x Z/8 at the zeroth Ulm invariant.

informal.UlmsTheorem.ulm_theorem: For any prime p and any two countable reduced abelian p-groups in the same arbitrary Lean universe, the groups are additively isomorphic if and only if all of their classical Ulm invariants, indexed by universe-zero ordinals, agree.
informal.UlmsTheorem.iso_of_ulm_invariants: Equal Ulm invariants at every universe-zero ordinal imply an additive equivalence between countable reduced abelian p-groups, via finite height-preserving partial isomorphisms and a back-and-forth limit.
informal.UlmsTheorem.ulmInvariant_iso_invariant: An additive equivalence preserves every classical Ulm invariant.
informal.UlmsTheorem.UlmDifferentialRegression.no: The groups Z/4 x Z/4 and Z/2 x Z/8 are not additively isomorphic; the proof exercises the classification theorem and independently detects their different zeroth Ulm invariants.

records.title: Unconditional Schauder Bases
records.abstract: Develops an API for Schauder bases and unconditional Schauder bases of complete normed spaces, including ordered partial-sum convergence, rearrangement criteria for unconditionality, and an arbitrary-index variant built on unconditional summability, then proves a finite sign criterion: a family with dense closed span, nonzero vectors, and a uniform finite sign bound is the basis of an unconditional Schauder basis.

informal.UnconditionalCriterion.exists_unconditio: Finite sign criterion for sequences: if `x : ℕ → E` has dense closed linear span, every `x n` is nonzero, and finite sign changes are uniformly bounded by `C`, then `x` is the basis sequence of an unconditional Schauder basis.

Abstract-index form of the finite sign criterion: under the same dense span, nonzero, and uniform finite sign bound hypotheses for an arbitrarily indexed family, there is an abstractly indexed unconditional Schauder basis whose basis family is exactly `x`.

records.title: Virasoro Project
records.abstract: Formalizes the Virasoro algebra, its Witt-algebra central extension, Verma modules, and the basic bosonic Sugawara construction.

informal.VirasoroProject.VirasoroAlgebra: Defines the Virasoro algebra as a one-dimensional central extension of the Witt algebra.
informal.VirasoroProject.sugawaraRepresentation: Constructs the basic bosonic Sugawara representation of the Virasoro algebra from locally truncated Heisenberg actions.

records.title: Viscosity solutions, Aleksandrov differentiability and harmonic Dirichlet problems
records.abstract: Develops second-order semijets, smooth test-function equivalence, Jensen contact sets, convex Aleksandrov differentiability, the quadratic-penalty Ishii lemma and compact-domain comparison for degenerate elliptic equations. Perron assembly retains explicit comparison, barrier and bumping assumptions; these are discharged for classical harmonic Dirichlet existence on bounded open domains satisfying a uniform exterior sphere condition.

informal.AleksandrovDifferentiability.convexAleks: A convex real-valued function on an open subset of any finite-dimensional real inner product space is second-order differentiable at Lebesgue-almost every point.
informal.ViscositySolns.JensenContactSetPositiveM: Under the localized semiconvexity and strict-contact hypotheses, the contact set arising from sufficiently small linear perturbations has positive Lebesgue measure.
informal.ViscositySolns.QuadraticPenaltyIshiiLemm: For an upper semicontinuous function and a lower semicontinuous function on locally compact subsets of real coordinate space, doubled-variable maxima with the quadratic penalty yield closed semijets satisfying the Ishii block-matrix bounds.
informal.ViscositySolns.comparison_of_constantShi: A viscosity subsolution lies below a supersolution on a nonempty locally compact domain with compact closure, assuming boundary comparison, semicontinuity on the closure, properness, operator continuity, the Ishii structural condition and uniform scalar decrease.
informal.ViscositySolns.viscositySubsolution_iff_: On an open domain, semijet and smooth C² test-function formulations of viscosity subsolutions agree for Hessian-continuous, symmetric-part-invariant operators.
informal.ViscositySolns.dirichlet_harmonic_modulu: On a bounded open subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space with a uniform exterior sphere condition, Lipschitz data on its closure admit a continuous extension that agrees on the boundary and is C² and harmonic in the domain, with a boundary modulus depending only on the domain and Lipschitz constant.

records.title: Vizing's theorem and equitable edge colourings
records.abstract: Proves the maximum-degree-plus-one edge-colouring bound for finite simple graphs by fans and Kempe exchanges. A separate component-swapping argument equitably rebalances any finite proper edge colouring on its original palette. Together they give equitable proper edge colourings on any palette of at least maximum degree plus one colours, with every class bounded by the ceiling of the average class size. Extracted from the published Paper IV formalization; these are classical colouring results, not a claim to new mathematics or to the paper's clique-partition bound.

informal.LeanPool.Vizing.lineGraph_colorable: The line graph of a finite simple graph G is colourable with maximum degree of G plus one colours.
informal.SimpleGraph.lineGraph_chromaticNumber_le: The chromatic number of the line graph of a finite simple graph G is at most maximum degree of G plus one.
informal.LeanPool.Vizing.Equitable.exists_equitab: Every proper edge colouring of a finite simple graph with a finite palette admits a proper recolouring on the same palette in which any two colour classes differ in size by at most one.
informal.LeanPool.Vizing.exists_equitable_edge_co: For every finite simple graph G and natural c at least maximum degree of G plus one, there is an equitable proper edge colouring with c colours; each colour class has at most ceiling(|E(G)|/c) edges.

records.title: Mean-field derivation and well-posedness of the Vlasov equation
records.abstract: Formalizes the mean-field limit, Dobrushin stability, and forward-in-time well-posedness for the Vlasov equation via Wasserstein-1 optimal transport.

informal.Vlasov.vlasovWellPosedness: Forward-in-time existence of a Lagrangian solution to the Vlasov equation on any finite horizon, for interaction forces that are Lipschitz gradients of an even pair potential (class AssW) — with no smallness restriction on the Lipschitz constant.
informal.Vlasov.dobrushin: A Wasserstein-1 form of Dobrushin's 1979 stability estimate (the original uses a truncated metric) - two Lagrangian Vlasov solutions with finite first moments at every time separate at most at an exponential Gronwall rate.
informal.Vlasov.meanFieldLimit: Conditional mean-field limit - given Wasserstein-1 convergence of the initial empirical data and a uniform Dobrushin stability estimate for the empirical curves, the N-particle empirical measures converge to the Vlasov solution uniformly on any finite horizon.
informal.Vlasov.weak_isLagrangianVlasovSolutionOn: On a time window with L * T^2 < 1, a weak solution with the standing regularity (even C^2 pair potential AssW2, finite first moments, narrow continuity, time-continuity of the convolution force at each point, continuity of the convolution-derivative field, and a uniform spatial first-moment bound on the window) is Lagrangian - the pushforward of its initial datum along the characteristic flow.

records.title: The Wallace problem in ZFC
records.abstract: Formalizes in ZFC a Hausdorff countably compact group topology without nontrivial convergent sequences on every torsion-free Abelian group of cardinality continuum. It specializes the construction to the rational direct sum and the additive real group, and derives a commutative Tychonoff countably compact cancellative semigroup that is not a group.

informal.Wallace.torsionFreeAbelianGroup_mainTheo: Every torsion-free Abelian group of cardinality continuum admits a Hausdorff countably compact group topology with no nontrivial convergent sequences.
informal.Wallace.continuumRationalGroup_and_real_: Both the continuum-indexed rational direct sum and the additive group of real numbers admit such Hausdorff countably compact group topologies without nontrivial convergent sequences.
informal.Wallace.commutativeTychonoffWallaceCount: There exists a commutative Tychonoff countably compact topological semigroup with two-sided cancellation which is not a group.

records.title: Whitehead's theorem for CW-complexes
records.abstract: Formalizes Whitehead's theorem — a continuous map between CW-complexes that induces isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence — including the supporting theory of CW-complexes, relative homotopy groups, the homotopy extension property, and compression of maps.

informal.WhiteheadTheorem: Proves that a continuous map between CW-complexes inducing isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence.

records.title: Irrationality of the Riemann zeta function at five
records.abstract: Proves that Mathlib's Riemann zeta function at five is an irrational real number, following Aabir Fauzan's September 2026 preprint. Constructs integer polynomials of degree 37n with positive values at zeta(5) that decay exponentially in n squared. Includes a general integer-polynomial irrationality criterion, Hankel determinant and moment-integral identities, logarithmic-energy estimates, prime-adic integrality bounds, and kernel-checked rational certificates. The formalization uses a different normalizer and a positive decay constant in place of the paper's specific constant 139/5. Reuses the prime number theorem infrastructure already in the MooreBound project.

informal.Zeta5Irrational.irrational_five: There exists an irrational real number x whose complex coercion equals Mathlib's Riemann zeta function evaluated at five.
informal.Zeta5Irrational.main_estimate: There is a positive real c such that, for all sufficiently large n, an integer polynomial Q of degree 37n is a positive rational multiple of the constructed determinant polynomial and satisfies 0 < Q(zeta(5)) < exp(-c*n^2).
informal.Zeta5Irrational.irrational_of_eventually: A real xi is irrational if, eventually, integer polynomials of degree at most d(n) have positive values at xi bounded by epsilon(n), and b^d(n)*epsilon(n) tends to zero for every positive natural b.

records.title: Thakur's hypotheses on power sums of F_q[t]
records.abstract: Formalizes four components of Thakur's hypotheses on power sums over finite polynomial rings, including uniqueness and monotonicity results for the carry-free digit optimization problems and the Laurent-series expansion of finite-field power sums.

informal.ZetaH123.H1.main_theorem: Proves uniqueness of the admissible base-q decomposition maximizing the H1 power-sum weight functional.
informal.ZetaH123.H2.main: Proves the H2 unique-minimizer statement for the recursive digit/carry-free optimization problem defining the values s_d(k).
informal.ZetaH123.H3.main_theorem: Proves the H3 monotonicity statement that s_d(k) is strictly less than s_d(k+1) when p does not divide k.
informal.ZetaH123.Lem41.main: Proves the Lemma 4.1 Laurent-series expansion for S_d(k), with nonzero coefficients indexed by the carry-free tuples.

records.title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function
records.abstract: Formalizes Lamzouri's Hilbert-space proof of lower bounds for simple and distinct zeros of the Riemann zeta function. From explicit Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation hypotheses, the development proves that eventually more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeros are simple and on the critical line and more than 83.625% are distinct. It includes the finite-multiset Hilbert-space inequality, zeta-zero multiplicity symmetries, an admissible cutoff construction, and certified trigonometric estimates.

informal.ZetaZeros.simple_proportion_d4: Assuming the stated Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation formulas, beyond some height more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeta zeros are simple and lie on the critical line.
informal.ZetaZeros.distinct_proportion_d5: Under the same two explicit analytic hypotheses, beyond some height more than 83.625% of nontrivial zeta zeros are distinct.
informal.ZetaZeros.card_simpleRealPart_lower: Bounds from below the number of multiplicity-one real points in a finite nonempty conjugation-invariant multiset using the squared test-kernel sum of any admissible function.
informal.ZetaZeros.card_lower: Bounds from below the number of distinct points in a finite nonempty conjugation-invariant multiset using the same Hilbert-space kernel method.

records.title: Linear independence of 1, zeta(2), and zeta(3)
records.abstract: Proves that 1, the Riemann zeta function at 2, and its value at 3 are linearly independent over the rationals, using integer polynomial approximation, p-adic coefficient bounds, prime-edge nonvanishing, and logarithmic potential energy estimates for Hankel determinants. Includes reusable irrationality criteria, contour integration, Andreief identities, Newton-basis valuation bounds, and energy inequalities for finite measures. The cited source is the completed Lean proof; independent novelty of the informal argument is not claimed.

informal.Zeta32.one_zeta_two_zeta_three_linearInd: The three complex numbers 1, riemannZeta 2, and riemannZeta 3 are linearly independent over the rational numbers.
informal.Zeta32Acceptance.one_zeta_two_zeta_three: For rational a, b, and c, if a plus b times the real sum of 1/(k+1)^2 plus c times the real sum of 1/(k+1)^3 is zero, then all three coefficients are zero; both sums range over natural numbers k.
informal.Zeta32.zeta3_sub_rat_mul_zeta2_irrationa: For every rational r, the real series for zeta(3) minus r times the real series for zeta(2) is irrational.

records.title: Irrationality of ζ(3)
records.abstract: Formalizes Beukers' proof of Apéry's theorem for ζ(3), including the integral identities, denominator estimates, positivity, upper bounds, and final irrationality contradiction.

informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.linear_int: Clears denominators in the Apéry integral to produce a linear form in 1 and ζ(3).
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.JJ_pos: Proves positivity of the transformed Beukers-Apéry integral.
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.JJ_upper: Bounds the Beukers-Apéry integral by a geometric factor times the ζ(3) series.
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.fun1_tendsto_ze: Shows that the denominator-cleared Apéry linear forms tend to zero.

records.title: ZFLean
records.abstract: Develops a practical ZFC set-theory framework with von Neumann naturals, integers, rationals, functions, embeddings, isomorphisms, booleans, and sums.

informal.ZFSet.isIso_of_biembedding: Proves a Cantor-Bernstein theorem for ZF sets.
informal.ZFSet.ZFNat.induction: Provides induction for the von Neumann natural numbers.
informal.ZFSet.ZFInt.induction: Provides induction for the quotient construction of ZF integers.

records.title: The Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon information inequality
records.abstract: Formalizes the Zhang-Yeung inequality, the first known non-Shannon-type entropy inequality, together with its dual and averaged forms derived through the copy lemma.

informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung: Proves the Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon-type information inequality for four discrete random variables.
informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung_dual: Proves the dual form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.
informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung_averaged: Proves the averaged symmetric form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.

records.title: Modular Schur numbers: S_m(k,ℓ) = n − 1 for k ≥ n − 1, where n = m/gcd(m,ℓ−1)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, with Mathlib, of the main results of the paper "Prime-power structure of the stable regime for modular Schur numbers" (docs/paper/modular-schur.pdf in this repository). The modular Schur number S_m(k,ℓ), introduced by Chappelon, Revuelta Marchena and Sanz Domínguez (2013), is the largest N such that 1, …, N can be coloured with k colours so that no colour class contains a solution of x_1 + ⋯ + x_ℓ ≡ y (mod m). For m ≥ 2 and ℓ ≥ 2, put n = m/gcd(m,ℓ−1). The main theorem is the closed form S_m(k,ℓ) = n − 1 for every k ≥ n − 1. D'orville, Sim, Wong and Ho (Integers 25 (2025) #A62) gave it when gcd(m,ℓ−1) = 1 (their Corollary 5). The general case is a short corollary of the singleton criterion and their Corollary 3; to the author's knowledge it is first stated in the paper. The proof turns on one value: ℓ copies of n sum to n modulo m, so the class {n} alone breaks the rule, while each of 1, …, n − 1 is safe in a class of its own. The formalization also proves the one-colour closed form S_m(1,ℓ) = min(ℓ − 1, ⌊m/ℓ⌋) for 2 ≤ ℓ ≤ m, which answers Problem 1.3 of D'orville et al.; the bound S_m(k,ℓ) ≤ m − 1 of Chappelon et al.; and the reduction from integers to residues modulo m. Twelve theorems with Mathlib-only statements are compared by lake comparator (statement identity, permitted axioms, and replay through the Lean, nanoda and con-ron kernels); their only axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The 33 project modules also contain further results, listed in LEAN_STATUS.md, that are proved and axiom-audited but are not compared, among them the bound m/p, with p the least prime factor of m, on the size of a set of residues whose pairwise differences all lie in a proper subgroup of ℤ/m. An earlier computational part of the project, which uses native_decide, is not in this repository and is not part of these results. The informal proofs, the Lean formalization and the paper were produced with AI systems (Claude, Aristotle and GPT-5) under the direction of the author.

records.title: Generalized Markoff strong approximation
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the generic branch of eventual strong approximation for generalized Markoff surfaces, specialized to a fixed ordered integral coefficient triple. It proves punctured transitivity for both the full Vieta group and the two-Vieta rotation group, supplies an explicit coefficient-dependent cutoff, and derives surjectivity of coordinatewise reduction onto the full finite-field surface.

records.title: Stafford 3.8
records.abstract: Lean formalization of Stafford's Conjecture 3.8 for every characteristic-zero field and every Weyl-algebra rank, proving that each nonzero d admits F, R, and S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S. The development also proves an exact Bernstein-degree fixed-source strengthening and derived localization, adjoint, and evolutionary results.

records.title: Moh's P3 curve is a set-theoretic complete intersection
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization proving that the Moh curve parametrized by x=t^6+t^31, y=t^8, z=t^10 is cut out set-theoretically by two explicit equations over every characteristic-zero field. The development computes the polynomial and formal-power-series parametrization kernels, proves the radical equality for the two-generated witness ideal, and proves that the curve ideal has height two and arithmetic rank two, both globally and after completion. It also verifies the exact Hilbert-Burch presentation given by the manuscript's explicit four-by-three matrix.

records.title: Centred maximal constants for cubes and Euclidean balls
records.abstract: Lean proofs of Yongxi Lin's original weak type (1,1) bounds: c_2 >= 1.6855 and c_2 <= 3.879 for cubes, c_2 <= e for Euclidean discs, and c_n <= (n/2)^(n/(n-2)) for balls in n >= 3. Also proves the classical cube bound c_d <= 2^d.

records.title: An interval-moment criterion for square-difference-free integer sets
records.abstract: We prove a general interval-moment criterion for square-difference-free integer sets and apply it to obtain an improved unconditional lower bound in Sarkozy's theorem, with exponent 0.7580758318008816. If D(N) is the largest size of a subset of {1, ..., N} containing no two distinct elements whose difference is a square, then for every epsilon > 0 and all sufficiently large N we prove D(N) >= N^(0.7580758318008816 - epsilon). The exact exponent is 473797394875551/625000000000000. The reusable criterion starts from finite digit sets in pairwise coprime square bases, with ordered intervals and width-moment inequalities. A strict surplus in the component exponents yields the asymptotic bound through finite stopping words, rank rounding, the Chinese remainder theorem, and interpolation between geometric scales. Both the general criterion and its numerical application are formalized in Lean. All nine concrete components are proved: six prime chains, a 25-state binary recursion, and two complete composite witnesses, at the primes 5 and 43 (three restricted digits at each) and at 19 and 23 (three at 19, two at 23). Every required ordering, numerical moment, lifting, and asymptotic argument is checked, with no remaining finite-certificate hypotheses. This version replaces the exponent 0.75806746 of version 1 with new finite witnesses and more precise certificates. The repository includes self-contained PDF and LaTeX write-ups of the full result and a simpler companion construction attaining exponent 0.758001 that explains several core ideas, together with exact computational certificate programs. The simpler construction is not separately formalized or a selected submission statement.

records.title: Absence of bounded-orbit wandering domains
records.abstract:
We formalise the proof of two major recent results on wandering domains of transcendental entire and meromorphic functions: every orbit in a wandering domain accumulates at infinity and at a non-isolated (derived) point of the spherical set of singular values.
Both results are obtained as a special case of a more general theorem, for locally defined functions on possibly disconnected complex one-manifolds. Let f be an open holomorphic function from an open subset O of such a manifold X into X. Different components of O may map to different components of X, even when those source components lie in the same ambient component. Suppose that U is a wandering component of the set of normality of f, and that z is in U. If the orbit of z is contained in a compact subset of X, then it accumulates at a non-isolated point s of the set of singular values. Moreover, this accumulation must occur close to singularities for infinitely many singular values. That is, there exists a sequence (s_n) of distinct singular values converging to s, a sequence of embedded discs D_n containing s and a sequence U_n of components of f^{-1}(D_n), with the following properties. (We say that the orbit of z has "singular encounters"; see HasSingularEncounterSequence in the formalisation.) * the discs D_n shrink to s; that is, every neighbourhood of s contains D_n for sufficiently large n; * each component U_n contains a point of the orbit of z; * s_n is a singular value of the restriction f:U_n\to D_n. In particular, the orbit of z is not contained in any compact subset of O. In the special case of a transcendental entire or meromorphic function, we can take X to be the Riemann sphere, and hence compact, so that the hypotheses are satisfied for any wandering Fatou component.
We also prove a corresponding theorem for measurable wandering subsets of the complement of the domain of normality on which all iterates are defined and injective; here the conclusion is that almost every point of the set (in any chart) behaves as above: ambient escape along a subsequence, or singular encounters.
As corollaries we recover Epstein's absence of wandering domains for finite-type maps on arbitrary open subsets of compact, possibly disconnected complex one-manifolds, and the classical no-wandering results for rational maps, compact-surface self-maps, and class S entire and meromorphic functions.
This is an update from the previous registered submission on Palomar, https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-09-25-000001&version=3 . The change in this update is to allow functions in the local result to take values in a possibly disconnected complex 1-manifold, rather than a Riemann surface. This aligns the definition with Epstein's original discussion of finite-type analytic maps, which likewise allow (compact) complex 1-manifolds.

records.title: The quasi-isometry classes of Galton–Watson trees: Lean formalisation
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalisation of the automorphism-matching theorems and the quasi-isometry classification of Galton–Watson trees from the paper "The quasi-isometry classes of Galton–Watson trees" by Jayadev S. Athreya and Sascha Troscheit (arXiv:2609.23882). The audited statements are: the i.i.d. matching theorem on the binary tree (Theorem 5.1), the general Markov matching theorem for typed label processes on the binary tree, in its finite-type and zero-compatible forms (Theorem 6.1), the complete classification, up to quasi-isometry, of Galton–Watson trees with finitely supported offspring law conditioned on infinite diameter (Theorem 1.2), the mutual embeddability theorem (Theorem 1.3), and two-value universality with its quantitative rate (Theorem 1.4). The statements are made in Challenge.lean over Mathlib alone and discharged by Solution.lean from four library targets.

records.title: At least one of the 2-adic zeta values ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9) is irrational
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that at least one of the 2-adic zeta values ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9) is irrational. The theorem has no hypotheses, and its proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The values are defined through the Volkenborn integral: zeta2 s = J(s−1)/((s−1)·2^s), where J(s) is the 2-adic limit of the Riemann sums 2^(−N) Σ_{x<2^N} (x+1/2)^(−s), and the theorem also proves that these limits exist. By Lemma 2.8 of Lai, Sprang and Zudilin (IMRN 2026), zeta2 s is the Kubota–Leopoldt value ζ₂(s) = L₂(s, ω^(1−s)) for s ≥ 2. That identification is cited, not formalised; it only involves a non-zero rational factor, which does not affect irrationality. The result sharpens Theorem 1.1 (case s = 3) of L. Lai (Int. J. Number Theory 2025), which shows that at least one of ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11), ζ₂(13) is irrational, and it implies the companion result, formalised in a separate repository, that at least one of ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11) is irrational. The proof uses linear forms S_n = ∫ R_n'''(t+1/2) dt in 1, ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9) built from the shifted well-poised rational functions R_n(t) = (2t+n) Π_{m=1}^{6} (t+1/2−h_m)_(n+2h_m) / (t)_(n+1)^6 with h = (n/40)(−17, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6). The 2-adic size of S_n comes from Lai's and Sprang's Δ-calculus. The size of the coefficients comes from a contour-integral representation and a saddle-point bound, whose numerical inequalities are certified in Lean. The odd part of the denominators is bounded by Legendre-type counts at the poles, the vanishing of R_n at half-integers, kernel-checked certificates and the prime number theorem (proved here from a vendored Lean proof of the Wiener–Ikehara theorem). If both values were rational, the valuations of the coefficients at the prime n − 1 (an idea of Lai and Sprang) would make S_n non-zero for infinitely many n, and Lai's irrationality criterion gives the contradiction. The mathematics and the Lean code were produced by AI agents under human direction and have not been refereed.

records.title: MAF composition criteria, exact enumeration of child-selection autocatalytic cores, and degradation regions of linear diluted source networks
records.abstract: We establish three sets of results addressing published questions about the composition, enumeration and degradation of autocatalytic reaction networks. In response to the composition questions of Gagrani, Wang, De Decker and Lacoste (arXiv:2603.02627, Discussion and outlook), we give exact criteria for strict increases in the maximum amplification factor (MAF) under reaction addition, nonnegative species aggregation and shared-species coupling, assuming nonnegative inputs and attained MAFs. A block direct sum attains the larger component MAF, while an explicit example shows that component MAFs alone do not determine the MAF of a coupled network. Addressing the CS-core enumeration direction of Golnik, Gatter, Stadler and Vassena (arXiv:2603.02770, Section 6), we prove exact reconstruction from a complete list of ordinary-core anchor matchings, each unique on its vertex set, by alternating-path generation and certified rational semipositivity filtering. We establish existence of the certified test, its rejection of the empty matching, and an explicit nonempty instance for A → 2A. For the arbitrary-degradation question discussed by Nandan, Nghe and Unterberger (arXiv:2507.15546, Section 6), we characterize growth, criticality and extinction for irreducible linear diluted source networks with nonnegative unary reaction data and species degradation d ≥ 0: the real spectral bound of A − diag(d) is positive, zero or negative exactly when d is componentwise strictly below, equal to or strictly above (Av)_i/v_i for some positive v. We also characterize partial-actuation stabilizability of Metzler matrices through a positive-vector certificate on the unactuated block. All eleven selected statements are formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

records.title: Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem (strategy-proof social choice)
records.abstract: Formalizes the Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem for finite electorates and finite alternative sets with at least three alternatives: every onto, strategy-proof social choice function is dictatorial. The proof constructs a social welfare function and reduces to Arrow's impossibility theorem.

records.title: Erdős Problem #1220 in Lean 4: the affirmative statement is not provable in ZFC
records.abstract: Erdős problem #1220 (erdosproblems.com/1220; Erdős–Hajnal 1971): let λ be a singular cardinal such that both λ and cf(λ) are ℵ₀-inaccessible (μ^ℵ₀ < κ for all μ < κ); does λ → (λ, ℵ₁)² hold?  This formalization settles the question as asked on erdosproblems.com in the negative sense "not provable": ZFC does not prove that every such λ satisfies λ → (λ, ℵ₁)² (erdos1220_not_provable : ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos1220)), i.e. there is a model of ZFC with a singular λ, λ and cf(λ) ℵ₀-inaccessible, and λ ↛ (λ, ℵ₁)².  Shelah and Stanley (Sh:258, Ann. Pure Appl. Logic 36 (1987)) showed that a negative answer is consistent with ZFC.  This project formalizes that consistency result: the comparator target erdos1220_not_provable : ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos1220) is stated for literally the same first-order theory ZFC, language and ZFSet interpretation as elliotglazer/erdos501's comparator challenge (imported from its statement module Erdos501.FOL.Statement), together with a faithfulness theorem erdos1220_sentence_faithful: in Mathlib's ZFSet the sentence Erdos1220 holds iff the Mathlib-level statement Erdos1220.Problem1220 holds.  The witness is the ground-model singular strong-limit cardinal λ = ℶ_{𝔠⁺} (cf λ = 𝔠⁺; λ and cf λ are ℵ₀-inaccessible without any deep cardinal-arithmetic input), not ℵ_{𝔠⁺}.  The forcing is the Shelah–Stanley §3 forcing, formalized as block-preserving, block-covering histories of basic conditions (weak extension order), with the μ⁺-strategic closure (hence μ-distributivity) and the (2^μ)⁺-chain condition proved in ZFC without GCH (Δ-system lemma for (2^μ)⁺ sets of size ≤ μ, blueprint counting (2^μ)^μ = 2^μ).  In the Boolean-valued model of its regular-open algebra (built with the Lean 4 port of Han–van Doorn's Flypitch vendored by erdos501) the hypotheses on λ are preserved, the generic colouring of [λ]² has neither a red homogeneous set of size λ nor a blue homogeneous set of size ℵ₁, and Flypitch's completeness theorem turns this into a two-valued model of ZFC satisfying ¬Erdos1220.  Both targets are proved from propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only and pass the Lean comparator.  Only the negative direction is claimed: independence (consistency of a positive answer) is NOT claimed.

records.title: Myerson-Satterthwaite impossibility theorem (continuous bilateral-trade version)
records.abstract: Formalizes the continuous-type bilateral-trade impossibility result: no mechanism can satisfy ex post efficiency (almost surely), Bayesian incentive compatibility, interim individual rationality, and weak ex ante budget balance when buyer and seller supports overlap. The proof uses payoff equivalence and envelope identities, together with the strict rent-gap identity B + C > S.

records.title: Hamilton cycles in Cayley graphs of polylogarithmic degree
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the following theorem: there are absolute constants C, n0 > 0 such that every connected Cayley graph Cay(G, S) on n >= n0 vertices whose degree d = |S| is at least C (log n)^13 / log log n contains a Hamilton cycle (Lovasz.hamiltonian_of_polylog_degree). Here G is a finite group, S is a connection set (S = S^-1 and 1 not in S, so the graph is |S|-regular), log is the natural logarithm, and connectivity is equivalent to S generating G. The theorem is a case of the Lovász conjecture (every connected vertex-transitive graph has a Hamilton path) in its Cayley-graph form (every connected Cayley graph on at least three vertices is Hamiltonian). For arbitrary connected Cayley graphs the previously published degree thresholds were linear degree (Christofides, Hladký and Máthé, 2014) and degree at least n^(1-c) (Bedert, Draganić, Müyesser and Pavez-Signé, 2026). The proof follows the source manuscript: it extracts a connected bipartite template with spectral gap of order (log n)^-2, allocates the vertices to weighted translates of the template by signed rounding (a robust signed integrality theorem derived from the capacitated b-matching polytope, swap rounding, and a trace-exponential matrix concentration bound), connects the pieces by a sparse matching chosen by mutual nominations and a signed circulation, absorbs the outside matching inside every piece with Hamilton routers built from even-cycle comparators, and merges cycles. Every lemma of the manuscript is proved in the repository, as are the classical results it uses without proof (normalized Cheeger inequality, Haxell's hypergraph matching theorem, the b-matching polytope, Watkins's connectivity bound, the Nash-Williams–Tutte tree-packing theorem, Hoffman's circulation criterion, scalar Chernoff bounds); Hall's theorem is taken from Mathlib, and matrix Bernstein is avoided by deriving the one lemma that used it from the manuscript's own concentration bound. The source manuscript is an unpublished research draft that describes its own proof as not independently verified; this formalization is, to the maintainer's knowledge, the first verification of the theorem. The proved theorem has no sorry and depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Existence of a Model Companion for Groups of Exponent 3: Lean Formalization
records.abstract: This project formalizes the existence of a model companion for the first-order theory of groups satisfying x^3 = 1. Its principal group-theoretic result gives a uniform, explicit bound on the number of generators needed to witness a failure of amalgamation with an existentially closed exponent-three group. The development follows the accompanying manuscript through free groups, associated graded Lie algebras, strict extensions, and the bounded-amalgamation criterion.

records.title: Metric TSP subtour-LP integrality gap
records.abstract: Lean proofs that every metric TSP instance on at least three vertices has a Hamiltonian tour costing at most (3/2 - 2.05522e-30) times any feasible subtour-LP objective, with one strictly larger saving uniform over all instances. The submission also exposes the exact finite-layer saving and a KKO-framework bound using GKL capacity estimates.

records.title: Uniform Minor-Arc Cancellation for Primes at the X^{2/15+ε} Scale
records.abstract: We prove uniform cancellation in prime-weighted exponential sums at the 2/15 scale, improving the 8/33 local Fourier scale in the Matomäki–Radziwiłł–Tao machinery for averaged prime-pair correlations. On the minor-arc part of every centered arc of radius 1/(2H), the squared von Mangoldt exponential sum over X < n <= 2X has integral at most C X (log X)^(-A), for every A > 0 and epsilon > 0, once H >= X^(2/15+epsilon) and X is large enough. The center may lie anywhere on the circle. The same cutoffs and constants work for every center and are chosen before X and H. This gives uniform minor-arc cancellation at the 2/15 threshold. Since 2/15 < 8/33, the admissible H is smaller, so the frequency windows of length 1/H are wider and the shift-averaging intervals are shorter. The constants C and X0 are ineffective because the proof uses Siegel's theorem. The development also contains an internal proof of the epsilon-form of Guth–Maynard's large-value estimate for Dirichlet polynomials. The recorded 20 September Lean 4.30 kernel replays checked 100,596 declarations for MAP and 75,874 for Guth–Maynard, using only standard axioms. The formal statement is AllCenterMAP.map_two_fifteenths, manuscript Theorem 1.1.

records.title: Corvaja–Zannier 2004: rational approximations to the powers of an algebraic number
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the whole of P. Corvaja and U. Zannier, On the rational approximations to the powers of an algebraic number: solution of two problems of Mahler and Mendès France (Acta Math. 193 (2004)), built on the repository's libraries ArithmeticHeights and DiophantineApproximation, whose Subspace Theorem it uses. The library CorvajaZannier2004 is sorry-free and within Lean's three standard axioms. It proves the Main Theorem (finitely many non-pseudo-Pisot δqu that are very close to integers, u in a finitely generated group of algebraic numbers), Theorem 1 (Mahler's question: if ‖αⁿ‖ < lⁿ infinitely often, some power of α is a Pisot number), Lemmas 1–5, Theorem 2 (Mendès France's question: the period of the continued fraction of αⁿ tends to infinity unless α is a unit or a square root of a rational, and is bounded for units), and the Appendix (the word "algebraic" cannot be dropped from Theorem 1). Eleven statements are compared.

records.title: Equivalence of the RAF abundance conjecture and Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture
records.abstract: In a catalytic reaction system with finitely many reactions, a RAF is a nonempty set of reactions whose reactants are produced from the food set by iterated closure under the selected reactions and whose reactions are each catalysed by a molecule of that closure. Steel (arXiv:2305.16714v4, Section 4) asked whether some reaction always lies in at least half of the RAFs. Call a reaction food-ready if all its reactants are food, and abundant if it lies in at least half of the sets in the family formed by the RAFs and the empty set. If some RAF U consists entirely of food-ready reactions, then some reaction of U is abundant, with no condition on the other reactions. If every reaction of the system, except at most two, is food-ready and the system has a RAF, then some reaction is abundant. Finally, the statement that every catalytic reaction system with finitely many reactions and a RAF has an abundant reaction is equivalent to Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture in the form: every finite union-closed family containing the empty set and a nonempty set has an element lying in at least half of its members.

records.title: Zero forcing number of the generalized Petersen graphs P(n,3)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that the zero-forcing number of the generalized Petersen graph P(n,3) is exactly 8 for every natural number n >= 13. The formalized result is the statement recorded as Conjecture 5 in Arnav Krishnan's July 2026 correction preprint; this repository supplies and kernel-checks a proof of that conjectured statement rather than formalizing a proof already given in the cited preprint.

records.title: The Four Color Theorem (Lean 4 port of Gonthier's Coq proof)
records.abstract:
A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the Four Color Theorem, ported from Georges Gonthier's Coq proof by Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic's AI model, working as an agent under the direction of Robert D. Barish. The main theorem, FourColor.RealPlane.four_color, states that every simple map of the real plane can be colored with at most four colors so that adjacent regions get different colors. The map may have infinitely many regions, bounded or not; each region must be open and connected, and two regions are adjacent when their closures share a point that lies in the closure of no third region. As in Coq, a compactness argument reduces the theorem to finite maps, which are turned into planar bridgeless hypermaps. A smallest hypermap that cannot be four-colored cannot exist: discharging shows that it would contain one of the 633 configurations of Robertson, Sanders, Seymour and Thomas, and each of these is reducible.
The port differs from the Coq proof in three main ways. Its statement uses Mathlib's real numbers rather than an arbitrary model of Coq's axiomatized reals; the two are equivalent, because all such models are isomorphic and the definitions use only the order. Coq checks that the 633 configurations are reducible with a procedure on trees of colorings, run by its virtual machine. The port replaces it with a new bit-parallel engine whose certificates, generated during the build, are checked by the Lean kernel itself. Finally, the case analysis of the unavoidability proof, written as tactic scripts in Coq, becomes case trees checked by a checker proved correct once. Every computation is carried out by the Lean kernel, without native_decide, and the proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Péterfalvi's Problem for p = 3: No Group Satisfies Hypothesis (B)
records.abstract: Glauberman and Norton (Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 119, 1993) end their paper on a combinatorial problem that arises in the proof of the Feit–Thompson odd order theorem with a question of Péterfalvi: can the hypothesis of their Proposition 9 be satisfied for p = 3? The same question is Problem 1 in Appendix C of Bender and Glauberman, Local Analysis for the Odd Order Theorem (1994). Let F be the field with p^q elements, P its additive group, U its group of units of norm one over the prime field, H the semidirect product P ⋊ U, and P₀ the image of the additive group of the prime field in H. Hypothesis (B) asks for an injective homomorphism σ from H into a group G, a finite abelian subgroup Q of G whose order is prime to p, and an element y of Q, such that σ(P₀) normalizes Q and σ(P₀)^y normalizes σ(U). Proposition 9 also assumes condition (A): q does not divide p − 1. This project proves in Lean 4 that the answer is negative: for every prime q with q ∤ 3 − 1, no group G, finite or infinite, satisfies hypothesis (B) with p = 3. It also proves Péterfalvi's example from the same paper, which shows that SL(2, 2^q) satisfies hypothesis (B) with p = 2, so the hypothesis is not empty. The proof is new. It turns a witness of hypothesis (B) into relations between three copies of the additive group of the field with 3^q elements, and it rules out these relations by arithmetic in that field.

records.title: Global class field theory in Lean 4.35.0-rc2
records.abstract: For every finite abelian extension L/K of number fields, the idèle class group C_K modulo the image of the idèle-class norm from C_L is isomorphic as a topological multiplicative group to Gal(L/K). The Challenge defines the norm as the determinant on the relative adèle algebra and descends it through principal idèles; the included ClassFieldTheory development supplies the proof of the resulting reciprocity theorem.

records.title: Local class field theory in Lean 4.35.0-rc2
records.abstract: For every finite abelian extension L/K of a nonarchimedean local field, the multiplicative group K× modulo the field-norm subgroup N_{L/K}(L×) is isomorphic as a topological group to Gal(L/K). The registered declaration is the finite norm-quotient form of local reciprocity proved in the included ClassFieldTheory development. Stronger compatibility, normalization and existence results in that development are documented separately and are not part of the compared declaration.

records.title: Lean Formalization of Interpreting Lambda Calculus in Domain-Valued Random Variables (CSL 2026)
records.abstract: Formalization in Lean 4 / mathlib of the existing paper by Furber, Mardare, Panangaden, and Scott, Interpreting Lambda Calculus in Domain-Valued Random Variables (LIPIcs, Vol. 363, CSL 2026, Article 48). This repository formalizes that published mathematics; it does not present the paper's results as new mathematics originating in this repository. Three capstones sit on top of the rest of the paper: Theorem 26 (internal λ-interpretation in SetoidF_A), Corollary 34 (the Engeler model with numerals in V^A), and Theorem 43 (two fair-coin subsets of ℕ that are incomparable under the λ-definable many-one preorder). Domain-theory background is imported from a vendored copy of scott1972. The Palomar Challenge locks Theorem 43 as csl2026 and proposition_36_i on the Engeler graph model. Full Corollary 34 remains kernel-checked in the library and is not represented by a weaker Mathlib-only proxy. Lean is written by AI agents under the direction and review of the author. Dana Scott gave the author the paper. This formalization does not claim that the paper's authors participated in it or endorsed it. There is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and Mathlib is the only Lake require.

records.title: Conditional Hilbert-space classification of Gromov--Hausdorff space
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the implication from five explicitly stated literature inputs to a homeomorphism between the ordinary Gromov--Hausdorff space of nonempty compact metric spaces and real square-summable sequences. The proof constructs invariant full-support probability assignments, finite dimensional local models, global AR domination and discrete approximation. The five literature inputs are assumptions, not theorems proved in this snapshot.

records.title: Adversary bounds and the polynomial method for quantum queries
records.abstract: Lean proofs of strong duality and exact block composition for the negative-weight adversary bound on total Boolean functions, explicit constant-factor characterizations of bounded-error quantum query complexity in value and Boolean XOR oracle models, and uniform extraction of query algorithms from supplied promise dual certificates. The submission also proves that every output probability of a q-query algorithm on Boolean inputs has a real polynomial representation of degree at most 2q in each model. Seven statements are compared against a standalone Mathlib-only specification of the finite quantum model.

records.title: A Lean formalization of the Erdős discrepancy theorem
records.abstract: A formalization in Lean 4 and Mathlib of the Erdős discrepancy theorem, proved by Terence Tao in 2015: for every sequence f(1), f(2), … of signs ±1 and every C there are d ≥ 1 and n with |f(d) + f(2d) + ⋯ + f(nd)| > C, so every ±1 sequence has unbounded discrepancy along homogeneous arithmetic progressions. This is the original ±1 formulation, Corollary 1.2 of Tao's paper; its Hilbert-space-valued Theorem 1.1 is not formalized. The proof follows the architecture of Tao's argument: a Fourier-analytic reduction from a sequence of bounded discrepancy to a stochastic completely multiplicative function with bounded mean-square partial sums; a van der Corput argument, driven by the logarithmically averaged two-point Elliott estimate, forcing such a function to pretend to be a twisted Dirichlet character; and a generalized Borwein–Choi–Coons argument excluding that case. The analytic number theory these steps use is proved in the same development rather than assumed: the entropy-decrement proof of the two-point Elliott estimate from Tao's companion paper, the Matomäki–Radziwiłł short-interval estimate on the major arcs via the Dirichlet-polynomial route of Matomäki, Radziwiłł and Tao, the Halász–Montgomery large-values inequality, a large-values bound for Dirichlet polynomials over primes from a zero-free region of the Riemann zeta function, that zero-free region from Weyl-sum bounds on zeta, and a form of Vinogradov's mean value theorem. Where a published route did not fit, the development adapts it; the adaptations are documented. The theorem depends only on Lean's three standard axioms. This is a formalization of a published result, not a new proof; it was produced by AI agents working through pull requests checked by continuous integration in the ProofFleet repository (formerly MoltResearch).

records.title: Characterizing digraph support families by rooted-interval deletion
records.abstract: We answer the set-theoretic characterization question for digraph support families posed by Mike Steel in Section 4 of Interior operators and their relationship to autocatalytic networks (arXiv:2305.16714v4, 2023). A digraph on a finite set E is given by a predecessor map P assigning to each vertex e a set P(e) of in-neighbours, loops allowed, and a set S is supported when every element e of S has some element of S in P(e). The characterization refers only to the family F. Start from the full power set of E with no roots used. A legal step chooses a remaining set S outside F that is inclusion-maximal among the remaining sets outside F, chooses a root r in S that has not been used before and lies in no member of F contained in S, and deletes every remaining set X with r in X and X contained in S. A family F of subsets of E is exactly the support family of some predecessor map on E if and only if some finite sequence of legal steps ends exactly at F.

records.title: Two-fold Langford sequences exist exactly when 3l ≥ 2d − 1; the m-fold counting bound and its attainment, and a residue bound
records.abstract: A Lean 4 characterization of two-fold Langford sequences. An m-fold Langford sequence of order l and defect d fills the positions 1, ..., 2ml so that every p in [d, d + l - 1] occupies the endpoints of m pairwise disjoint pairs of positions at distance p. For d, l >= 1 a two-fold sequence exists exactly when 3l >= 2d - 1. For every m, (2m - 1)l >= 2d - 1 is necessary, with l(2d + l + 1) = 0 (mod 4) for odd m, and the bound is attained whenever 2d + l = 2ml + 1; the row of order one exists exactly when d divides m; no three-fold sequence of order 3 and defect 6 exists; and for every m >= 3 the necessary conditions are not sufficient. For every T >= 1, with r = ml mod T, every m-fold sequence satisfies the residue bound r(T - r) <= m * sum |p - T| over p in [d, d + l - 1], which contains the counting bound and the necessity half of the order-one theorem. Every m-fold sequence satisfies the forced-endpoint bound 6mld + ml <= 4d^2 + 2(ml)^2 + ml^2. For every m >= 3 the cell (d, l) = (3m - 3, 3) meets the necessary conditions and admits no m-fold sequence. Equality 2d + l = 2ml + 1 holds exactly when every pair straddles the middle, that is ml < i + s_i for every position i <= ml. Alkasasbeh, Dyer and Howell define these sequences and ask for necessary and sufficient conditions when m >= 2; this repository answers the question for m = 2. Necessity is a distance sum. Sufficiency at m = 2 is strong induction on l: sixteen literal cells, concatenation, and otherwise a mirror-symmetric sequence built by Lemma S from a signed permutation, which is found on the whole cone by inversion, the reversal, a descent along lines of fixed mu, and in the band by 21 block-reversal families plus the two-block reversal tau_l, eight sporadic cells and three bases. The tight line is m interleaved copies of the source's Table 1.

records.title: Erdős Problem #1219 in Lean 4: Σ_k 2^{ℵ_{n_k}} → (ℵ_ω)² (Shelah 1975)
records.abstract: Erdős problem #1219 (erdosproblems.com/1219; Erdős–Hajnal 1971, Problem 3, asked by Erdős, Hajnal and Rado): let (n_k) be an increasing sequence of integers such that 2^{ℵ_{n_k}} is strictly increasing and 2^{ℵ_{n_0}} > ℵ_ω; is it true that Σ_k 2^{ℵ_{n_k}} → (ℵ_ω)²?  Shelah (Notes on partition calculus, 1975, §1) proved that the answer is yes.  This project formalizes that proof in Lean 4 with Mathlib: the comparator target erdos_1219 states that for every strictly increasing n : ℕ → ℕ with k ↦ 2 ^ ℵ_(n k) strictly increasing and ℵ_ω < 2 ^ ℵ_(n 0), the binary partition relation PartitionArrow (Σ_k 2 ^ ℵ_(n k)) ℵ_ω holds, i.e. every 2-colouring of the 2-element subsets of a set of cardinality Σ_k 2 ^ ℵ_(n k) has a monochromatic subset of cardinality ℵ_ω (PartitionArrow is the binary case of formal-conjectures' Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel).  The proof follows Shelah's Canonization Lemma 1.1 and Theorem 1.2: the unbalanced Erdős–Rado theorem (2^μ)⁺ → ((2^μ)⁺, μ⁺)² (proved here with a critical-ordinal / closure-point argument), a canonization of the colouring across blocks of sizes (2^{ℵ_{n_k}})⁺ by means of guides generic over all small subsets of the earlier blocks, and Ramsey's theorem for pairs on ℕ.  The target is proved from propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only and passes the Lean comparator (landrun sandbox, NanoDa kernel).

records.title: Erdős Problem 809: rainbow odd cycles
records.abstract: A Lean proof resolving the Burr–Erdős–Graham–Sós conjecture (Erdős Problem 809): for every fixed odd cycle of length at least seven, the maximal anti-Ramsey threshold at floor(n²/4) + 1 edges is n²/8 + o(n²). The seven-cycle case is new to our knowledge. The development proves it and formalizes the stronger full-density result of Bucić, Chen, and Ma for odd cycles of length at least nine.

records.title: One-generated (1518 + 3862)-magmas are trivial or the Z/3 shift; an explicit family of finite 1518-magmas violating laws 47, 614, 817, 3862
records.abstract: Lean 4 results (core Lean, no dependencies, no axioms beyond the standard three) about law 1518 of the Equational Theories Project, x = (y ◇ y) ◇ (x ◇ (y ◇ x)). Theorem A: in every magma satisfying 1518 and 3862 (x ◇ x = (x ◇ (x ◇ x)) ◇ x), writing S x = x ◇ x, the set {x, S x, S (S x)} is closed under ◇ with u ◇ v = S v and S (S (S x)) = x; hence every one-generated such magma is the trivial magma or the three-element cyclic shift x ◇ y = y + 1. This proves a classification conjectured by Terence Tao on the Lean Zulip on 2024-11-29 (message 485148288). That message assumed 1518 together with all four of 47, 614, 817 and 3862 and carried no finiteness hypothesis; assuming 3862 alone is no weaker, because Matthew Bolan reported the same day (message 485153888) that 1518 and 3862 already imply the other three. What is added here is a machine-checked proof, not a weaker hypothesis: no proof of the classification was found in the venues searched. Theorem A is what the compared declarations state. Outside them the repository holds an explicit family of finite 1518-magmas that do violate the four targets, with two members checked by kernel evaluation, and kernel-checked certificate identities behind a cohomological obstruction theorem (every 1518-cocycle over the shift with finite fibre is a coboundary), whose reduction is a written proof, and the computations classifying base-dependent extensions of the shift.

records.title: NP-hardness of Gaussian c-separation
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof development of reduction idea toward NP-hardness of feature selection for relative Gaussian c-separation in the formulation of Borozan et al. The argument starts from NP-completeness of equal-cardinality partition of positive squares, giving integral Gaussian data via integer roots and an even paired total. Three Gaussians enforce partition balance, and a schedule of d+1 Gaussians enforces binary selectors. Explicit separation of the two blocks makes cross-block hinge penalties vanish. The fixed threshold is (dot s 1 / 2)*d*(d+1)/2 - 3*d/4, an integer multiple of 1/4 for natural input weights. Here d is the full dimension. The main proved result is the pointwise gadget iff. The full complexity reduction is not formalized. The threshold depends only on the input. General Karamata inequality and an unconditional ordinary-PARTITION to perfect-square equal-cardinality partition equivalence are auxiliary results stated in Solution.lean. The square encoding has proved injectivity and numerical size bounds; its NP-completeness argument is documented prose. The original Gaussian gadget predicate also has a proved binary certificate verifier with soundness, completeness, and quadratic work in a bit-cost model. The Gaussian gadget equivalence and square-partition reduction were developed and first presented by the author in this formalization. Their mathematical novelty and priority relative to earlier literature are unknown; no systematic literature search or comparison establishing them has been documented.

records.title: At least one of ζ(7), ζ(9), …, ζ(21) is irrational
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that at least one of the eight values ζ(7), ζ(9), ζ(11), ζ(13), ζ(15), ζ(17), ζ(19), ζ(21) of the Riemann zeta function is irrational. The statement uses only Mathlib's riemannZeta, the theorem has no hypotheses, and its proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The shortest list of odd zeta values starting at ζ(7) that our literature search found proved to contain an irrational number was ζ(7), ζ(9), …, ζ(35) (W. Zudilin, Math. Notes 2001). The proof uses the very-well-poised linear forms of Zudilin (J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux 2004, §8) with five derivatives, 23 factors and the direction vector η₀ = 160, η = (47, 47, 47, 47, 48, 50, 50, 51, 52, …, 66); they are linear forms in 1, ζ(7), ζ(9), …, ζ(21) with rational coefficients. Zudilin anticipated such an improvement but could not prove the asymptotics of his forms (his Lemma 20) for more than three derivatives. The proof here does not need them. The denominators of the coefficients are bounded by Zudilin's arithmetic lemma, the prime number theorem (proved from a vendored Lean proof of the Wiener–Ikehara theorem) and a kernel-checked table of 2602 pieces of Zudilin's function φ. For large n the forms are bounded by e^(−748.1n), through a contour integral on a fixed vertical line, pointwise estimates and certified numerical inequalities, without saddle-point analysis. They are non-zero if the eight values are rational, because at the auxiliary primes ℓ = 63n − 1, of which there are infinitely many by Dirichlet's theorem, the constant term has ℓ-adic valuation −5 while the coefficients of the zeta values are ℓ-integral. The theorem does not say which value is irrational. The mathematics and the Lean code were produced by AI agents under human direction and have not been refereed.

records.title: Determinants and unstable cores in sequential distributive phosphorylation
records.abstract: Vassena and Stadler (arXiv:2308.11486v3, Supplementary Example D) conjectured that sequential distributive phosphorylation cycles have only unstable-positive cores and that every invertible child-selection matrix has determinant of absolute value one. The determinant assertion is proved, and the restriction to unstable-positive cores is disproved. In the n-site cycle, every child-selection matrix has determinant 0, 1 or -1. For every n >= 3, a six-species child-selection matrix is minimally Hurwitz-unstable and has determinant 1, giving an unstable-negative core. For every n >= 2, there is an unstable-positive core on 2n+1 species, so their sizes are unbounded; every proper principal submatrix remains nonunstable under every positive column scaling. For every n >= 3, there is also a five-species D-unstable core: a positive column scaling makes it unstable, while every proper principal submatrix remains nonunstable under all such scalings.

records.title: Attracting oscillations in sequential distributive phosphorylation
records.abstract: Vassena (arXiv:2608.27081v2, Section 8) left open whether sequential distributive phosphorylation cycles with three or more sites admit Hopf bifurcation under mass-action kinetics. For every n >= 3, a componentwise-affine family of positive rate constants is constructed for the n-site cycle with one kinase and one phosphatase and a fixed positive equilibrium. A family of strictly positive, nonconstant periodic orbits bifurcates from this equilibrium, with amplitudes tending to zero and periods tending to a finite positive limit. Each orbit is orbitally asymptotically stable within its compatibility class: sufficiently nearby states with the same kinase, phosphatase and substrate totals have unique positive forward solutions that remain close to the orbit and converge to it.

records.title: Adamczewski–Bugeaud 2007: the complexity of algebraic numbers in integer bases
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of B. Adamczewski and Y. Bugeaud, On the complexity of algebraic numbers I. Expansions in integer bases (Ann. of Math. 165 (2007)), built on the repository's libraries ArithmeticHeights, DiophantineApproximation and ForMathlib, whose Subspace Theorem with algebraic coefficients it uses. The library AdamczewskiBugeaud2007 is sorry-free and within Lean's three standard axioms. It proves Theorem 1 (the complexity of an irrational algebraic number in an integer base satisfies p(n)/n → ∞, with (1), p(n) − n → ∞), Theorems 2–4 (automatic and morphic expansions), Theorem 5 in full (β Pisot or Salem, bounded integer digits satisfying Condition (∗)_w: the number lies in ℚ(β) or is transcendental), Lemma 1, Theorems 1A–5A on β-expansions with K. Schmidt's periodicity theorem, and the p-adic Theorems 6 and 1B–4B, together with the finite automata and morphisms of §3, and Theorem 7 in corrected form (u_k < min(b, p)) with Christol's theorem (algebraic ⇒ automatic) and a counterexample to Theorem 7 as printed. The counterexample and the corrected hypothesis were worked out during this formalization, not taken from the cited works (see limitations). Thirty-two statements are compared.

records.title: Zero-divisor criteria for absolute concentration robustness
records.abstract: García Puente et al. (arXiv:2401.00078v3, Question 3.13) asked whether a unique positive zero-divisor value is necessary or sufficient for absolute concentration robustness (ACR) in at-most-bimolecular mass-action networks. Explicit networks with positive rational rates answer both questions negatively. A further three-species example shows that their candidate algorithm can miss a zero-divisor ACR value under an admissible elimination order, refuting the unrestricted elimination-order form of Conjecture 4.7. For block orders that compare the other species before the distinguished species, completeness is established: every real zero-divisor ACR value is returned when the finite basis consists of nonzero steady-ideal elements whose leading monomials cover the ideal. ACR includes existence of a positive steady state; zero-divisor values include coordinate differences lying in the steady-state ideal.

records.title: kissing-number-lean
records.abstract: The kissing number of Euclidean 3-space is 12: at most twelve unit balls with disjoint interiors touch a given unit ball, and twelve do. The upper bound follows Musin's extension of the Delsarte linear-programming method. The Delsarte machinery on the sphere (positive-definite zonal kernels up to degree 9 and the LP bound, which by itself gives only 13) is built from scratch, since Mathlib has no spherical harmonics. The lower bound is the cuboctahedron.

records.title: Irrationality of Li₂(1/2)
