records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the irrationality of Li₂(1/2) = Σ_{n≥1} 2^(-n)/n². The proof is inspired by A. Fauzan's work on the irrationality of ζ(5) and builds on Moritz Firsching's Lean formalization in mo271/Zeta5. The central idea is to establish the irrationality of a real number r by constructing a sequence of integer polynomials P_n whose values P_n(r) decay rapidly as n tends to infinity, while for every rational q, P_n(q) ≠ 0 for infinitely many n. Analytic umbral calculus was used to find suitable polynomials Q_n with rational coefficients. Random matrix theory provides rapid decay of Q_n(r) as n tends to infinity. Estimates of p-adic valuations, together with the prime number theorem, ensure that the values P_n(r) of the corresponding primitive integer polynomials also decay rapidly as n tends to infinity, completing the proof. Similar methods may apply to other values Li₂(1/n), but those cases are not included here. The compared theorem depends on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and on nothing else, and there is no sorry outside the one deliberate hole in Challenge.lean.

records.title: Hong and Kung's red-blue pebble game: the partition lemma and I/O lower bounds for the FFT and matrix multiplication
records.abstract: The red-blue pebble game of Hong Jia-Wei and H. T. Kung (STOC 1981) models a computation on a directed acyclic graph run with S words of fast memory and unlimited slow memory: a red pebble on a vertex is its value held in fast memory, a blue pebble its value held in slow memory, and each load or store costs one I/O operation. This formalisation defines the game, complete calculations and the minimum I/O time Q, and proves three families of results from the paper, with explicit constants and, where the paper states one, in its asymptotic form. Q is 0 by convention where no complete calculation exists, so each statement about Q is made only where one does. First, the partition lemma (Theorem 3.1 and Lemma 3.1): every complete calculation with at most S red pebbles and q I/O operations yields a 2S-partition of the graph into h sets with q <= S h <= q + S, so that Q >= S (P(2S) - 1) wherever a complete calculation exists. Read literally, the paper's Theorem 3.1 is false in two ways, since its rules let inputs be computed free of charge and let inputs be vertices other than the sources; here, as in Elango et al. (2014), the inputs are exactly the sources and cannot be computed. Second, the n-point FFT graph, for n = 2^k with k >= 1: every S-dominator partition has h sets with n (log2 n + 1) <= h S log2(2S) (Theorem 4.1, with a per-set bound sharper than the paper's, which also closes a gap in its proof), a complete calculation exists exactly when S >= 3, and every complete calculation has q >= 2n and n log2 n <= 5 q log2 S (Corollary 4.1 with an explicit constant); Q log S = Omega(n log n) holds with one constant for all such n and all S >= 3, and P_D(S) = Omega(n log n / (S log S)) with one constant for all such n and all S >= 2. Third, matrix multiplication by the ordinary algorithm, for every graph in which the m k n products A_il B_lj are vertices of their own, each with an edge from its two factors, and no vertex can be reached from the products of two different entries of the result; for m, k, n >= 1 this class contains every independent evaluation in the paper's sense. Every complete calculation has m k n <= 2 q sqrt(S) (Corollary 6.2 with an explicit constant), and for k >= 1 also q >= mk + kn + mn; Q sqrt(S) = Omega(m k n) holds with one constant over any collection of such graphs, for every graph of the collection and every S at which that graph has a complete calculation; and for all m, k, n >= 1 some such graph has a complete calculation exactly when S >= 3. Mathlib has no pebble games, so the statements rest on twelve definitions of the formalisation's own, which the Challenge restates for the reader. Not formalised: the paper's upper bounds (its Theorem 2.1 and section 8, which it states without proof), its sections 5 and 7, and its Theorem 6.1 for general expressions.

records.title: Near-linear cycles in connected vertex-transitive graphs
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the near-linear cycle theorem in "Lovász conjecture holds asymptotically". For every positive ε, sufficiently large connected finite vertex-transitive graphs contain a simple cycle with at least n^(1−ε) edges. The development includes a weaker-constant Bondy–Locke path-to-cycle comparison and the finite approximate-group and expansion arguments used in the path proofs.

records.title: Frankl-Kupavskii-Swanepoel Theorem 3: fewer than C(d+2,2) edges embeds in R^d
records.abstract: For every integer d ≥ 4, every finite simple graph with fewer than C(d + 2, 2) edges has an injective placement in Euclidean d-space under which every edge has length 1, and the complete graph K_{d+2} has exactly C(d + 2, 2) edges and has no such placement. Equivalently, f(d) = C(d + 2, 2), where f(d) is the least number of edges in a finite simple graph with no unit-distance representation in R^d. Non-edges may also lie at distance 1. Finite simple graphs are represented as SimpleGraph (Fin n), including the empty graph. The proof is Frankl–Kupavskii–Swanepoel Theorem 3, already proved in the GraphDimension library and imported here. The spherical half of the same theorem is not stated. The question belongs to discrete geometry and extremal graph theory, specifically the study of unit-distance representations and the dimension of graphs.

records.title: Krohn–Rhodes decomposition of finite monoids into aperiodic and simple-group factors
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the Krohn–Rhodes prime decomposition theorem for finite monoids, in a form with aperiodic factors: every finite monoid M divides an iterated wreath product of finite monoids, each of which is aperiodic or a simple group, and every simple group among the factors divides M. The proof follows the local-divisor proof of Diekert, Kufleitner and Steinberg. Unlike the classical statement, the aperiodic factors are not reduced to copies of the three-element flip-flop monoid U₂; for an aperiodic M the statement holds with M as its only factor, and in general it separates the group structure of M, as simple groups dividing M, from aperiodic factors.

records.title: The 2-adic zeta value ζ₂(7) is irrational
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that the 2-adic zeta value ζ₂(7) is irrational. The theorem has no hypotheses, and its proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The value is defined through the Volkenborn integral: zeta2 s = J(s−1)/((s−1)·2^s), where J(s) is the 2-adic limit of the Riemann sums 2^(−N) Σ_{x<2^N} (x+1/2)^(−s), so zeta2 7 = J(6)/768; the theorem also proves that these limits exist. By Lemma 2.8 of Lai, Sprang and Zudilin (IMRN 2026), zeta2 s is the Kubota–Leopoldt value ζ₂(s) = L₂(s, ω^(1−s)) for s ≥ 2. That identification is cited, not formalised; it only involves a non-zero rational factor, which does not affect irrationality. ζ₂(3) and ζ₂(5) are known to be irrational, and L. Lai (Int. J. Number Theory 2025) proved that at least one of ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11), ζ₂(13) is irrational; the theorem here implies that result and the two registered formalisations of the same maintainer for {ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11)} and {ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9)}. An unrefereed draft by C. D. Long claims, by a different method, that ζ₂(s) is irrational for every odd s with 3 ≤ s ≤ 29; it is not used here, and an internal review of it (docs/long_review.md) found a gap in its large-prime step, so we do not regard it as settling the question. No refereed proof that ζ₂(7) is irrational is known to us. The proof uses the linear forms S_n = ∫ R_n'''(t+1/2−n/2) dt = ρ_n + Z_n ζ₂(7) of the rational functions R_n(t) = (2t+n) Π_{m=1}^{6} Π_{c∈C_m} (t+1/2+c) / Π_{k=0}^{n} (t+k)^(a_k), with six nested well-poised numerator blocks C_m = [η_m n, (1−η_m) n − 1], η = (5, 7, 7, 9, 11, 13)/40, and pole orders a_k ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4} that ramp up from both ends; the evaluation at the centred point t + 1/2 − n/2 leaves ζ₂(7) as the only zeta value. The 2-adic size of S_n comes from Lai's and Sprang's Δ-calculus, and the size of the coefficients from residue-level Cauchy bounds and a certified maximum of an explicit potential. The odd part of the denominators is bounded by a residue-class analysis of the partial fractions (a class lemma, a kernel identity and per-pole bounds, evaluated on local models of the residue classes whose values are certified in Lean on finitely many intervals) and the prime number theorem, proved here from a vendored Lean proof of the Wiener–Ikehara theorem. If ζ₂(7) were rational, the valuations at the auxiliary prime ℓ = 19n/20 − 1 (an idea of Lai and Sprang) would make S_n non-zero for infinitely many n, and Lai's irrationality criterion gives the contradiction. The mathematics and the Lean code were produced by AI agents under human direction and have not been refereed.

records.title: Deciding D-stability is coNP-hard
records.abstract: The computational difficulty of D-stability, raised by Chen, Fan and Yu (1995, doi:10.1016/0167-6911(94)00036-U), is addressed by an explicit integer-matrix reduction from PARTITION. For positive weights of total 2T, the construction produces a matrix of order m + 4 that is D-stable exactly when no subset has weight T. When an equal split exists, some positive diagonal scaling has an eigenvalue with strictly positive real part. A Pell recursion supplies the parameters, with a logarithmic search bound and an explicit bound on every matrix entry. These bounds give polynomial binary output length. Together with the classical NP-completeness of PARTITION, the reduction yields coNP-hardness of D-stability and D-semistability, and NP-hardness of strict D-instability, even for a four-dimensional core with attachments at one coordinate.

records.title: A critical-point criterion for D-stability in every dimension
records.abstract: Johnson's contact criterion for D-stability is expressed as an explicit principal-minor critical-point system. For every real square matrix and every choice of positive barrier weights, D-stability is equivalent to Hurwitz stability and the absence of positive solutions of the associated Fritz-John equations. The proof applies a proper exhaustion of the positive orthant to Johnson's contact variety, so that every nonempty contact set contains a critical point. In dimension five, the criterion is written explicitly as a Lagrange system and a tangency system, with coefficients given by principal minors. Both equivalences are formalized in Lean. The result applies the classical critical-point method to the characterization problem discussed by Kanovei and Logofet (1998) and Kushel (arXiv:2604.16526).

records.title: Improved sum–difference inequalities in abelian groups
records.abstract: For all finite subsets X,Y of an abelian group,  |X-Y| <= |X+Y|^λ with λ = (9451e-3286)/(5378e+787) = 1.454277448906…, less than the classical exponent 3/2. A multiscale transfer gives the upper bound (13524e-7359)/(9451e-3286) = 1.312373302115… for the Gyarmati–Hennecart–Ruzsa small-sumset exponent, less than their exponent 4/3. The proof of the first result combines a coupling with distinct differences, entropy inequalities for independent sums, a finite certificate using non-Shannon inequalities, and an explicit limiting certificate. The transfer uses localization and the Plünnecke-Ruzsa inequality over a sequence of scales.

records.title: solid-lean
records.abstract: The tower theory H is the many-sorted first-order theory of a tower of ZFC universes Z_0, Z_1, ... cut at consecutive inaccessible cardinals, with transition maps j_n identifying Z_n with the rank segment V(kappa_n) of Z_{n+1}.  H is solid in Enayat's sense.  For models M, N, P, with N interpreted in M and P interpreted in N, and an M-definable isomorphism between M and P, there is an M-definable isomorphism between M and N.  The registered statement (Palomar/Challenge.lean) writes out the many-sorted first-order logic of H from scratch, with structures, formulas, satisfaction and definability with parameters.  It states the axioms of H with Separation and Replacement as schemes over all definable classes, finitary interpretations in one-coordinate normal form (each interpreted sort is a definable subset of a single sort modulo a definable equivalence; the reduction from tuple domains is not formalized), presentations, and definable isomorphisms.  The theorem is Theorem 2.1 of the accompanying paper, "Solid idealized Lean", where it is the tower half of the bi-interpretability of an idealized Lean with H.  The proof (Palomar/Solution.lean) reduces the statement to the development's semantic solidity theorem tower_solid.

records.title: ProbStack — Random Stacking on Trees
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of a deterministic finite-path necessity theorem for graph-pebbling stackability: a positive-mass nonstackable path configuration above an explicit mass threshold must contain an actual directed integer branch message at most -h.  The package also verifies the exact fixed-total corollary at total n*mu, forcing a message at most -(2*mu-1).  The project's two-sided random path threshold theorem is not part of this Palomar result.

records.title: Local Hodge generation of sl(15) and scalar response rigidity
records.abstract: An explicit local Hodge operator on the oriented coordinate four-plane 0123, extended by zero, together with the fifteen adjoint basis actions of the orthogonal algebra for diag(1,1,1,-1,1,-1), generates sl(15,K) over every field of characteristic different from two. A finite integral commutator certificate produces signed skew matrix units and one symmetric seed; a general propagation lemma then produces all trace-free matrices. Dimension 224 follows from generation. As a consequence, an endomorphism of this algebra commuting with the commutator actions of the same sixteen generators is scalar, with determinant c^224. The proof includes characteristics three and five without a simplicity assumption. The contribution is this constructive generation-and-rigidity theorem. PDT motivates the chosen operators; assigning a physical response magnitude or gravitational coupling is outside the selected claim.

records.title: Unistationarity of Type II_l and Type V normal forms with nonnegative degradation
records.abstract: Nandan, Nghe and Unterberger (arXiv:2507.15546, Theorem 5.2 and the following remark) left uniqueness with degradation unresolved for Type II_l cores with l > 2 and, when some degradation rates vanish, for Type V cores. For the source-minimal Type II_l normal forms with l ≥ 3 and the Type V normal forms, unistationarity is established for reversible mass-action kinetics with positive forward and reverse rate constants and arbitrary nonnegative linear degradation. Any two strictly positive stationary concentration vectors coincide, including all internal species of the reversible unit chains. The Type II_l class includes separated stems and the coincident three-fork case. The proof combines passive-chain elimination and a ratio argument for Type V with boundary Jacobian nonsingularity and an implicit-function argument for Type II_l.

records.title: FKS Problem 2 in dimension three
records.abstract: A Lean-checked proof of the d = 3 case of FKS Problem 2: for every simple graph G on seven vertices, G or its complement has an injective placement in Euclidean three-space under which every edge has length 1. Non-edges are unconstrained and may also have length 1. The full question, for graphs on 2d + 1 vertices in dimension d, is stated and marked open. In the notation of Alon and Kupavskii, the proved case gives f_D(7) ≤ 3; together with the published lower bound it implies f_D(7) = 3. The formal target is the seven-vertex disjunction, not a definition or equality for f_D. The research audience is discrete geometers and extremal graph theorists studying unit-distance representations, graph dimension and distance Ramsey questions.

records.title: Unconstrained detection of productive autocatalytic cores is NP-complete
records.abstract: Kosc, Kuperberg, Rajon and Charlat (PNAS 122, e2421274122, 2025, Section 2.1) left open the complexity of detecting an autocatalytic core without a prescribed target species or allowed-food set. For finite reversible reaction networks with literal nonnegative integer reactant and product matrices, this unconstrained detection problem is proved NP-complete. A core is a nonempty entity/reaction pair, minimal under componentwise inclusion, with a selected reactant and product in every selected reaction and a signed real flow that strictly produces every selected entity. The input uses a canonical binary encoding. NP membership and a total polynomial-time many-one reduction from SAT are formalized using Complexitylib’s multi-tape Turing machines, including the Cook–Levin theorem.

records.title: FKS Problem 1 on at most twice the dimension vertices
records.abstract: A Lean-checked proof of FKS Problem 1 for graphs on at most 2d vertices, for every d ≥ 4: every finite simple graph of maximum degree at most d with no connected component isomorphic to K_{d+1} has an injective placement in Euclidean d-space, with every vertex of norm 1/√2 and every edge at distance exactly 1. Non-edges are unconstrained and may also have length 1. The unrestricted question is false at d = 4: Mishra and Senthilkumar (2026) showed that the square of the nine-cycle, on 2d + 1 = 9 vertices, has no such placement. The bound proved here is therefore sharp at d = 4. Neither result settles the question restricted to d ≥ 5. The exception is interpreted componentwise: a K_{d+1} component already precludes such a placement even when other components are present. The research audience is discrete geometers and extremal graph theorists studying spherical unit-distance representations, graph dimension and bounded-degree embedding problems.

records.title: Black-Scholes pricing via Girsanov change of measure
records.abstract: Formal proof of the time-zero Black-Scholes formula for a European call on any strong solution of the geometric Brownian motion SDE, with positive initial price, strike, volatility and maturity, and constant drift and interest rate. The change of measure uses the constant-drift case of the general predictable (dynamic) Girsanov theorem. The discounted stopped asset is a martingale under one fixed terminal measure, and the call-payoff expectation equals the closed-form Black-Scholes expression.

records.title: Linear independence of 1, ζ(2), ζ(3) over ℚ
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the linear independence of 1, ζ(2) and ζ(3) over ℚ. The proof is inspired by A. Fauzan's work on the irrationality of ζ(5) and builds on the Lean formalization of the irrationality of Li₂(1/2), registered in Palomar as PALOMAR-2026-09-30-000013. It shows that the method of that proof can be pushed further. The main difference from the Li₂(1/2) proof is that the rational functions appearing here are allowed to have poles of order two. The remaining details are similar, with some minor modifications. The compared theorems depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and on nothing else, and there is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean.

records.title: Evertse 1984: sums of S-units and linear recurrences
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the whole of J.-H. Evertse, On sums of S-units and linear recurrences (Compositio Math. 53 (1984)), built on the repository's libraries ArithmeticHeights and DiophantineApproximation, whose p-adic Subspace Theorem (Schlickewei's, the paper's Theorem 4) it uses. The library Evertse1984 is sorry-free and within Lean's three standard axioms. It proves Theorem 2 (a lower bound for S-integral sums without vanishing subsums, at any set of places), Theorem 1 (finitely many admissible projective solutions of x₀ + ⋯ + xₙ = 0), Corollaries 1 and 2, Lemmas 1 and 2 (polynomial values and shifted polynomial quotients that are S-units), Theorem 3 (for a non-degenerate linear recurrence with at least two characteristic roots, the largest prime ideal norm of u_r / u_s tends to infinity), and Corollaries 3 and 4 (P(u_r) → ∞; u_r = u_s has finitely many solutions r ≠ s). It also compares the paper's cited Theorem 4, the repository's p-adic Subspace Theorem. Fourteen statements are compared.

records.title: Embedding countable groups into groups of type FP_n
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of Theorem A: every countable group embeds in a group of type FP_n over the integers for each finite n >= 2. The proof uses a 23-index, 15-triple Fano-plane construction to supply the finite input to geometric, homological, and relative Leary arguments. It does not assert the existence of one FP_infty overgroup.

records.title: Pascal Extremes
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalisation of sharp p-adic extremal behaviour for the restricted binomial gcd G(N;m) = gcd{C(N,k) : 0 < k < N, m divides k}. For every prime p and m >= 2 with p not dividing m, it proves that the maximum of v_p(G(N;m)) over admissible rows is the least r >= 1 with m < p^r, with constructive attainment proved before the least extremal row T is used. It then proves, for every prime p and a >= 2, the exact least-row formula T_p(p^a+1) = p^(3a)+1.

records.title: Formalization of a discrete Carleson theorem of Stein-Wainger type
records.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem of the papers arXiv:1907.00405 and arXiv:2107.14616 by Ben Krause and Joris Roos. The result concerns l^p boundedness for a  discrete maximal singular oscillatory operator of Stein-Wainger type, also called a discrete Carleson operator.

records.title: Metric–Pfaffian Stabilizers and Fixed-Hodge Field Recovery
records.abstract: For the explicit bivector metric induced by diag(1,1,1,-1,1,-1) and the Pfaffian cubic on fifteen real coordinates, the joint infinitesimal stabilizer is exactly the uniquely parameterized fifteen-dimensional orthogonal adjoint span. Under the metric condition, ninety specified cubic derivative checks certify preservation at every point. Within the joint stabilizer, commutation with a displayed local Lorentz Hodge operator is equivalent to annihilating its complementary reference and yields a unique six-plus-one decomposition, of dimension seven. Within this fixed-Hodge space, exactly the complementary line acts trivially on all extracted four-plane fields; six specified scalar readings reconstruct the entire visible action. The contribution is the explicit constructive classification and recovery certificates, situated in classical Pfaffian-preserver theory. The metric, cubic and four-plane are supplied data. PDT motivates the construction; selecting a physical coupling is outside these claims.

records.title: A complete crystalline-measure space of countably infinite Hamel dimension
records.abstract: There exists a locally finite set Λ in the real line such that the complete complex vector space of tempered distributions locally given by atomic measures on Λ, whose distributional Fourier transforms are also locally atomic on Λ, has Hamel dimension ℵ₀. A countable family gives a unique finite linear expansion of every admissible distribution, and every finite expansion is admissible. The theorem includes the equivalence between a Schwartz-vanishing-ideal definition and the local atomic formulas on both Fourier sides. Temperedness is distributional; no additional polynomial total-variation bound is assumed. This is an exhaustive occurrence result for one constructed carrier, not a classification of arbitrary carriers.

records.title: Amenability of Lie, group and Hopf algebras
records.abstract: Formalization of 18 claims from manuscript Theorems A, B, C, E (extension direction), F, G, H (hierarchy inclusions and characteristic-zero strictness), I, and J. The claims include coalgebraic rounding, algebraic and coalgebraic amenability, Hopf-module quotients, cleft extensions, group and Lie applications, and augmentation-associated graded amenability. Every selected claim is proved without unformalized literature inputs or project-local axioms. Theorem D, the equivalence form of E, and arbitrary-characteristic strictness in H remain in the library but are excluded from the submission.

records.title: A two-reaction counterexample to the gross-amplification affinity bound
records.abstract: Despons, De Decker and Lacoste (https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02366, conjecture following Eq. (33)) proposed that the affinity at maximum production flux is bounded below by the logarithm of the gross amplification ratio in seed-dependent autocatalytic networks. A two-species reversible mass-action counterexample is given by X ⇌ Y with forward/reverse rates (3, 2) and 2Y ⇌ 2X + Y with rates (7, 6). On the positive Y-stationary set, the production current has its unique global maximum at (X, Y) = (1, 1). At this point the exponential of the overall affinity is 7/4, strictly below the gross amplification ratio 2. The network has positive rates, an invertible net stoichiometric matrix, unit production mode and a positive detailed-balance state. The formal theorem establishes the counterexample; the correspondence with the published conjecture is supplied by the witness’s stationary branch and reactant matrix, together with the source’s affinity and chemostat conventions.

records.title: A Short Proof of Ball's Plank Theorem
records.abstract: Formalization in Lean 4 of the paper 'A Short Proof of Ball's Plank Theorem' by Arseniy Akopyan and Alexander Polyanskii (arXiv:2609.36163). The paper gives a short proof of Keith Ball's 1991 theorem: if a centrally symmetric convex body in R^d is covered by finitely many planks, the sum of their relative widths with respect to the body is at least 1. The proof is based on a simple proof of a core theorem about linear functionals on R^n and an orthonormal basis. It also yields a short proof of Davenport's problem for centrally symmetric convex bodies (interior-disjointness of a homothet K/(n+1) from n hyperplanes).

records.title: Greedy Uniformity on Trees
records.abstract: Formalization of exact distributional results for the random-permutation greedy maximal-independent-set process on finite trees. For every finite nonempty tree, the complete greedy output law is uniform over maximal independent sets exactly for K1 and K2. For the mixed-spider family T_{k,l}, the development counts maximal independent sets, proves exact output probabilities, and for l=2^k-k proves positive total-variation bias with decay O(sqrt(k)/4^k), equivalently O(sqrt(log n_k)/n_k^2) along n_k=2^k+k+1. The Stage-4 novelty classification is "plausibly new with bounded uncertainty"; no worldwide-priority, global-optimality, matching lower-bound, all-n extremal, or other stronger claim is made.

records.title: minimax-theorem-lean
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of von Neumann's 1928 finite two-player zero-sum minimax theorem, a foundation of modern game theory and a cornerstone of mathematical economics. Nash equilibrium existence builds directly on its mixed-strategy solution concept by extending equilibrium existence beyond the two-player zero-sum case; this is historical motivation, not a claimed Lean proof of Nash's theorem. The formal result is Minimax.minimax_theorem {A B : Type*} [Fintype A] [Fintype B] [Nonempty A] [Nonempty B] (u : A → B → ℝ) : maxminValue u = minmaxValue u. The reported Palomar registry API search on 2026-09-29 for "minimax" returned zero entries. The M1 Mathlib survey found no finite zero-sum game specialization in the pinned Mathlib, whose general Sion saddle-point theorem is reused here.

records.title: Local conjugacy in prosolvable groups
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of all eleven numbered results and both counterexamples in Local conjugacy in prosolvable groups, arXiv:2609.37678v1. Closed supplements of a pronilpotent normal subgroup are conjugate exactly when locally conjugate under the stated structural hypotheses. Continuous nonabelian cohomology has the stated primary restriction decomposition. Local inclusion and fixed-point results, the GL(2,3) quaternion counterexample, and the order-162 Heisenberg wreath-product counterexample are formalized.

records.title: Discriminative Kalman Filter Formalized
records.abstract: Asymptotic correctness of the discriminative Kalman filter for a stationary linear Gaussian state model with nonlinear and non-Gaussian observations. Formalizes Appendix B, Theorem 2, Lemma 1, and Remarks 1–4 of Burkhart et al. (2020): weak convergence, eventual Gaussian well-definedness, L1 consistency, the exact Gaussian parameter update, the robust update, and the extension to random input distributions with convergence in probability.

records.title: bulow-klemperer-lean
records.abstract: A Lean proof that a no-reserve second-price auction with one additional independent bidder has at least the expected revenue of the optimal normalized BIC auction under a regular common value distribution.

records.title: roberts-theorem-lean
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of Roberts theorem: for finite nonempty agent and alternative types with at least three alternatives, every onto dominant-strategy incentive compatible choice function is an affine maximizer. The proof follows the modular route: the taxation principle and weak monotonicity, reduction to strong monotonicity by tie-breaking, no-veto-power range analysis, the two-agent affine price representation, and induction on the number of agents.

records.title: vcg-mechanism-lean
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the Green-Laffont characterization: for finite, nonempty agent and alternative types, efficiency and dominant-strategy incentive compatibility imply that payments have Groves form. The project also verifies four standard properties of the finite VCG mechanism with Clarke pivot payments.

records.title: gleason-finite-lean
records.abstract: A machine-checked proof of Gleason's theorem in finite dimensions. On a complex Hilbert space of dimension at least 3, every frame function on the orthogonal projections has the form P ↦ Re Tr(ρP) for exactly one density operator ρ. The statement is Kim Morrison's lean-eval problem gleason_theorem_finite, unchanged. The proof follows Cooke, Keane and Moran's elementary proof of Gleason's core lemma for matrices on ℂᴺ, then moves the result to operators by taking matrices in an orthonormal basis.

records.title: revenue-equivalence-lean
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of Myerson's 1981 revenue equivalence theorem in a single-parameter Bayesian mechanism-design model with continuous real types. The formal result is RevenueEquivalence.Palomar.revenueEquivalence (X P1 P2 : ℝ → ℝ) (h1 : BIC X P1) (h2 : BIC X P2) (hU : interimUtility X P1 0 = interimUtility X P2 0) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) : P1 t = P2 t: two Bayesian incentive-compatible mechanisms with the same interim allocation rule and the same interim utility at the reference type (type zero) charge the same interim payments at every nonnegative type. Types range over all of ℝ; there is no lowest type, and zero is only the normalization point for the payment identity. The envelope lemma RevenueEquivalence.Palomar.envelope_integral and the expected-revenue corollary RevenueEquivalence.Palomar.expectedRevenueEqual are proved alongside; the corollary requires both interim payment rules to be integrable with respect to the prior ((hInt1 : Integrable P1 μ) (hInt2 : Integrable P2 μ)), so its conclusion is an equality of finite expected revenues rather than a vacuous totalized-integral identity. The Palomar registry API search on 2026-10-01 for "revenue equivalence" returned zero entries; the queries "Myerson" and "auction" returned only different theorems (see related_formalizations note). These are dated, limited observations, not universal prior-art claims.

records.title: Myerson's Optimal Auction Theorem
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of Myerson's 1981 optimal auction theorem, regular case, in a single-parameter independent-private-values model with real types. Finitely many bidders draw independent types from TypeDist priors: probability measures on ℝ with a continuous monotone CDF and a nonnegative Lebesgue density that vanishes for negative types, so each prior's mass lies on [0, ∞). The formal results are MyersonOptimalAuction.Palomar.virtualSurplusIdentity: under BIC, the support hypothesis (hsupp : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → 0 < D.F t, i.e. the prior puts positive mass in (0, t] for every t > 0 so zero is in the support), and five integrability hypotheses, the expected payment equals the expected virtual surplus minus the interim utility at the reference type (type zero), expectedPayment p D = expectedVirtualSurplus x D - interimUtility x p 0; and MyersonOptimalAuction.Palomar.optimalAuction: for regular priors (hreg : Regular D, i.e. each bidder's virtual value ψ(t) = t - (1 - F t) / f t is nondecreasing on nonnegative types), the auction that allocates the item to the least-index bidder attaining the highest virtual value whenever that value is strictly positive (no sale otherwise), with envelope payments normalized to zero utility at type zero, is Bayesian incentive compatible and interim individually rational, and raises at least as much expected revenue as any feasible BIC and interim-IR mechanism. Independence is the product measure over type profiles; feasibility is pointwise (∑ i, X i t ≤ 1 for every profile t). Types range over all of ℝ; zero is only the reference/normalization type, never a lowest type. The Bochner integrals defining expectations are totalized, so every expectation claim carries the integrability hypotheses that make it non-vacuous. Ironing for irregular distributions is out of scope. The Palomar registry API searches on 2026-10-01 for "optimal auction", "virtual surplus", and "virtual value" returned no existing Myerson optimal auction formalization ("optimal auction" matched only PALOMAR-2026-10-01-000007, Bulow-Klemperer, a different theorem). These are dated, limited observations, not universal prior-art claims.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Pointwise provable equality and the failure of composition
records.abstract: In their study of pathologies in recursion categories, Montagna (1989) and Di Paola–Montagna (1991) introduce the algebraic systems S′ and S′_T, respectively, and claim that they are categories. We show that the proposed composition is not independent of the choice of representatives. For every consistent recursively enumerable extension T of Peano arithmetic (PA), we exhibit two unary programs whose partial functions are provably equal in T, separately at each standard input. Composing each after a program that searches for a T-proof of contradiction and returns its code yields programs that are not equivalent in this sense. An alternative proof uses the productivity of the complement of the diagonal halting set. Montagna's S′ is the case T = PA. More generally, for consistent T ⊇ PA, pointwise provable equality is a composition congruence exactly when T proves every true Π⁰₁ sentence, in which case it is extensional equality. This completeness condition fails for every consistent recursively enumerable T ⊇ PA by Gödel's second incompleteness theorem. For every extension T ⊇ PA, the least composition congruence containing pointwise provable equality is extensional equality if T is Σ⁰₁-sound and the universal relation otherwise.

records.title: Counting recurrences for the permutation classes Av(1342) and Av(12453)
records.abstract: For a permutation pattern τ, let Av_n(τ) be the set of permutations of length n that avoid τ.  This formalization proves, for every n, that four recurrences from the source paper compute |Av_n(1342)| and |Av_n(12453)|. For 1342 they are the one-threshold recurrence W and the scalar kernel recurrence G, and for 12453 the literal two-threshold recurrence H and the transfer-kernel recurrence G.  These are the cases d = 1 and d = 2 of the paper's counting recurrences for the classes Av(12...d ⊕ 231), the direct sum of an increasing pattern and 231, whose kernel form gives polynomial-time algorithms for every fixed d (the complexity bounds themselves are not formalized).  The counting sequence of Av(1342) has been known since Bóna (1997).  That of Av(12453) was previously known only up to n = 38, from a program of Biers-Ariel that evaluates the recurrence H, and the paper uses its kernel algorithm to compute it up to n = 150 (that computation is not formalized).

records.title: Gale's Top Trading Cycles (Shapley-Scarf Housing Market)
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of Gale's top trading cycles algorithm (1974) for the Shapley-Scarf housing market. Finitely many agents (Fin n) each own exactly one house (the endowment is a bijection endow : Fin n ≃ Fin n) and have strict preferences over houses, given most-preferred-first as per-agent permutations rank i : Fin n ≃ Fin n; agent i strictly prefers house a over house b iff (rank i).symm a < (rank i).symm b. The comparator-checked results are TTC.Palomar.ttcTerminates: the TTC procedure (each remaining agent points to the owner of their favourite remaining house, each house points to its owner; each round removes the single directed cycle reachable from a chosen remaining agent, whose members trade and leave) removes every agent within n rounds, since each round deletes at least one nonempty directed cycle from the finite functional pointing graph. This one-cycle-at-a-time form computes the same allocation as the simultaneous version (see the remark in README.md); TTC.Palomar.ttcInCore: the TTC allocation is in the ordinary core, i.e. no coalition S can reallocate its own endowments (Set.BijOn y S (M.endow '' S)) so that every member strictly prefers the deviation; TTC.Palomar.ttcUniqueStrictCore: strict-core uniqueness, i.e. for (x : Fin n → Fin n) with (hxb : Function.Bijective x) and (hx : StrictCore M x) the conclusion is x = ttcAllocation M. This is uniqueness among bijective strict-core allocations (no coalition can weakly block), not a singleton claim about the ordinary core. The library also proves the TTC allocation Pareto optimal (TTC.ttcPareto), individually rational (TTC.ttcIR), in the strict core (TTC.ttcInStrictCore), and strategyproof (TTC.ttcStrategyproof, Roth 1982: no unilateral misreport is profitable); these four are library-only and are not on the comparator surface. The Palomar registry API was searched on 2026-10-01 for "top trading cycles", "housing market", "shapley scarf", "TTC", and "trading cycles" and returned no existing TTC formalization among 397 entries; this is a dated, limited observation, not a universal prior-art claim.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Rochet's Cyclic-Monotonicity Characterization
records.abstract: For any nonempty report type T, any outcome type X, any real-valued valuation v : T -> X -> Real and allocation f : T -> X, DSIC payments exist exactly when every finite closed walk has nonnegative sum of weights l(s,t) = v(t,f(t)) - v(t,f(s)). The proof constructs payments as the infimum of finite path weights from a fixed anchor. Direct edges establish nonemptiness; a return edge supplies an explicit real lower bound before using the infimum's order properties. The payments are zero at the anchor and satisfy every implementing difference inequality. The characterization also holds for arbitrary agents with heterogeneous nonempty report spaces and decidable agent equality, by fixing other reports and assembling anchored slice payments. A three-type example satisfies all two-cycle inequalities but has a negative three-cycle and admits no DSIC payment.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: A nontrivial critical window for RAF emergence in the binary polymer model
records.abstract: Hordijk and Steel (https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.03919, Section 7, Eq. (21)) conjectured a zero-one threshold for RAF emergence at linear mean catalysis. In the uniform reversible binary-polymer model with split-position reaction identities and food consisting of monomers and dimers, a nontrivial limiting law is established. Each molecule independently catalyzes each reaction, with one catalysis coordinate shared by both directions. If the mean catalysis parameter f(n) satisfies f(n)/n → λ > 0, the probability of a reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated (RAF) set converges to L(λ). The function L is continuous and nondecreasing, with 0 < L(λ) ≤ 1 − exp(−36λ) < 1. Thus no finite positive threshold separates limiting RAF probability zero from one in this model.

records.title: An Exponent of 1.043 for the Unit Distance Problem: Lean formalization at exponent 1.04315, conditional on one zeta inequality
records.abstract: Lean formalization accompanying the paper An Exponent of 1.043 for the Unit Distance Problem by Eric Naslund (cited under sources), which proves the exponent 1.043171 unconditionally with a computer-assisted certificate. Conditional theorem on unit distances in the Euclidean plane. Let B = Q(sqrt 241) and let E be the number field of degree 512 generated over Q by sqrt 241 and square roots of the eight elements -1, -71011068 + 4574225 sqrt 241, (-6101 - 393 sqrt 241)/2, (6101 - 393 sqrt 241)/2, 31 - 2 sqrt 241, 31 + 2 sqrt 241, 326 - 21 sqrt 241 and 326 + 21 sqrt 241 of B (a basis of the {2,3,5}-units of B modulo squares). Let E_W be the field of degree 8192 obtained from E by adjoining square roots of four explicit elements beta_1, ..., beta_4 of E, each generating with two of the square roots a dihedral extension of B of degree 8 (the elements are written out in the Challenge). Hypothesis (H_W) is one displayed numerical inequality for the Dedekind zeta function of E_W: log(Re zeta_{E_W}(1 + 1/4411))/8192 + (1/4411)((L - gamma - log(4 pi))/4 - Re((zeta_{E_W}'/zeta_{E_W})(2))/8192) < 50969/1000000, where L = (9/4) log 2 + (1/2) log 3615 and gamma is Euler's constant. The compared theorem proves that (H_W) implies the existence of finite sets U_j in the plane with |U_j| -> infinity such that the number of unordered pairs of points of U_j at distance one, divided by |U_j|^(20863/20000), tends to infinity. The exponent is exactly 20863/20000 = 1.04315. The conclusion is a sequence statement only; no bound at every sufficiently large cardinality is asserted. The infinite pro-2 tower over B with Frobenius caps at both primes above 29 and at one prime above 41 (generators, relation bound, presentation, Golod-Shafarevich infinitude, local data), its fields, which are Galois over B and over a fixed base field but not over Q, their local types and signature, the root-discriminant bound, the field E_W with its degree, its embedding in the base field and its local data, the passage from (H_W) to the analytic ceiling, the numerical margin and the planar construction are proved in Lean over Mathlib; (H_W) itself is not proved. Outside Lean, a rigorous computation (certified values of the 576 L-functions of degrees 4 and 8 in the factorization of zeta_{E_W} and an Euler product with explicit tail) bounds the left side of (H_W) by 0.0509172; that computation is not part of the formal proof. The earlier formalization registered as PALOMAR-2026-10-01-000018 version 1 proved the exponent 10427/10000 from a different inequality, for the field E.

records.title: Border's Finite Auction Feasibility Theorem
records.abstract: For arbitrary finite bidders with heterogeneous finite type spaces, a nonnegative normalized real joint prior, and an interim allocation rule with values in [0,1], a randomized allocation of at most one item realizes the weighted interim masses if and only if every collection of bidder-specific type subsets satisfies Border's union-probability inequality. Weighted feasibility is proved equivalent to conditional feasibility on positive marginal support. Null-type interim values remain unrestricted within [0,1]. For a product of nonnegative normalized distributions, the independent-prior corollary has right side 1 minus the product of the complementary marginal probabilities. Full real-valued sufficiency is proved by finite threshold decomposition and compact convex separation; no sufficiency oracle is assumed.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Linnik's constant is at most 3.99: A formalization of a weighted version of Heath-Brown's near-density estimate, and of the proof's certificate checker
records.abstract: Two components of the proof, in the paper "Linnik's constant is at most 3.99" (paper/linnik399.pdf in this repository), that every reduced residue class modulo q contains a prime below q^3.99 for all large q. That bound itself is NOT formally verified here: the paper's zero-location arguments, case analysis and exterior regimes have conventional proofs and computer checks only. (1) The graded near lemma: fix test data (a detector f satisfying Heath-Brown's Condition 1, a Gram test g satisfying his Conditions 1 and 2, a Selberg-sieve weight with heights h_k >= 0 on cells [t_k, t_{k+1}) with t_0 > 1/3 + 2 eps', finitely many nonnegative anchor offsets, a positive lower bound for the weight omega where f is nonzero, and I_B > 0) and eta > 0. For all large q, take a finite family of entries (chi_j, gamma_j, delta_j) of non-principal characters mod q with heights |gamma_j| <= T <= (log q)/3 and a safe anchor at height 2T+1, whose characters are pairwise distinct whenever some sieve height h_k is nonzero (condition (iii) of the paper's Theorem 8.4; without sieve weights a character may repeat, and repeated characters enter through the pair excess e_j). Then the prime-sum responses satisfy (sum_j a_j R_j)_+^2 <= (1+eta) I_B [sum_j (D(delta_j) - d_1 + e_j) a_j^2 + (d_1 + eta)(sum_j a_j)^2] for all a_j >= 0. This is a weighted version of Heath-Brown's Lemma 12.1 (1992), which Heath-Brown remarks (section 16, item 9) no neat way of achieving "seems available". Its zero form: the response lemma (a response is bounded below by the zeros it keeps, via the local explicit formula), the threshold form exists tau: sum_j (v_j - tau)_+^2 / D_j <= 1 - tau^2/d with features computed from kept zeros, provided every diagonal numerator D(delta_j) - d_1 + e_j is positive, the entry bounds F(hi - s_j) of the rows, the normalization used by the leaf builders, and the vanishing of the pair excess for separated same-character pairs. (2) The leaf LPs: an exact integer checker for the certificates of the leaf linear programs (bisection trees over threshold boxes, first-order and tangent relaxations with safe rounding, exclusions, weak duality with a free dual) is proved sound: if it accepts a certificate with value v, every feasible point of the LP has objective at most v < 10^16. A bridge lemma turns the threshold form into the LP's near rows. Seven certificates (six leaves of the 3.99 corpus and the program of the large first-zero range) are checked by the kernel (decide +kernel) in the repository (not part of the compared theorems). The analytic part is conditional on four published estimates, stated as explicit hypotheses in the Challenge, each no stronger than its source: Xylouris's Lemmas 3.1 and 3.2 (= Heath-Brown's Lemmas 5.3 and 5.2), Burgess's character-sum bound with k = 3 as printed for primitive characters (Heath-Brown's Lemma 2.1; the form for all non-principal characters is derived), and Graham's asymptotic for Selberg-sieve sums. Mertens' estimate, Abel and partial summation, the Selberg majorant, the decay of Laplace transforms, the finiteness and multiplicities of zeros in a disc, the equality of multiplicities of conjugate zeros for real characters, and all error bookkeeping are proved.

records.title: On Graham's rearrangement conjecture (Pham–Sauermann)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of H. T. Pham and L. Sauermann, "On Graham's rearrangement conjecture" (arXiv:2602.15797v1). Graham conjectured in 1971 that for every prime p, every subset S of Z_p \ {0} has an ordering whose partial sums are pairwise distinct. The formalization proves the paper's main theorem (Theorem 1.2): for every 0 < α < 1 there is a constant C_α > 0 such that, for every prime p, every S ⊆ Z_p \ {0} with C_α ≤ |S| ≤ p^(1-α) has such an ordering. It also proves the paper's anticoncentration bounds for the sum of a uniformly random m-element subset R of a set S ⊆ Z_p with |S| ≥ 2: the probability that the sum of R equals any given z is at most 1/p + C/(|S|√m), for an absolute constant C > 0, when C log|S| ≤ m ≤ 10^-3 |S|/log|S| (Theorem 1.3), and, for every 0 < ε < 1, at most 1/p + C_ε √(log|S|)/(|S|√m) for every positive integer m ≤ (1-ε)|S| (Corollary 1.4). Every result that the paper proves is formalized, following its argument, and so are the two hypergeometric tail bounds that its proofs take from the Chernoff bound of Janson, Łuczak and Ruciński.

records.title: Optimal packings of one to seven unit squares in a disk
records.abstract: For n = 1, …, 7: the least radius of a closed disk holding n unit squares with disjoint interiors, each placed and rotated freely, and every packing that attains it. The radii are √2/2, √5/2, 5√17/16, √2, √(5/2), √q* ≈ 1.68854 and √13/2, where q* is a quartic irrational. Up to rotation about the disk centre and relabelling, the optimal packing is unique for n ≤ 6: the square, the 2 × 1 rectangle, the T, the 2 × 2 block, the plus, and for six squares a central square with four neighbours, two of them pushed along its sides, and a sixth square turned by π/4 between those two. For n = 7 the optimal packings form a three-parameter family: two columns of two squares and, between them, a column of three whose heights vary independently, at least 1 apart and within √3 − 1/2 of the disk centre. The proofs for three to six squares bound the arcs the squares occupy on a small circle about the disk centre. For six squares this finds the square that contains the disk centre; five fixed points label the others, and a weighted sum of separating inequalities, with estimates uniform in the angles of the squares, forces the optimal radius. For seven squares, each square avoiding the disk centre gets a direction from it, and in the optimal disk two disjoint such squares get directions at least π/3 apart. We found no earlier proof for five, six or seven squares, and no exact one for three, where a computer-assisted enclosure of the radius and the optimal arrangements was known. Four squares, uniqueness included, were settled by hand in 2026, by the same idea as here.

records.title: Cremer-McLean Full Surplus Extraction Theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the Cremer-McLean full surplus extraction theorem (Econometrica, 1988): for a single indivisible object with finitely many bidders, finite type spaces, and a correlated joint prior with full support, if every bidder's family of conditional distributions over the others' types is convex independent (no conditional lies in the convex hull of the rest), then there exists a Bayesian incentive compatible, interim individually rational direct mechanism that allocates ex post efficiently and extracts the full surplus: every bidder's interim expected utility is zero, so expected seller revenue equals the expected maximum value. The proof hinges on constructing side-bet lotteries with zero own-conditional expectation and strictly positive cross-conditional expectation, obtained by strict separation of each conditional from the convex hull of the others, scaled to dominate any misreport gain.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: The Herzog–Schönheim conjecture for solvable groups
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the Herzog–Schönheim conjecture (the index form, which implies the cardinality form asked in Erdős problem 274) for every solvable group, finite or infinite: if a solvable group is partitioned into finitely many, and at least two, left cosets of subgroups, then two of the subgroups have the same index (hence, in the cardinality form, the same cardinality). The conjecture for arbitrary groups is open and is not claimed. The infinite case reduces to a finite solvable quotient by the common core of the parts; the finite case is proved for a least counterexample by considering its largest prime divisor p, using the subgroup generated by the p-prime-part elements, divisibility restrictions on local indices obtained from fixed-point counts in a primitive solvable quotient, and an extra closure argument at p = 7. The statements use the same exact covering structure as the formal-conjectures file for Erdős problem 274.

records.title: maskin-nash-implementation-lean
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of Maskin's theorem on Nash implementation: necessity of Maskin monotonicity and sufficiency of monotonicity plus no-veto power via the canonical mechanism. Alternatives form a finite nonempty type, agents are indexed by Fin n, preferences are complete preorders, and the social choice correspondence is nonempty-valued. Sufficiency requires at least three agents; implementation is in pure strategies.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: agv-mechanism-lean
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the AGV (d'Aspremont-Gérard-Varet-Arrow) expected-externality mechanism: with independent types, ex post efficiency, Bayesian incentive compatibility, and budget balance are jointly attainable. Agents are indexed by Fin n with 2 ≤ n; each agent has a finite nonempty type space with an independent PMF prior; alternatives form a finite nonempty type; values are private. The efficient rule xmax maximizes utilitarian welfare, and agvTransfer pays each agent its expected externality minus an equal share of the other agents' receipts. Interim individual rationality is not claimed.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Finite Bayes Correlated Equilibrium, Information Expansions and Information Order
records.abstract: Bergemann–Morris Theorem 1 for arbitrary finite players and states with heterogeneous action and original-signal spaces: a normalized decision rule is obedient if and only if a finite marginal-preserving information expansion supports a valid mixed Bayes–Nash strategy profile inducing its joint law. The recommendation expansion and the converse for arbitrary extra signals and independent behavioral randomization are proved. Null fibers are handled without conditioning, and exact induction is equivalent to the paper's positive-support quotient. Zero prior masses are permitted, extending the paper's full-support assumption. The one-player decision-problem specialization and explicit examples are included. Theorem 2 proves that individual sufficiency is equivalent to BCE outcome inclusion across all finite basic games with arbitrary heterogeneous actions and utilities and full-support common priors, on a nonempty finite state space. Its converse constructs actual couplings from finite quadratic-scoring games and weighted compactness.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Optimality, uniqueness and stability of Gerver's sofa from one coercive certificate, formalized in Lean 4
records.abstract:
The moving sofa problem asks for the largest area of a planar shape that can be moved around the right-angled corner of a hallway of unit width. Jineon Baek proved (arXiv:2411.19826) that Gerver's sofa G, of area 2.2195..., is optimal. His proof bounds the area of every large moving sofa by a concave functional Q of a triple (K, B, D) of convex bodies built from a cap K of the sofa, and shows that Q is largest at Gerver's triple, where it equals |G|.

This entry proves one estimate for Q, the coercive certificate, and derives three results from it. On an enlarged domain of triples, on which the cap need not satisfy Baek's injectivity condition, Q(K, B, D) <= |G|, and the cap K lies within Euclidean Hausdorff distance 2 sec(phi) sqrt(|G| - Q(K, B, D)) of the horizontal translate of Gerver's cap with the same leftmost point, where phi = 0.039... is Gerver's angle. The proof writes |G| - Q as a sum of nonnegative terms, and the energy terms among them also bound that distance. The bound is attained: Gerver's triple lies in the enlarged domain, and Q equals |G| there.

From the certificate: optimality, Baek's theorem, proved without his Theorem 1.1.1 and without the balance argument of his Chapters 4 to 6; uniqueness, every moving sofa with the area of G is mapped onto G by a rotation and a translation (a translation suffices); and stability, after a translation a moving sofa of area |G| - epsilon lies within Euclidean Hausdorff distance C sqrt(epsilon) of G, their symmetric difference has area at most C' sqrt(epsilon), its rotation angle misses a right angle by at most C'' epsilon, and the exponent 1/2 cannot be improved. The Challenge also states the correspondence between Baek's definitions and those of Google DeepMind's formal-conjectures, and formal-conjectures' statements, among them the uniqueness, which it lists as open; here they are proved through the certificate.

Versions 1 to 4 of this entry registered the formalization of Baek's paper with a first proof of uniqueness that uses his Theorem 1.1.1; they state the same optimality, uniqueness and formal-conjectures theorems, proved through Baek's argument, and the repository keeps their Challenge and Solution in baek/. This version proves those theorems through the certificate and adds the certificate and the stability. A script in the repository, scripts/AuditCoerciveRoute.lean, run by the continuous integration, checks that its proofs reach neither Baek's Theorem 1.1.1, nor the results of his balance argument, nor the main theorem and the equality analysis of the first proof of uniqueness.

records.title: Anomalous diffusion by fractal homogenization
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of S. Armstrong and V. Vicol, "Anomalous diffusion by fractal homogenization" (arXiv:2305.05048). For every alpha in (0, 1/3) it constructs one divergence-free, Z^2-periodic drift b in C^0_t C^{0,alpha}_x intersect C^{0,alpha}_t C^0_x on [0,1] x T^2, and proves three properties of the advection-diffusion equation with this drift: anomalous dissipation of scalar variance for every mean-zero H^1 datum (Theorem 1.1 of the paper); a uniform C^{0,mu}([0,1]; L^2) bound by C times the H^1 norm of the datum along a set of diffusivities accumulating at zero (Remark r.LeBron.2); and non-uniqueness of vanishing-diffusivity limits for a class of data containing cos(2 pi n x_1) for infinitely many n (a corrected form of the paper's no-selection principle). The three properties are combined in one theorem, restated in a Mathlib-only comparator challenge. The formalization also proves existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and the classical facts the paper uses without proof.

records.title: Finite Bayesian-to-Dominant-Strategy Equivalence
records.abstract: Finite Gershkov–Goeree–Kushnir–Moldovanu–Shi (2013) Theorem 2 for arbitrary finite agents and alternatives, heterogeneous ordered finite scalar type supports, arbitrary independent positive support masses, and linear private values with nonnegative slopes and arbitrary constants. The library constructs a feasible dominant-strategy mechanism preserving every support type's interim expected utility and ex ante social surplus. Weighted monotone lifting is proved by a compact feasible quadratic minimizer and an improving perturbation. Adjacent transfer bounds imply full-report IC by telescoping. Selected results are finite equivalence, weighted monotone lifting and optimizer monotonicity; scalar IC and support-restriction facts remain in the library as supporting lemmas. Validation evidence is recorded separately for the exact candidate.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Uniqueness of four-body convex central configurations for all masses
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Theorems A and B of arXiv:2609.35632 on the central configurations of the planar Newtonian four-body problem. For every choice of four positive masses and every cyclic order of the bodies there is exactly one strictly convex central configuration with that cyclic order, up to similarity, so there are exactly three convex central configurations up to similarity. This answers Problem 10 in the list of Albouy, Cabral and Santos (2012). The main step of the paper is Theorem B: at every strictly convex central configuration of positive masses, the Hessian form Q of U + (λ/2)I is at least one quarter of its radial part K. It follows that every convex central configuration is a nondegenerate local minimum of U I^(1/2), whose Hessian vanishes exactly on the tangent space of the orbit of the similarities. The computer-assisted step, a branch and bound with interval arithmetic over the three-dimensional set of normalized convex central configurations in the coordinates of Corbera, Cors and Roberts, proves tr S < 3/4 and is checked by Lean's kernel with `decide +kernel` in 7307 certificate theorems. No compiled code is trusted, and the proofs use only Lean's three standard axioms.

records.title: Critical-window emergence of autocatalytic sets under reaction-channel quotienting
records.abstract: Hordijk and Steel (https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.03919, Section 7, Eq. (21)) conjectured a zero-one threshold for RAF emergence at linear mean catalysis. An interior limiting law is established for the reversible binary-polymer model with monomer/dimer food and reaction channels obtained by identifying the split descriptions u + v and v + u precisely when uv = vu. Each molecule independently catalyzes each channel, with one catalysis coordinate shared by both directions. For every real sequence f(n)/n → λ > 0, the clamped channel parameter eventually equals f(n)/|J_n|, and the probability of a reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated (RAF) set converges to a limit L(λ) depending only on λ. The function L is nondecreasing and satisfies 0 < L(λ) ≤ 1 − exp(−34λ) < 1 at every positive finite intensity. Thus a zero-one step threshold is excluded in this channel model.

records.title: NP-completeness of SAT, 3-SAT and their variants (the Cook–Levin theorem) in Lean 4
records.abstract:
A Lean 4 proof of the Cook–Levin theorem and of the NP-completeness of several variants of satisfiability, for an explicit machine model, using only Lean's core library. The compared theorems state that the following languages are NP-complete: SAT, the set of binary codes of satisfiable CNF formulas (Complexity.sat_np_complete); 3-SAT, with at most three literals per clause (threeSAT_np_complete); exactly-3-SAT, with exactly three literals per clause on three distinct variables (exactThreeSAT_np_complete); (≤1,≤2)-SAT, with two or three literals per clause and every variable occurring at most once positively and at most twice negatively (leOneLeTwoSAT_np_complete); SAT with variable indices written in binary (binarySAT_np_complete); planar 3-SAT, whose variable–clause incidence graph is planar (planarThreeSAT_np_complete); and Lichtenstein's planar 3-SAT, whose incidence graph stays planar with the cycle through the variables added (cyclePlanarThreeSAT_np_complete). Planarity is Gonthier's from the formal proof of the Four Color Theorem: a graph is planar when a hypermap on its half-edges embeds it with genus zero, the genus being computed from the Euler formula. NP-complete means: in NP, and every language in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one (Karp) reduction. A further compared theorem, inNP_iff_nondeterministicPolyTime, proves that NP, defined by verifiers, is the class of languages accepted in polynomial time by nondeterministic machines with two transition tables. Languages are sets of binary words. Computation is by deterministic Turing machines with a single two-way infinite tape over a four-symbol alphabet, and time is the number of machine steps. NP is defined by polynomial-time verifiers and polynomially bounded certificates, the standard certificate characterization; a reduction is a function computed by such a machine within a polynomial number of steps. Formulas are coded with unary variable indices and list lengths (binary indices for the binary variant); words that code no formula belong to none of the languages.
For an arbitrary NP verifier, the hardness proof builds a CNF formula describing the computation tableau of the verifier on the input and an unknown certificate; it is satisfiable exactly when some certificate makes the verifier accept. The reduction is itself implemented as a machine: it is written in a small language of loops over unary counters, compiled through finite programs on Boolean stacks to the single-tape model, and its running time is proved by counting the executed steps. SAT is reduced to 3-SAT by replacing each clause with a chain of clauses of at most three literals linked by fresh variables, and the reductions are composed as machines. Exactly-3-SAT and (≤1,≤2)-SAT are reached by transforming the Cook–Levin formula generator itself: every literal occurrence gets its own copy variable, a cycle of implications links the copies of each variable, long clauses are split by chains, and short clauses are padded. The binary variant is reached by a machine converting unary indices to binary. For planar 3-SAT, the Cook–Levin formula is turned into a grid formula in the style of Lichtenstein (one column of crossover gadgets per clause, copies of each variable joined by nested two-literal clauses), proved equisatisfiable and planar with its variable cycle through a general lemma on formulas drawn as combs; the plain version subdivides the cycle edges. Membership in NP is proved with explicit verifier machines for every language; for the planar versions the certificate also describes a planar embedding. For the nondeterministic characterization, a deterministic verifier simulates a nondeterministic machine with its choices read from the certificate, and conversely a nondeterministic machine guesses a certificate in a unary budget and runs the verifier. The development was written by AI under human direction: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI) produced the proof, and Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) ran its full verification, revised the statement for auditability and prepared it for Palomar, with the variants and the nondeterministic characterization proved by Claude agents. The proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Pascal Cofactors
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalisation of p-adic valuation laws for alternating cofactors C_d(p^a) = (p^(ad)+1)/(p^a+1) with odd d. It proves finite-window coefficient scaling and an exact pre-extremal restricted-binomial-gcd formula, identifies the sparse endpoint, proves the least extremal row T_p(C_d(p^a)) = p^(ad)+1 for odd d >= 5, and gives the full cubic classification for p^(2a)-p^a+1. The Palomar Challenge records coefficient scaling, the exact bounded gcd formula, the odd-degree least-row theorem, and the cubic classification.

records.title: Continuity of solutions to abstract linear control systems
records.abstract: Formalization of all the numbered statements of F. Marbach, "Continuity of solutions to abstract linear control systems" (2026), https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00022. For abstract linear control systems in the sense of Weiss (a strongly continuous semigroup T on a Banach space X and bounded input maps Phi_t : L^p(R_+; U) -> X satisfying the concatenation identity), the main results are: for p = infinity, every system is zero-class, i.e. the operator norm of Phi_t tends to zero as t -> 0+ (Theorem 1.5), and t -> Phi_t u is continuous on [0, infinity) for every u in L^infinity (Corollary 1.6), a positive answer to Weiss' 1989 Problem 2.4. No integral representation of the input maps is assumed. The proof packs nearly extremal controls into one bounded operator on l^infinity and uses Phillips' lemma (Lemma 2.2), which is proved here. The development also covers the continuity of semigroup orbits (Proposition 1.2), the classical case p < infinity (Proposition 1.3), and the examples of Section 3: a non zero-class system for p < infinity (Proposition 3.1), an exotic invariant mean on periodic L^infinity functions (Lemma 3.2), and a scalar system with p = infinity without integral representation and not E_F-admissible for any Young function F (Proposition 3.3).

records.title: Continuous binary implementation congruence and sharp finite welfare frontier
records.abstract: A general two-alternative implementation characterization on own-type domains containing an open ball: affine private and social valuation differences, nonzero social linear form, one active welfare cut, and a fixed independent opposing probability law force nonnegative coefficient alignment. Arbitrary measurable efficient lotteries have integrable Bayesian incentive compatible transfers exactly under alignment, with explicit ex-post truthful-opponent transfers and a measurable efficient allocation witness. Arbitrary distributions including atoms are covered. A genuine independent uniform-square auction model rules out efficiency even under only agent 0 incentive compatibility for every a,b>0. The separately proved finite sharp welfare/error frontier and original example corollary are retained. This does not formalize arbitrary-alternative Theorem 4.3 or genericity, and makes no novelty claim.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: The hitting time for loose Hamilton cycles in r-graphs
records.abstract: A Lean formalisation of a hitting time theorem of Wanfang Chen, Jared León and Xizhi Liu. For every fixed integer r ≥ 3, assume all r-element subsets of n vertices are exposed in a uniformly random order. As n tends to infinity through multiples of r − 1, with probability tending to one, a loose Hamilton cycle first emerges exactly when the last isolated vertex disappears.

records.title: Regularity of asymptotically axisymmetric Navier–Stokes solutions with analytic forcing
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of Constantin, Ignatova and Vicol on the regularity of asymptotically axisymmetric solutions of the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with analytic forcing (arXiv:2609.20803). A suitable weak solution on the unit parabolic cylinder, smooth before the blow-up time, whose force is bounded in C^2 up to the blow-up time and real analytic in space, whose angular mean satisfies anisotropic Type II bounds, and which is exactly axisymmetric on a ball around the axis at every time, is axisymmetric and regular at the putative singular point (Theorem 1.1); the axisymmetric theorem (Theorem 1.3), the meridional smallness proposition, the consequences for the force (Corollary 2.3) and the lemmas of Sections 3 and 5 are formalized with it. The interior analyticity theorem of Kahane, the interior estimates of Serrin and the regularity criterion of Gustafson, Kang and Tsai, in the forms the paper uses, are proved rather than assumed. The thirteen results use only the standard axioms and build on the Lean formalization of the Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg theorem; five of them are restated in a Mathlib-only comparator challenge and proved from the library theorems.

records.title: Optimal Information and Concavification in Bayesian Persuasion
records.abstract: Kamenica and Gentzkow's finite-state persuasion theorem from economic primitives: nonempty compact metric actions, continuous sender and receiver utilities, and a full-support common prior. Receiver best replies and sender-preferred tie actions exist. The induced sender payoff is bounded and upper semicontinuous. Finite signals realize exactly finite Bayes-plausible posterior splittings, with prescribed posteriors recovered only at nonnull messages. An optimal finite signal with at most the number of states plus two messages exists and dominates every finite experiment. Its value is the least concave majorant of the induced payoff on the entire belief simplex; strict persuasion gain is exactly the concavification gap. This covers the signal/splitting part of Proposition 1 and Corollary 2, including attainment. The straightforward recommendation branch and compact-state extension are outside this scope. Related finite splitting and abstract attainment are already formalized in Daniel Lyng's Econlib; no first-formalization or novelty claim is made.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák and Ladyzhenskaya–Prodi–Serrin regularity
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of two classical regularity theorems for the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations. The Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák theorem states that a Leray–Hopf solution whose spatial L³ norm remains bounded in time is smooth at positive times and unique among Leray–Hopf solutions with the same initial data. The Ladyzhenskaya–Prodi–Serrin theorem gives the corresponding conclusion under a family of mixed space-time integrability conditions. The development includes the local regularity theorem, L⁵ space-time integrability under the endpoint L³ condition, and the supporting Carleman inequalities, unique continuation and backward uniqueness. It builds on the Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg formalization and includes a manuscript presenting the proofs.

records.title: Milgrom–Shannon's Monotonicity Theorem: the Full Characterization
records.abstract: Milgrom and Shannon (1994), Theorem 4, in both directions: for an arbitrary lattice X, partially ordered parameter space T, and real-valued objective, strong-set monotonicity of constrained maximizers over every pair of strongly ordered feasible subsets is equivalent to quasisupermodularity of every section and both weak and strict preference-preservation clauses of single crossing. The theorem imposes no finiteness, completeness, topology, continuity, compactness, nonemptiness, or optimizer existence assumptions. Supporting results and counterexamples distinguish crossing clauses and fixed-domain from varying-feasible-set monotonicity. Earlier Lean sufficiency results in Econlib and nonmathlib4 are explicitly cited.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Falmagne–Block–Marschak Random-Utility Characterization
records.abstract: A full constructive formalization of the Falmagne–Block–Marschak theorem for any finite nonempty alternative set, without a cardinality bound. A normalized stochastic choice rule on all nonempty menus is generated by a single probability distribution over complete strict rankings if and only if all Block–Marschak alternating-sum coefficients are nonnegative. The proof derives Boolean-lattice flow conservation, constructs a finite ranking mixture by positive-path subtraction, and proves exact lower-contour probability identities by Möbius inversion. Compiled adversarial examples show that regularity alone is insufficient.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Distance-Shell Tomography: Geometric Certificates for Fault-Tolerant Sensing, Moment Compression, and Hypercube Equalization
records.abstract: Substantive Lean development for labelled distance-shell observations of anonymous integer populations. The focused 14-statement interface covers six result groups. Square grids have an exact four-corner interval-cut characterization of recovery of all populations of mass at most two after one erased report, an equivalent distance-sum compression contract, and exact corner-constrained optimum ceil(3(n+1)/2) for every n at least 3. For every positive q, the actual-distance equalizer cardinality of Q_(4q) lies between 2^(4q-1)+2q-1 and 2^(4q-1)+2q; explicit prefixes also give the infinite contradiction to the sourced exponential formula. Further selected results prove the long-rectangle optimum, ordinary 2-domination on every positive even bishop board, two exact Petersen double-total-domination values, and a connected real fractional-face counterexample. The complete library is included, not an external or assumption-based wrapper. Supporting algebra and geometric lemmas remain proved but unselected. The public README explains mathematical scope, antecedents, and limitations without treating known ingredients or all supporting lemmas as separate original results.

records.title: Monderer–Shapley Exact-Potential Characterization
records.abstract: The full cycle characterization for arbitrary finite player types and arbitrary nonempty player-dependent action spaces. A real-valued exact potential exists if and only if deviators' payoff differences sum to zero around every finite closed path, every finite simple closed path, every simple four-cycle, or every two-player rectangle. The construction uses finite-subset induction and imposes no finiteness restriction on actions. Exact potentials are unique up to an additive constant. With finite actions, the cycle condition yields a pure Nash equilibrium. Adversarial examples distinguish matching pennies, infinite actions, unequal dependent actions, and the finite-action boundary.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Lower bounds for the covering numbers C(24,14,4) and C(25,15,5)
records.abstract: A Lean proof that every family of 14-element subsets of a 24-element set covering all 4-element subsets has at least 20 members, so the covering number C(24,14,4) is at least 20, improving the previously tabulated lower bound of 19. Point derivation (the Schönheim bound) then gives C(25,15,5) >= 34, improving the tabulated 32. The proof excludes a hypothetical 19-block covering using degree and codegree counting, a Gram-matrix rank argument that forces balanced bipartite components, and a structural analysis of the two resulting cases.

records.title: Quantum Pauli basis test
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the quantum Pauli basis test from MIP*=RE. The comparator-configured results give a value-one symmetric projective consistent commuting strategy, quantum soundness of the simultaneous low-degree test, soundness of the Pauli basis test up to local isometries with the explicit deltaQld error, and the corresponding qubit-coordinate form.

records.title: Identifying the rooted species tree from unrooted gene trees under the coalescent
records.abstract:
A formalization of E. S. Allman, J. H. Degnan and J. A. Rhodes, "Identifying the rooted species tree from the distribution of unrooted gene trees under the coalescent", J. Math. Biol. 62 (2011) 833-862. The multispecies coalescent is defined from Kingman's coalescent on forests of gene lineages (its generator, the matrix exponential, and a recursion over the species tree).

Proved: the distribution of unrooted topological gene trees, with one lineage sampled per taxon, determines the rooted species tree and its internal branch lengths when there are at least five taxa (Theorem 9); on four taxa it determines exactly the unrooted metric species tree (Proposition 3); with several lineages per taxon it also determines the corresponding pendant branch lengths (Corollary 10); and all of this holds for nonbinary species trees (Proposition 11). Every other result of the paper is proved too, with the explicit gene tree distributions, linear invariants and inequalities for five taxa, and the cited results that the proofs use: Tavare's formula, the reconstruction of trees from quartets, and Cayley's count of tree shapes.

records.title: Gallai's conjecture with two exceptional even vertices
